# PlexUI: full reference
> The most flexible UI kit for React. Production-grade components with pixel-perfect Figma parity.

React components with every documented example. Quick overview: https://plexui.com/llms.txt
Vue 3: https://plexui.com/llms-vue.txt and https://plexui.com/llms-vue-full.txt

Install: npm install @plexui/ui
Docs: https://plexui.com
Components: 50

## Setup

```css
@layer theme, base, components, utilities;
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@plexui/ui/css";
@source "../node_modules/@plexui/ui";
```

Wrap your app with <PlexUIProvider linkComponent={Link}> from "@plexui/ui/components/PlexUIProvider" (your router's Link, or "a")

Size scale: 3xs, 2xs, xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl
Colors: primary, secondary, danger, success, warning, caution, discovery, info
Variants: solid, soft, outline, ghost

---

## Accordion
Vertically stacked panels that expand to reveal content, with one or several items open at a time and full keyboard navigation.
Import: import { Accordion } from "@plexui/ui/components/Accordion"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/accordion
Props:
  - type ("single" | "multiple") default: — — Required. Whether one item or many can be open at a time
  - value (string | string[]) default: — — Controlled open item(s)
  - defaultValue (string | string[]) default: — — Uncontrolled initial open item(s)
  - onValueChange ((value) => void) default: — — Fires when the open item(s) change
  - collapsible (boolean) default: false — When type="single", allow closing the open item
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable every item
  - dir ("ltr" | "rtl") default: "ltr" — Reading direction
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "vertical" — Layout axis
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root <div>
  Accordion.Item:
    - value (string) default: — — Required. Unique identifier used by value / defaultValue
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable this item
    - className (string) default: — — Applied to the item wrapper

### Overview
```tsx
<Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="shipping">
<Accordion.Item value="shipping">
  <Accordion.Trigger>What are your shipping options?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>
    We offer standard (5–7 business days), express (2–3 days), and overnight shipping…
  </Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
<Accordion.Item value="returns">
  <Accordion.Trigger>What is your return policy?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>Returns are accepted within 30 days of delivery…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
<Accordion.Item value="support">
  <Accordion.Trigger>How can I contact customer support?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>Reach us by email, live chat, or phone Monday–Friday…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
</Accordion>
```

### Single
Default shape. type="single" + collapsible lets users close the currently open item; without collapsible, one item is always open.
```tsx
<Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="trial">
{items.map((item) => (
  <Accordion.Item key={item.value} value={item.value}>
    <Accordion.Trigger>{item.trigger}</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>{item.content}</Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
))}
</Accordion>
```

### Multiple
Use type="multiple" when readers can keep several sections open at once: settings pages, long FAQs, step-by-step references.
```tsx
<Accordion type="multiple" defaultValue={["notifications"]}>
{items.map((item) => (
  <Accordion.Item key={item.value} value={item.value}>
    <Accordion.Trigger>{item.trigger}</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>{item.content}</Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
))}
</Accordion>
```

### Disabled
Pass disabled to an Accordion.Item to make it read-only. The row stays visible so the reader understands the section exists; keyboard focus skips it.
```tsx
<Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="history">
<Accordion.Item value="history">
  <Accordion.Trigger>Can I see my usage history?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
<Accordion.Item value="audit" disabled>
  <Accordion.Trigger>Audit log export (Enterprise only)</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
<Accordion.Item value="two-factor">
  <Accordion.Trigger>How do I enable two-factor auth?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
</Accordion>
```

### Card
Composed inside Card, the most common landing-page FAQ pattern.
```tsx
<Card>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>Subscription & billing</Card.Title>
  <Card.Description>Common questions about plans, invoices, and cancellations.</Card.Description>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Content>
  <Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="plans">
    {items.map((item) => (
      <Accordion.Item key={item.value} value={item.value}>
        <Accordion.Trigger>{item.trigger}</Accordion.Trigger>
        <Accordion.Content>{item.content}</Accordion.Content>
      </Accordion.Item>
    ))}
  </Accordion>
</Card.Content>
</Card>
```

## Alert
Inline message for notices and warnings with semantic colors, variants, a title, a description, action slots, and a dismiss control.
Import: import { Alert } from "@plexui/ui/components/Alert"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/alert
Props:
  - title (ReactNode) — Title displayed in the alert
  - description (ReactNode) — Description text
  - actions (ReactNode) — Actions (for example buttons)
  - actionsPlacement ("end" | "bottom") — Placement of actions; automatic from sizing when unset
  - actionsClassName (string) — Class applied to the actions container
  - color (SemanticColors) default: "primary" — Color scheme
  - variant ("solid" | "soft" | "outline") default: "outline" — Style variant
  - indicator (ReactNode | false) — Custom indicator or false to hide
  - onDismiss (() => void) — Shows the dismiss button when set
  - banner (boolean) default: false — Full-width strip: square corners, lines above and below only
  - className (string) — Class applied to the alert container

### Overview
```tsx
<Alert
title="Scheduled maintenance"
description="We'll be offline 2 - 4 AM UTC on July 14 while we upgrade our database."
actions={<Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Dismiss</Button>}
/>
```

### Colors & variants
You can stylize the display of the alert using the color and variant props.
```tsx
<Alert
color="primary"
variant="outline"
title="Scheduled maintenance on Saturday, 2-4 AM PT"
description={<>Track status updates on <TextLink color="currentcolor" href="#">status page</TextLink></>}
/>
```

### Title
You can optionally include a title for your alert with the title prop.
```tsx
<Alert title="Your current access level limits what you can view or modify" />
```

### Description
You can optionally include description text for your alert with the description prop.
```tsx
<Alert
description={
  <>
    We're working on centralizing SCIM and invite settings. For now, setup is handled within individual product settings. <TextLink href="#">Learn more</TextLink>
  </>
}
/>
```

### Actions
You can add actions to the alert with the actions prop, which accepts ReactNode. Combine with onDismiss to add a dismiss button.
```tsx
<>
<Alert
  variant="soft"
  color="warning"
  title="Password expires in 3 days"
  description="Update it now to avoid losing access to your account."
  actions={<Button color="primary" pill>Update password</Button>}
/>
<Alert
  variant="soft"
  color="warning"
  title="Your API key will be rotated soon"
  description="Automatic key rotation is scheduled for March 10. Download the new key afterward to keep your integrations running."
  actions={<Button color="warning" variant="soft" pill>Remind me later</Button>}
  onDismiss={() => {}}
/>
</>
```

### Action placement
Actions are automatically positioned in the alert by default. You can force a specific position with the actionsPlacement prop by passing either 'end' or 'bottom'.
```tsx
<Alert
title="Our terms of service has been updated"
description="We've updated our terms to clarify how we handle data, billing, and user permissions. Please review and accept the latest terms to avoid impacting your service."
actions={(
  <>
    <Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Set reminder</Button>
    <Button color="primary" variant="solid" pill>Review terms</Button>
  </>
)}
actionsPlacement="bottom"
/>
```

### Indicator
Alert provides an indicator icon by default. You can override it by passing a custom icon to indicator, or pass indicator={'{false}'} to hide it entirely.
```tsx
<>
<Alert
  indicator={<Lightbulb />}
  description={
    <>
      We're working on centralizing SCIM and invite settings. For now, setup is handled within individual product settings. <TextLink href="#">Learn more</TextLink>
    </>
  }
/>
<Alert
  indicator={false}
  description="Version 2.18.5 rolls out behind-the-scenes tweaks to caching and background sync. You don't need to do anything."
/>
</>
```

### Dismissible
The suggested approach for dismissible notices is to use labeled buttons via actions. You can also provide onDismiss to render a dismiss button in the alert chrome.
```tsx
<>
<Alert
  className="items-start"
  title="Try our new dashboard layout"
  description="We've introduced a streamlined layout that makes using the dashboard even easier. You can switch back any time."
  actions={(
    <>
      <Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Dismiss</Button>
      <Button color="primary" variant="solid" pill>Try it</Button>
    </>
  )}
/>
<Alert
  title="Thank you!"
  description="Your application has been received. We will review your application and respond within the next 48 hours."
  onDismiss={() => {}}
/>
</>
```

### Banner
Use banner for a full-width strip across the top or bottom of a page or panel: offline, read-only, a new version. It drops the rounded corners and keeps only the lines above and below. Pass indicator={'{false}'} for a plain strip.
```tsx
<Alert
banner
color="caution"
variant="soft"
indicator={false}
description="You are offline. Changes will sync when the connection is back."
/>
```

## Avatar Group
Stacks user avatars into a single overlapping cluster, with a configurable stacking direction and one size for the whole group.
Import: import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/Avatar"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/avatar-group
Props:
  - children (ReactNode) — The avatars of the group
  - size (number) — Size of all avatars in the group
  - stack ("start" | "end") default: "start" — Stacking direction
  - className (string) — Applied to the group container; other props are not forwarded

### Overview
```tsx
<AvatarGroup size={42}>
<Avatar name="Tyler" imageUrl="https://gravatar.com/avatar/9531b260b9693f3394bea8646c6ea141ce58fe5a138b7db7729d60a4c5dde552" />
<Avatar name="Jane" color="primary" variant="solid" />
<Avatar name="Tech support" Icon={Robot} variant="solid" />
<Avatar overflowCount={5} />
</AvatarGroup>
```

### Stacking direction
You can control the stacking direction using the stack prop, as either "start" or "end".
```tsx
<AvatarGroup stack="end" size={42}>
<Avatar name="Tyler" imageUrl="https://gravatar.com/avatar/9531b260b9693f3394bea8646c6ea141ce58fe5a138b7db7729d60a4c5dde552" />
<Avatar name="Will" />
<Avatar name="Tech support" Icon={Robot} variant="solid" />
<Avatar overflowCount={5} variant="soft" />
</AvatarGroup>
```

### Group sizing
You can control the size of all avatars in the group by passing size directly to the &lt;AvatarGroup&gt; component.
```tsx
<AvatarGroup size={48}>
<Avatar name="Tyler" color="info" />
<Avatar name="Jane" color="discovery" />
<Avatar name="Will" color="danger" />
<Avatar overflowCount={5} />
</AvatarGroup>
```

## Avatar
An avatar for user identities that shows an initial, a photo or an icon, with overflow counts, semantic colors and roundness options.
Import: import { Avatar } from "@plexui/ui/components/Avatar"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/avatar
Props:
  - name (string) — Display name; used for text initial when no image/icon
  - imageUrl (string) — Absolute URL for image avatar
  - Icon (React.ComponentType) — Icon component for icon avatar
  - size (number) — Width and height in pixels
  - color ("primary" | "secondary" | "success" | "info" | "discovery" | "danger") default: "secondary" — Semantic color for text/icon avatar
  - variant ("soft" | "solid") default: "soft" — Style variant
  - overflowCount (number) — Show overflow count (e.g. +9)
  - className (string) — Applied to the avatar root
  - onClick (() => void) — Makes avatar interactive (renders a button)
  - onPointerDown (() => void) — Makes avatar interactive (renders a button)

### Overview
A variety of avatar types: text, image, icon, and overflow.
```tsx
<div className="flex gap-4">
<Avatar name="Tyler" imageUrl="https://gravatar.com/avatar/9531b260b9693f3394bea8646c6ea141ce58fe5a138b7db7729d60a4c5dde552" size={48} />
<Avatar name="Will" size={48} />
<Avatar name="Tech support" Icon={Robot} size={48} color="primary" variant="solid" />
</div>
```

### Text
For text-based avatars, a single initial is displayed based on the name prop passed to the component.
```tsx
<Avatar name="David" size={48} />
```

### Image
To display an image avatar, provide an absolute URL to the image with imageUrl. Images will have a soft fade entrance once loaded, or fall back to a text display if the image fails to load.
```tsx
<Avatar
name="Tyler"
imageUrl="https://gravatar.com/avatar/9531b260b9693f3394bea8646c6ea141ce58fe5a138b7db7729d60a4c5dde552"
size={48}
/>
```

### Icon
To display an icon avatar, provide an icon to render to the Icon prop. The name prop is not used in this case, and can be omitted.
```tsx
<Avatar
Icon={Robot}
size={48}
/>
```

### Overflow count
To display an overflow avatar, provide a number to the overflowCount prop. The number will be automatically formatted and scaled to fit.
```tsx
<Avatar overflowCount={9} size={48} />
```

### Sizing
To size the avatar, pass a number to the size property, which will set the width and height in pixels. Text and icon avatars will scale their sizes dynamically based on this value.
```tsx
<Avatar name="David" size={48} />
```

### Colors & variants
You can stylize the display of the avatar using the color and variant props.
```tsx
<div
className="grid items-center gap-x-8 gap-y-5"
style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(2, minmax(0, auto)) auto", justifyItems: "center" }}
>
{(["soft", "solid"] as const).map((variant) => (
  <div key={variant} className="text-sm font-medium" style={{ color: "var(--color-text-tertiary)" }}>
    {variant}
  </div>
))}
<div />
{(["primary", "secondary", "success", "danger", "info", "discovery"] as const).map((color, idx) => (
  <Fragment key={color}>
    {(["soft", "solid"] as const).map((variant) => (
      <Avatar key={variant} name={String.fromCharCode(65 + idx)} color={color} variant={variant} size={48} />
    ))}
    <div className="text-sm font-medium justify-self-start" style={{ color: "var(--color-text-tertiary)" }}>
      {color}
    </div>
  </Fragment>
))}
</div>
```

### Roundness
By default, avatars are fully rounded. You can override this by passing a Tailwind rounding class to className.
```tsx
<Avatar name="Acme, co." color="primary" variant="solid" size={48} className="rounded-lg" />
```

### Interactive
Avatars can be used as interactive elements by passing an onClick (or onPointerDown) handler. The avatar then renders a button and applies semantic and visual interaction styles.
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
<Avatar name="Will" size={48} onClick={saySup} />
<Avatar
  imageUrl="https://gravatar.com/avatar/9531b260b9693f3394bea8646c6ea141ce58fe5a138b7db7729d60a4c5dde552"
  name="Tyler"
  size={48}
  onClick={saySup}
/>
<Avatar name="Tech support" Icon={Robot} size={48} color="info" onClick={saySup} />
</div>
```

## Badge
Compact label for statuses and inline metadata, with semantic colors, three variants and sizes, icon support, and a loading state.
Import: import { Badge } from "@plexui/ui/components/Badge"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/badge
Props:
  - children (ReactNode) — Content inside the badge
  - color ("secondary" | "success" | "danger" | "warning" | "info" | "discovery" | "caution") default: "secondary" — Semantic color
  - variant ("solid" | "soft" | "outline") default: "soft" — Style variant
  - size ("sm" | "md" | "lg") default: "sm" — Badge size
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded
  - className (string) — Class applied to the badge

### Overview
Status badges in different colors and compositions.
```tsx
<div className="flex gap-4 flex-wrap">
<Badge color="success" size="lg">Successful</Badge>
<Badge size="lg" className="gap-1.5"><LoadingIndicator /> In progress</Badge>
<Badge color="danger" size="lg">Failed</Badge>
<Badge color="warning" size="lg" pill><Flask /> Beta</Badge>
<Badge color="caution" size="lg">Caution</Badge>
</div>
```

### Colors & variants
You can stylize the display of the badge using the color and variant props.
```tsx
const variants = ["soft", "solid", "outline"] as const
const colors = ["secondary", "success", "warning", "danger", "info", "discovery", "caution"] as const

<div className="w-full overflow-x-auto">
<div className="pt-1 pb-6 px-8 w-fit min-w-full">
  <div className="grid gap-6 items-center justify-center" style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "auto repeat(7, min-content)" }}>
    <div />
    {colors.map((color) => (
      <div key={color} className="text-center mb-1 text-sm" style={{ color: "var(--color-text-tertiary)" }}>
        {color}
      </div>
    ))}
    {variants.map((variant) => (
      <Fragment key={variant}>
        <div className="text-right mr-3 text-sm" style={{ color: "var(--color-text-tertiary)" }}>
          {variant}
        </div>
        {colors.map((color) => (
          <div key={color} className="text-center">
            <Badge color={color} variant={variant}>Sample</Badge>
          </div>
        ))}
      </Fragment>
    ))}
  </div>
</div>
</div>
```

### Size & roundness
You can control the size and roundness of the badge with size and pill props. When pill is set, extra horizontal gutter is dynamically applied to the badge.
```tsx
<Badge color="info" size="md">New</Badge>
```

### Icon
Content within the badge can be composed, like showing icons. Color, sizing, and spacing adapt by default.
```tsx
<Badge color="warning" size="lg"><Flask /> Beta</Badge>
```

### Loading
In this example, additional gap is added with a Tailwind gap-1.5 class to provide the appropriate visual spacing.
```tsx
<Badge size="lg" color="secondary" className="gap-1.5">
<LoadingIndicator /> In progress
</Badge>
```

## Breadcrumb
The trail of pages that leads to the current one, above a page title, with links, plain steps and the current page.
Import: import { Breadcrumb } from "@plexui/ui/components/Breadcrumb"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/breadcrumb
Props:
  - size ("sm" | "md") default: "md" — Text size: sm above a compact header, md above a page title
  - separator (ReactNode) default: a small chevron — What stands between two items
  - aria-label (string) default: "Breadcrumb" — Name of the navigation landmark
  - className (string) — Applied to the nav element
  Breadcrumb.Item:
    - href (string) — Link destination. Internal paths use the linkComponent of PlexUIProvider
    - to (string) — Router destination, for link components that take to
    - current (boolean) default: false — The current page: plain text marked aria-current="page"
    - onClick ((event: MouseEvent) => void) — Makes an item without a destination act as a button
    - className (string) — Applied to the li element

### Overview
Breadcrumb renders a nav landmark named "Breadcrumb" around an ordered list. An item with href is a link (internal paths use the linkComponent of PlexUIProvider, such as your router's link); the current item is plain text marked aria-current="page".
```tsx
<Breadcrumb>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/">Home</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/settings">Settings</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>Members</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
```

### Sizes
Use size="sm" for a trail above a compact header; the default md sits above a page title.
```tsx
<Breadcrumb size="sm">
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/projects">Projects</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/projects/website">Website</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>Deployments</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
```

### Separator
A small chevron stands between items by default. Pass any node to separator, such as a slash for file paths. Separators are hidden from assistive technology.
```tsx
<Breadcrumb separator="/">
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/acme">acme</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/acme/design-system">design-system</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>README.md</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
```

### Long trails
A trail that does not fit wraps onto the next line instead of leaving the screen. An item without href is a plain step; give it onClick to make it act as a button.
```tsx
<Breadcrumb>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/">Workspace</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/accounts">Customer accounts</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/accounts/northwind">Northwind Traders</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item>Archived</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>Invoice 2024-0193</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Button Group
Join buttons into a single visual unit for toolbars, steppers, split buttons and search affordances.
Import: import { ButtonGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/ButtonGroup"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/button-group
Props:
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Direction of the joined items
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root <div>
  ButtonGroup.Text:
    - asChild (boolean) default: false — Render as the passed child (e.g. a <label> tied to an input)
    - className (string) default: — — Applied to the wrapper

### Overview
```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Go back">
    <ArrowLeftSm />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm">Pin</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm">Tag</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm">Bookmark</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="More options">
    <DotsHorizontal />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Orientation
Pass orientation="vertical" to stack the buttons, useful for + / − steppers, zoom controls, or any vertical toolbar.
```tsx
<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Zoom controls">
<Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Zoom in">
  <PlusSm />
</Button>
<Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Zoom out">
  <Minus />
</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Size
Set size on every Button inside the group so corner radii match. Mix icon-only (uniform) with text buttons; each child keeps its own padding.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-6">
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm">Small</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm">Button</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm">Group</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Add"><PlusSm /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary">Default</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary">Button</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary">Group</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" uniform aria-label="Add"><PlusSm /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="lg">Large</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="lg">Button</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="lg">Group</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="lg" uniform aria-label="Add"><PlusSm /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
</div>
```

### Nested
Place ButtonGroup inside ButtonGroup to create visually separated sub-groups. The outer group automatically adds a small gap between children; pagination with arrow navigation is the canonical pattern.
```tsx
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Pager">
<ButtonGroup>
  {[1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((page) => (
    <Button key={page} variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm">{page}</Button>
  ))}
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Previous page">
    <ArrowLeftSm />
  </Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Next page">
    <ArrowRightSm />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Separator
Drop a ButtonGroup.Separator between items to add a visible divider, commonly used for Undo / Redo pairs or any "two related actions" toolbar.
```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary" size="sm"><Undo /> Undo</Button>
<ButtonGroup.Separator />
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary" size="sm">Redo <Redo /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Split
The classic split button: an action joined to a secondary affordance via ButtonGroup.Separator. Useful for Save / Save-As, Filter / Add-filter, Delete / Undo.
```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary" size="sm"><Filter /> Filter</Button>
<ButtonGroup.Separator />
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Add filter">
  <Plus />
</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Input
Join an Input to a trailing Button for inline search, token entry, or URL shorteners. The input flexes to fill the row; the button hugs its content.
```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
<Input placeholder="Search docs..." size="sm" />
<Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" aria-label="Search">
  <SearchSm />
</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Input group
Richer composition for message composers: wrap each slot (leading action, flexible Input) in its own ButtonGroup so the outer group inserts a gap between them. The voice toggle rides inside the input via endAdornment. Use Input.AdornmentButton: it sizes off the input's own size token so the button stays concentric with the pill at every size.
```tsx
<ButtonGroup style={{ width: "100%", maxWidth: 280 }}>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" pill size="sm" uniform aria-label="Add attachment">
    <Plus />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Input
    pill
    size="sm"
    placeholder={voiceEnabled ? "Recording your idea…" : "Describe a component…"}
    disabled={voiceEnabled}
    endAdornment={
      <Input.AdornmentButton
        color={voiceEnabled ? "caution" : undefined}
        aria-label="Toggle voice mode"
        aria-pressed={voiceEnabled}
        onClick={() => setVoiceEnabled((prev) => !prev)}
      >
        <Mic />
      </Input.AdornmentButton>
    }
  />
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Dropdown menu
Compose a primary action with a Menu trigger for follow-up options. Common for Export / Format, Save / Save-As, Share / ….
```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
<Button variant="outline" color="secondary" pill={false} size="sm">Export</Button>
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" pill={false} size="sm" uniform aria-label="More export options">
      <ChevronDownMd />
    </Button>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Content align="end" minWidth={200}>
    <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><FileImage /> PNG image</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><FileCode /> SVG vector</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><FileDocument /> PDF document</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Separator />
    <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Copy /> Copy as code</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Link /> Copy share link</Menu.Item>
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Select
Mix a Select and an Input inside one ButtonGroup for unit pickers, currency entry, or any "qualifier + value" pattern. Wrap each slot in a nested ButtonGroup to get a gap between the compound field and the send affordance.
```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Select
    options={units}
    value={unit}
    onChange={(option) => setUnit(option.value)}
    variant="outline"
    size="sm"
    block={false}
  />
  <Input placeholder="2.50" size="sm" inputMode="decimal" />
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" size="sm" uniform aria-label="Log weight">
    <ArrowRight />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Popover
Same split-button shape, but the trailing trigger opens a Popover instead of a menu, useful for richer panels (prompt composers, notification preferences, link previews).
```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
<Button variant="outline" color="secondary" pill={false} size="sm"><Sparkles /> Generate</Button>
<Popover>
  <Popover.Trigger>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" pill={false} size="sm" uniform aria-label="More generate options">
      <ChevronDownMd />
    </Button>
  </Popover.Trigger>
  <Popover.Content minWidth={320} side="bottom" align="end" className="p-4">
    <Card variant="ghost" size="sm">
      <Card.Header>
        <Card.Title>Generate a component</Card.Title>
        <Card.Description>Describe what to build in plain English.</Card.Description>
      </Card.Header>
      <Card.Content>
        <Textarea placeholder="A login form with email and password…" rows={3} />
      </Card.Content>
      <Card.Footer>
        <Card.Description>Plex will draft the code and preview it live.</Card.Description>
      </Card.Footer>
    </Card>
  </Popover.Content>
</Popover>
</ButtonGroup>
```

## Button Link
A semantic anchor with full button styling, for internal and external links with icons and block layout.
Import: import { ButtonLink } from "@plexui/ui/components/Button"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/button-link
Props:
  - children (ReactNode) — Content inside the link button
  - color ("primary" | "secondary" | "danger" | "success" | "info" | "discovery" | "caution" | "warning") default: "primary" — Visual color
  - variant ("solid" | "soft" | "outline" | "ghost") default: "solid" — Style variant
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Control height and typography scale
  - gutterSize ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl") — Override horizontal padding
  - iconSize ("sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl") — Override icon size
  - href (string) — Link URL
  - to (string | object) — Router link destination (internal)
  - as (ComponentType) — Link component override (e.g. Next Link)
  - external (boolean) — Force external-link behavior
  - opticallyAlign ("start" | "end") — Apply optical negative margin alignment
  - block (boolean) default: false — Full width
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable link
  - disabledTone ("relaxed") — Use relaxed visual tone for disabled state
  - className (string) — Custom classes for the root element
  - onClick ((event: MouseEvent) => void) — Called on click, unless disabled

### Overview
```tsx
<ButtonLink color="primary" pill={false} href="#">View API Keys <ArrowRight /></ButtonLink>
```

### Internal link
When a relative href or to is provided, ButtonLink automatically uses the configured LinkComponent from PlexUIProvider so your router handles navigation and prefetching.
```tsx
<ButtonLink href="/components/button" color="primary">
Internal link <ArrowRight />
</ButtonLink>
```

### External link
When linking to an external URL (or when external is set), &lt;a&gt; is used with target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer" added automatically. If your link is not being automatically identified, you can force external link behavior with the external prop.
```tsx
<ButtonLink href="#" color="primary">
External link <ArrowUpRight />
</ButtonLink>
```

### Colors & variants
Stylize the link with color and variant props.
```tsx
const colors = ["primary", "secondary", "danger", "info", "discovery", "success", "caution", "warning"] as const
const variants = ["soft", "solid", "outline", "ghost"] as const

<div className="w-[calc(100%+48px)] -mx-6 overflow-x-auto [scrollbar-width:none] [&::-webkit-scrollbar]:hidden">
<div className="pt-1 pb-6 px-8 w-fit min-w-full">
  <div className="grid gap-6 items-center justify-center" style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "auto repeat(8, min-content)" }}>
    <div />
    {colors.map((color) => (
      <div key={color} className="text-center text-sm mb-1 text-tertiary">{color}</div>
    ))}
    {variants.map((variant) => (
      <Fragment key={variant}>
        <div className="text-right text-sm mr-3 text-tertiary">{variant}</div>
        {colors.map((color) => (
          <div key={color} className="text-center">
            <ButtonLink href="#" size="lg" color={color} variant={variant} className="whitespace-nowrap">
              Button
            </ButtonLink>
          </div>
        ))}
      </Fragment>
    ))}
  </div>
</div>
</div>
```

### Sizing & roundness
Sizing of the link is controlled with size and gutterSize props. size sets the control height, and gutterSize sets the horizontal padding. Create fully rounded links with the pill prop. When pill is set, extra horizontal gutter is dynamically applied to the link.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 justify-start items-start">
<ButtonLink color="primary" size="lg" href="#" className="whitespace-nowrap">
  View account <ArrowRight />
</ButtonLink>
<ButtonLink color="primary" size="lg" href="#" className="whitespace-nowrap">
  View account
</ButtonLink>
</div>
```

### Icons
Icon sizing is controlled by the iconSize prop, which makes it easy to add icons as children without additional props. size will provide a default value for iconSize, but setting the prop will force the specified size.
```tsx
<ButtonLink color="info" size="lg" iconSize="lg" variant="soft" href="#" className="whitespace-nowrap">
<Globe /> View website
</ButtonLink>
```

### Block
Create full-width links with the block prop.
```tsx
<div className="w-[290px] text-center p-2 border border-dashed border-alpha/20 rounded-md">
<ButtonLink block size="lg" href="#" className="whitespace-nowrap">Continue to dashboard</ButtonLink>
</div>
```

### Disabled
Use disabled to both visually and accessibly disable a link. The component renders as a span[role="link"], and onClick handlers are not bound.
```tsx
<ButtonLink href="#" color="primary" disabled className="whitespace-nowrap">
<Key /> View API Keys
</ButtonLink>
```

## Button
Button with four variants (solid, soft, outline, ghost), eight semantic colors, icon slots, loading, and block layout.
Import: import { Button } from "@plexui/ui/components/Button"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/button
Props:
  - color ("primary" | "secondary" | "danger" | "success" | "info" | "discovery" | "caution" | "warning") default: "primary" — Visual color scheme
  - variant ("solid" | "soft" | "outline" | "ghost") default: "solid" — Button style variant
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Control height and default gutter/icon size
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded corners
  - block (boolean) default: false — Full width
  - uniform (boolean) default: false — Square icon button (width equals height)
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Visually and accessibly disabled; onClick is not called
  - disabledTone ("relaxed") — Default cursor instead of not-allowed while disabled
  - loading (boolean) default: false — Shows loading indicator
  - inert (boolean) default: loading — Accessibly disabled without visual change
  - selected (boolean) default: false — Selected state styling
  - opticallyAlign ("start" | "end") — Offset gutter for optical alignment
  - gutterSize ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl") — Horizontal padding size; defaults from size
  - iconSize ("sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl") — Size of icons in children; defaults from size
  - type ("button" | "submit" | "reset") default: "button" — Native button type
  - onClick ((event: MouseEvent) => void) — Called on click, unless disabled

### Overview
A showcase of Button's key styles: solid, soft, outline, ghost, and icon-only.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
<Button color="primary">Submit</Button>
<Button variant="soft"><CompareArrows /> Compare</Button>
<Button color="danger" gutterSize="sm" pill={false} aria-label="Delete"><Delete /></Button>
<Button variant="outline">Next <ArrowRight /></Button>
<Button variant="ghost" color="secondary" uniform aria-label="Clear"><Clear /></Button>
</div>
```

### Colors & variants
You can stylize the display of the button using the color and variant props.
```tsx
const colors = ["primary", "secondary", "danger", "info", "discovery", "success", "caution", "warning"] as const
const variants = ["soft", "solid", "outline", "ghost"] as const

<div className="w-[calc(100%+48px)] -mx-6 overflow-x-auto [scrollbar-width:none] [-ms-overflow-style:none] [&::-webkit-scrollbar]:hidden">
<div className="pt-1 pb-6 px-8 w-max mx-auto">
  <div className="grid gap-6 items-center justify-center" style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "auto repeat(8, min-content)" }}>
    <div />
    {colors.map((color) => (
      <div key={color} className="text-center text-sm mb-1" style={{ color: "var(--color-text-tertiary)" }}>
        {color}
      </div>
    ))}
    {variants.map((variant) => (
      <Fragment key={variant}>
        <div className="text-right text-sm mr-3" style={{ color: "var(--color-text-tertiary)" }}>
          {variant}
        </div>
        {colors.map((color) => (
          <div key={color} className="text-center">
            <Button color={color} variant={variant} size="md">Submit</Button>
          </div>
        ))}
      </Fragment>
    ))}
  </div>
</div>
</div>
```

### Sizing & roundness
Control height with size and horizontal padding with gutterSize. Use pill for fully rounded corners. size sets the button to a specific control height, and gutterSize sets the horizontal padding. Each size provides default values for gutterSize and iconSize props, as well as font-size. Each of these values can be overridden independently. When pill is set, extra horizontal gutter is dynamically applied to the button.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 items-center">
<Button color="primary" size="xl" pill><Mail /> Button <ArrowRight /></Button>
<Button color="primary" size="xl" pill>Button <ArrowRight /></Button>
<Button color="primary" size="xl" pill><Mail /> Button</Button>
<Button color="primary" size="xl" pill>Button</Button>
</div>
```

### Icons
Add icons as children. Sizing is automatic via the iconSize prop. Default values for iconSize are provided through the size prop, but you can pass the prop directly to change the defaults. For icon-only buttons, there are two common approaches: Square: create perfect square icon buttons with the uniform prop. When uniform is passed, gutterSize is ignored. Combine with pill to make circular icons. Tighter gutters: applying a smaller gutterSize than size can create well-sized, but not exactly square, icon buttons.
```tsx
<Button color="primary" size="lg" aria-label="Add">
<PlusLg />
</Button>
```

### Block
Create full-width buttons with the block prop.
```tsx
<div className="w-[290px] mx-auto text-center p-2 border border-dashed border-alpha/20 rounded-md">
<Button color="primary" size="lg" block>Continue</Button>
</div>
```

### Disabled
Use disabled to both visually and accessibly disable a button. Clicks do not call onClick.
```tsx
<Button color="primary" disabled>Submit</Button>
```

### Inert
Use inert to accessibly disable a button without any visual changes. Note: For accessibility reasons, disabled is used instead of applying inert directly to the button. Visual disablement in the disabled prop is applied via [data-disabled].
```tsx
<Button color="primary" inert>Submit</Button>
```

### Loading
Use loading to display a loading indicator in the button, fading out the current content. Interactions are prevented during this state, because inert defaults to loading. Override it with inert, or use disabled to add visual disablement.
```tsx
<Button loading size="xl" pill><ArrowUp /> Click to load</Button>
```

### Selected
Use selected to show that a button is in an open or selected state. The exact visual behavior differs across each variant. This behavior is automatically configured with components like Menu that apply [aria-expanded="true"] or [data-state="open"] attributes.
```tsx
<Popover>
<Popover.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" selected variant="solid">Click to open</Button>
</Popover.Trigger>
<Popover.Content minWidth="auto" className="p-4 text-sm">
  Button should look selected
</Popover.Content>
</Popover>
```

### Optical alignment
Use opticallyAlign with either "start" or "end" to offset the gutter of the button.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
<div className="border border-dashed border-alpha/20 rounded-md py-4 px-6">
  <div className="mb-2 text-secondary text-sm">Default gutters</div>
  <Button variant="ghost">Ghost button</Button>
</div>
<div className="border border-dashed border-alpha/20 rounded-md py-4 px-6">
  <div className="mb-2 text-secondary text-sm">opticallyAlign="start"</div>
  <Button variant="ghost" opticallyAlign="start">Ghost button</Button>
</div>
</div>
```

## Card
Card surface for composing login flows, sign-up forms, pricing tiles, payment methods, empty states, and stat showcases.
Import: import { Card } from "@plexui/ui/components/Card"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/card
Props:
  - variant ("outline" | "solid" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Visual variant
  - size ("sm" | "md" | "lg") default: "md" — Padding scale
  - interactive (boolean) default: false — Adds hover and focus affordances. Automatic when href is set.
  - href (string) default: — — Renders the Card as a link via the configured LinkComponent.
  - external (boolean) default: auto-detected — Forces target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer" when href is set.
  - as (ComponentType | "a") default: — — Overrides the link component (e.g. next/link).
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root element

### Overview
```tsx
<Card style={{ maxWidth: 380 }}>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>Project activity</Card.Title>
  <Card.Description>
    Your team opened 12 issues and closed 8 pull requests over the last 7 days.
  </Card.Description>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Footer>
  <Button color="primary" variant="solid" size="sm">View report</Button>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="outline" size="sm">Dismiss</Button>
</Card.Footer>
</Card>
```

### Login
A classic login form with a primary Log in CTA and an inline Sign up link below.
```tsx
<Card style={{ maxWidth: 380 }}>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>Log in to your account</Card.Title>
  <Card.Description>Enter your email below to log in to your account.</Card.Description>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Content>
  <div style={{ display: "flex", flexDirection: "column", gap: 20 }}>
    <Field label="Email">
      <Input type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
    </Field>
    <div style={{ display: "flex", flexDirection: "column", gap: 6 }}>
      <div style={{ display: "flex", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "space-between", gap: 8 }}>
        <Label htmlFor="card-login-password">Password</Label>
        <TextLink href="#" primary>Forgot your password?</TextLink>
      </div>
      <Input id="card-login-password" type="password" />
    </div>
  </div>
</Card.Content>
<Card.Footer style={{ flexDirection: "column", alignItems: "stretch", gap: 12 }}>
  <Button color="primary" variant="solid" block>Log in</Button>
  {/* Description sits flush under a title by default; here it follows a button */}
  <Card.Description className="text-center" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
    Don't have an account? <TextLink href="#" primary>Sign up</TextLink>
  </Card.Description>
</Card.Footer>
</Card>
```

### Create project
Right-aligned footer with Cancel / Deploy. Use {'style={{ justifyContent: "flex-end" }}'} on Card.Footer.
```tsx
<Card style={{ maxWidth: 380 }}>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>Create project</Card.Title>
  <Card.Description>Deploy a new project in one-click with sensible defaults.</Card.Description>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Content>
  <div style={{ display: "flex", flexDirection: "column", gap: 20 }}>
    <Field label="Name">
      <Input placeholder="billing-service" />
    </Field>
    <Field label="Region" description="Where your functions and database will live.">
      <Input placeholder="us-east-1" />
    </Field>
  </div>
</Card.Content>
<Card.Footer style={{ justifyContent: "flex-end" }}>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="outline" size="sm">Cancel</Button>
  <Button color="primary" variant="solid" size="sm">Deploy</Button>
</Card.Footer>
</Card>
```

### Payment Method
Full-fidelity payment form. Month, Year and CVV share one row, with a Select for the month and the year. A Separator sets off the Billing Address section, whose Checkbox takes its text through label.
```tsx
const monthOptions = Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, i) => {
const value = String(i + 1).padStart(2, "0")
return { label: value, value }
})
const yearOptions = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, i) => {
const value = String(2024 + i)
return { label: value, value }
})

const [month, setMonth] = useState("")
const [year, setYear] = useState("")
const [sameAsShipping, setSameAsShipping] = useState(true)

<Card style={{ maxWidth: 420 }}>
<div style={{ display: "flex", flexDirection: "column", gap: 16 }}>
  <Card.Header>
    <Card.Title>Payment Method</Card.Title>
    <Card.Description>All transactions are secure and encrypted</Card.Description>
  </Card.Header>

  <Field label="Name on Card">
    <Input placeholder="Aisha Cooper" />
  </Field>

  <Field label="Card Number" description="Enter your 16-digit card number">
    <Input placeholder="1234 5678 9012 3456" inputMode="numeric" />
  </Field>

  <div style={{ display: "grid", gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr 1fr", gap: 16 }}>
    <Field label="Month">
      <Select value={month} options={monthOptions} placeholder="MM" onChange={(option) => setMonth(option.value)} />
    </Field>
    <Field label="Year">
      <Select value={year} options={yearOptions} placeholder="YYYY" onChange={(option) => setYear(option.value)} />
    </Field>
    <Field label="CVV">
      <Input placeholder="123" inputMode="numeric" />
    </Field>
  </div>

  <Separator />

  <Card.Header>
    <Card.Title>Billing Address</Card.Title>
    <Card.Description>The billing address associated with your payment method</Card.Description>
  </Card.Header>

  <Checkbox checked={sameAsShipping} onCheckedChange={setSameAsShipping} label="Same as shipping address" />

  <Separator />

  <Field label="Comments">
    <Textarea placeholder="Add any additional comments" rows={3} />
  </Field>

  <div style={{ display: "flex", gap: 8 }}>
    <Button color="primary" variant="solid">Submit</Button>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
  </div>
</div>
</Card>
```

### No team members (empty state)
Compose Card with EmptyMessage for a center-aligned empty state with icon badge, title, description, and primary action.
```tsx
<Card style={{ maxWidth: 380, padding: 24 }}>
<EmptyMessage>
  <EmptyMessage.Icon>
    <UserAdd />
  </EmptyMessage.Icon>
  <EmptyMessage.Title>No team members</EmptyMessage.Title>
  <EmptyMessage.Description>Invite your team to collaborate on this project.</EmptyMessage.Description>
  <EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
    <Button color="primary" variant="solid" size="sm">Invite members</Button>
  </EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
</EmptyMessage>
</Card>
```

### How did you hear about us?
A single-question survey using RadioGroup with direction="col" and a full-width submit button.
```tsx
const [source, setSource] = useState("social")

<Card style={{ maxWidth: 380 }}>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>How did you hear about us?</Card.Title>
  <Card.Description>Select the option that best describes how you heard about us.</Card.Description>
</Card.Header>
```
