```tsx
  <RadioGroup value={source} onChange={setSource} direction="col">
    <RadioGroup.Item value="social" block>Social Media</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="search" block>Search Engine</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="referral" block>Referral</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="other" block>Other</RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
</Card.Content>
<Card.Footer>
  <Button color="primary" variant="solid" block>Submit</Button>
</Card.Footer>
</Card>
```

### Processing your request
Loading state built with EmptyMessage and a LoadingIndicator as the visual anchor.
```tsx
<Card style={{ maxWidth: 380, padding: 24 }}>
<EmptyMessage>
  <div style={{ marginBottom: 12, color: "var(--color-text-tertiary)" }}>
    <LoadingIndicator size={28} />
  </div>
  <EmptyMessage.Title>Processing your request</EmptyMessage.Title>
  <EmptyMessage.Description>
    Please wait while we process your request. Do not refresh the page.
  </EmptyMessage.Description>
  <EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="outline" size="sm">Cancel</Button>
  </EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
</EmptyMessage>
</Card>
```

### Pricing
Mix variant="outline" and variant="solid" to emphasize a highlighted plan.
```tsx
const plans = [
{ name: "Starter", price: "$0", highlighted: false, features: ["1 project", "Community support", "Plex UI core"] },
{ name: "Pro", price: "$19", highlighted: true, features: ["Unlimited projects", "Priority support", "All Figma kits", "Early components"] },
]

<div style={{ display: "grid", gap: 16, gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(auto-fit, minmax(240px, 1fr))", maxWidth: 720 }}>
{plans.map((plan) => (
  <Card key={plan.name} variant={plan.highlighted ? "solid" : "outline"}>
    <Card.Header>
      <Card.Title>{plan.name}</Card.Title>
      <Card.Description>
        <span style={{ fontSize: 28, fontWeight: 600, color: "var(--color-text)" }}>{plan.price}</span>
        <span style={{ marginLeft: 4 }}>/ month</span>
      </Card.Description>
    </Card.Header>
    <Card.Content>
      <ul style={{ listStyle: "none", padding: 0, margin: 0, display: "flex", flexDirection: "column", gap: 8 }}>
        {plan.features.map((feature) => (
          <li key={feature} style={{ display: "flex", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
            <Check style={{ width: 16, height: 16, color: "var(--color-text-success-soft)" }} />
            {feature}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </Card.Content>
    <Card.Footer style={{ marginTop: "auto", paddingTop: 4 }}>
      <Button
        color={plan.highlighted ? "primary" : "secondary"}
        variant={plan.highlighted ? "solid" : "outline"}
        block
      >
        Choose {plan.name}
      </Button>
    </Card.Footer>
  </Card>
))}
</div>
```

## Checkbox
Checkbox for binary on/off selection with solid, pill, and ghost variants, an indeterminate state, and rich labels with inline descriptions.
Import: import { Checkbox } from "@plexui/ui/components/Checkbox"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/checkbox
Props:
  - variant ("solid" | "ghost") default: "solid" — Visual style: solid (filled background) or ghost (checkmark only)
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded indicator corners
  - checked (boolean | "indeterminate") — Controlled state
  - defaultChecked (boolean | "indeterminate") — Initial state (uncontrolled)
  - onCheckedChange ((next: boolean) => void) — Called with the next state when it changes
  - label (ReactNode) — Accessible label. Accepts ReactNode for rich content
  - description (ReactNode) — Second line below the label, linked via aria-describedby. Renders only with a label
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Prevent interaction
  - required (boolean) — Required for form submission
  - name (string) — Form field name
  - value (string) default: "on" — Value when submitted
  - orientation ("left" | "right") default: "left" — Checkbox position relative to the label
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to the wrapper node
  - id (string) — The id of the checkbox element (generated when omitted)
  - onFocus ((event: FocusEvent) => void) — Called when the checkbox gains focus
  - onBlur ((event: FocusEvent) => void) — Called when the checkbox loses focus

### Overview
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
<Checkbox label="Same as billing address" />
<Checkbox label="Subscribe to newsletter" defaultChecked />
</div>
```

### With Radio Group
Place Checkbox alongside RadioGroup controls to verify that indicator sizes, label baselines, and spacing align consistently in both horizontal and vertical layouts.
```tsx
const channels = [
{ value: "email", label: "Email", description: "Messages delivered to your inbox." },
{ value: "sms", label: "SMS", description: "Text messages to your phone number." },
{ value: "push", label: "Push", description: "Real-time alerts on your device." },
]
const topics = [
{ label: "Product updates", description: "New features and improvements.", checked: true },
{ label: "Security alerts", description: "Account activity and login notifications.", checked: true },
{ label: "Community", description: "Events, meetups, and discussions.", checked: false },
]

<div className="flex flex-col gap-6 w-full max-w-md">
<Field label="Notification channel" description="Choose how you'd like to be notified.">
  {() => (
    <RadioGroup direction="col" defaultValue="email" aria-label="Notification channel">
      {channels.map((channel) => (
        <RadioGroup.Item key={channel.value} value={channel.value}>
          <div className="flex flex-col">
            <span className="font-medium">{channel.label}</span>
            <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">{channel.description}</span>
          </div>
        </RadioGroup.Item>
      ))}
    </RadioGroup>
  )}
</Field>
<Field label="Topics" description="Select the topics you want to follow.">
  {() => (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5">
      {topics.map((topic) => (
        <Checkbox
          key={topic.label}
          defaultChecked={topic.checked}
          label={
            <div className="flex flex-col">
              <span className="font-medium">{topic.label}</span>
              <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">{topic.description}</span>
            </div>
          }
        />
      ))}
    </div>
  )}
</Field>
</div>
```

### Descriptions
Combine Field-level label and description with item-level descriptions for options that need additional context. Use a plain label without descriptions when the options are self-explanatory.
```tsx
const [settings, setSettings] = useState({
marketing: true,
security: true,
everything: false,
mentions: true,
nothing: false,
})
const toggle = (key: keyof typeof settings) => () =>
setSettings((prev) => ({ ...prev, [key]: !prev[key] }))

<div className="flex flex-col max-w-sm w-full divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Email notifications" description="Configure which emails you receive.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5">
        <Checkbox
          label={
            <div className="flex flex-col">
              <span className="font-medium">Marketing</span>
              <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Receive emails about new products and features.</span>
            </div>
          }
          checked={settings.marketing}
          onCheckedChange={toggle("marketing")}
        />
        <Checkbox
          label={
            <div className="flex flex-col">
              <span className="font-medium">Security</span>
              <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Receive emails about account activity and security.</span>
            </div>
          }
          checked={settings.security}
          onCheckedChange={toggle("security")}
        />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="Push notifications">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <Checkbox label="Everything" checked={settings.everything} onCheckedChange={toggle("everything")} />
        <Checkbox label="Direct messages and mentions" checked={settings.mentions} onCheckedChange={toggle("mentions")} />
        <Checkbox label="Nothing" checked={settings.nothing} onCheckedChange={toggle("nothing")} />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

### Variants
The checkbox supports three visual styles: solid (default) with a filled background and standard radius, solid pill with fully rounded corners, and ghost, which renders only the checkmark without a border or background fill.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-x-12 gap-y-6">
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 items-start">
  <span className="text-xs text-secondary font-mono mb-1">solid</span>
  <Checkbox label="Unchecked" />
  <Checkbox label="Checked" defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox label="Indeterminate" checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 items-start">
  <span className="text-xs text-secondary font-mono mb-1">solid pill</span>
  <Checkbox label="Unchecked" pill />
  <Checkbox label="Checked" pill defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox label="Indeterminate" pill checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 items-start">
  <span className="text-xs text-secondary font-mono mb-1">ghost</span>
  <Checkbox label="Unchecked" variant="ghost" />
  <Checkbox label="Checked" variant="ghost" defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox label="Indeterminate" variant="ghost" checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Pill
Set pill to render the checkbox indicator with fully rounded corners (border-radius: full) instead of the default square radius.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
<Checkbox label="Unchecked" pill />
<Checkbox label="Checked" pill defaultChecked />
<Checkbox label="Indeterminate" pill checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
```

### Ghost
Use variant="ghost" to render the checkbox without a border or background. The checkmark uses the text color instead of white, making it suitable for subtle inline selections or task lists.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
<Checkbox label="Unchecked" variant="ghost" />
<Checkbox label="Checked" variant="ghost" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox label="Indeterminate" variant="ghost" checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
```

### With description
Use description for a second line under the label. It sits outside the label, so the checkbox keeps the label as its name and gets the description through aria-describedby. The description renders only next to a label.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4 max-w-sm">
<Checkbox
  label="Accept terms and conditions"
  description="By checking this box, you agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy."
  defaultChecked
/>
<Checkbox
  label="Enable notifications"
  description="You can enable or disable notifications at any time from settings."
/>
</div>
```

### Indeterminate
Use checked="indeterminate" to indicate a partially selected state. This is typically used for "select all" controls where only some child items are checked. Here checked starts as "indeterminate" and each click moves it to the next state.
```tsx
const [checked, setChecked] = useState<boolean | "indeterminate">("indeterminate");

<Checkbox
checked={checked}
onCheckedChange={() =>
  setChecked(c => c === "indeterminate" ? true : c ? false : "indeterminate")
}
label="Select all"
/>
```

### Disabled
When disabled is set, the checkbox is dimmed to 50% opacity and prevents interaction. It works the same across all variants: solid, pill, and ghost.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-x-12 gap-y-6">
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 items-start">
  <span className="text-xs text-secondary font-mono mb-1">solid</span>
  <Checkbox label="Unchecked" disabled />
  <Checkbox label="Checked" disabled defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox label="Indeterminate" disabled checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 items-start">
  <span className="text-xs text-secondary font-mono mb-1">solid pill</span>
  <Checkbox label="Unchecked" pill disabled />
  <Checkbox label="Checked" pill disabled defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox label="Indeterminate" pill disabled checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 items-start">
  <span className="text-xs text-secondary font-mono mb-1">ghost</span>
  <Checkbox label="Unchecked" variant="ghost" disabled />
  <Checkbox label="Checked" variant="ghost" disabled defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox label="Indeterminate" variant="ghost" disabled checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Label orientation
By default the checkbox renders to the left of the label. Set orientation="right" to place the checkbox after the label.
```tsx
<Checkbox label="Accept terms and conditions" orientation="right" />
```

### Without label
When no label is provided, the checkbox renders as a standalone control, so pass aria-label to give it an accessible name. All three visual states are shown: unchecked, checked, and indeterminate.
```tsx
<div className="flex gap-4">
<Checkbox aria-label="Accept terms" />
<Checkbox aria-label="Subscribe" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox aria-label="Select all" checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
```

### Group with select all
Combine a parent checkbox with child checkboxes to create a "select all" pattern. The parent shows an indeterminate state when only some children are checked. Each child is controlled by its item in items.
```tsx
const [items, setItems] = useState([
{ id: "read", label: "Read", checked: true },
{ id: "write", label: "Write", checked: false },
{ id: "execute", label: "Execute", checked: false },
])

const allChecked = items.every((i) => i.checked)
const noneChecked = items.every((i) => !i.checked)
const parentChecked = allChecked ? true : noneChecked ? false : "indeterminate"

<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
<Checkbox
  label="Permissions"
  checked={parentChecked}
  onCheckedChange={() => {
    const next = !allChecked
    setItems((prev) => prev.map((i) => ({ ...i, checked: next })))
  }}
/>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 pl-6">
  {items.map((item) => (
    <Checkbox
      key={item.id}
      label={item.label}
      checked={item.checked}
      onCheckedChange={(next) => {
        setItems((prev) => prev.map((i) => (i.id === item.id ? { ...i, checked: Boolean(next) } : i)))
      }}
    />
  ))}
</div>
</div>
```

### Group with description
Wrap a group of checkboxes in a Field for a shared label and description. This is a common pattern for preference lists and settings panels.
```tsx
<Field label="Show on desktop" description="Select the items you want to display on the desktop.">
{() => (
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
    <Checkbox label="Hard disks" defaultChecked />
    <Checkbox label="External disks" />
    <Checkbox label="CDs, DVDs, and iPods" />
    <Checkbox label="Connected servers" />
  </div>
)}
</Field>
```

### With Field
Wrap checkboxes in a Field component for form layout with label, description, and error message support. A single control passed as the child gets aria-describedby and aria-invalid automatically; the render-prop form receives them as arguments, so spread them onto the control that should carry them.
```tsx
const [agreed, setAgreed] = useState(false)

<Field
label="Terms"
description="Please review and accept the terms before continuing."
errorMessage={showError ? "You must accept the terms to continue." : undefined}
>
{() => (
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 mt-1">
    <Checkbox
      label="I agree to the Terms of Service"
      checked={agreed}
      onCheckedChange={(next) => setAgreed(Boolean(next))}
    />
    <Checkbox label="Subscribe to product updates" />
  </div>
)}
</Field>
```

### Grouped sections
Use dividers to separate checkbox groups into logical sections. Each section can be wrapped in a Field with its own label and description.
```tsx
const [settings, setSettings] = useState({
emailMarketing: true,
emailSecurity: true,
pushEverything: false,
pushMentions: true,
pushNothing: false,
})
const toggle = (key: keyof typeof settings) => () =>
setSettings((prev) => ({ ...prev, [key]: !prev[key] }))

<div className="flex flex-col max-w-sm w-full divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Email notifications" description="Configure which emails you receive.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
        <Checkbox
          label={
            <div className="flex flex-col">
              <span className="font-medium">Marketing</span>
              <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Receive emails about new products and features.</span>
            </div>
          }
          checked={settings.emailMarketing}
          onCheckedChange={toggle("emailMarketing")}
        />
        <Checkbox
          label={
            <div className="flex flex-col">
              <span className="font-medium">Security</span>
              <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Receive emails about account activity and security.</span>
            </div>
          }
          checked={settings.emailSecurity}
          onCheckedChange={toggle("emailSecurity")}
        />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="Push notifications" description="Configure which push notifications you receive.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <Checkbox label="Everything" checked={settings.pushEverything} onCheckedChange={toggle("pushEverything")} />
        <Checkbox label="Direct messages and mentions" checked={settings.pushMentions} onCheckedChange={toggle("pushMentions")} />
        <Checkbox label="Nothing" checked={settings.pushNothing} onCheckedChange={toggle("pushNothing")} />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

## Code Block
Code block with syntax highlighting, a copy button, and collapsible long snippets with configurable expanded height limits.
Import: import { CodeBlock } from "@plexui/ui/components/CodeBlock"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/code-block
Props:
  - children (string) — Code content
  - language (string) — Prism language name
  - className (string) — Additional wrapper class
  CollapsibleCodeBlock:
    - children (string) — Code content
    - language (string) — Prism language name
    - defaultExpanded (boolean) default: false — Start expanded
    - collapsedHeight (number) default: 140 — Height when collapsed (px)
    - maxExpandedHeight (number) — Max height when expanded (px); taller code scrolls
    - copyable (boolean) default: true — Show copy button
    - className (string) — Additional wrapper class

### Overview
```tsx
<CodeBlock language="javascript">{codeSnippet}</CodeBlock>
```

### Collapsible
Use CollapsibleCodeBlock to display code in a compact view with gradient overlay and an expand action.
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="tsx">{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Expanded by default
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="tsx" defaultExpanded>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Custom collapsed height
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="typescript" collapsedHeight={60}>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Max expanded height
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="typescript" defaultExpanded maxExpandedHeight={200}>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Without copy button
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="python" defaultExpanded copyable={false}>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Supported languages
A pragmatic set of Prism grammars are pre-registered out of the box.
```tsx
<CodeBlock language="javascript">{code}</CodeBlock>
```

## Copy Tooltip
A copy-to-clipboard tooltip that wraps any trigger element and confirms when the value has been copied.
Import: import { CopyTooltip, Tooltip } from "@plexui/ui/components/Tooltip"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/copy-tooltip
Props:
  - children (ReactNode) — Trigger element (for example Tooltip.TriggerDecorator)
  - copyValue (string) — Required. Content to copy to clipboard
  - openDelay (number) default: 150 — Tooltip open delay in milliseconds
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Preferred tooltip alignment against the trigger
  - alignOffset (number) default: 0 — Offset from start/end alignment in pixels
  - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "top" — Preferred side of the trigger
  - sideOffset (number) default: 5 — Distance from trigger in pixels
  - onCopy ((copied: boolean) => void) — Called once the clipboard write settles, with whether it succeeded. The tooltip says Copied! only after a successful write

### Overview
```tsx
<CopyTooltip copyValue="Very cool content to copy">
<Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>sess_12345abcdefg</Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>
</CopyTooltip>
```

## Date Input
Masked text input for typing dates and times, with automatic formatting, min and max limits, and validation.
Import: import { DateInput } from "@plexui/ui/components/DateInput"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/date-input
Props:
  - value (DateTime | null) — Required. Selected date (Luxon DateTime)
  - onChange ((date: DateTime | null) => void) — Required. Called when a complete valid date is entered or the field is cleared
  - mode (MaskitoDateMode) default: "dd/mm/yyyy" — Date format mode: dd/mm/yyyy, mm/dd/yyyy, yyyy/mm/dd, etc.
  - separator (string) default: "." — Character between date parts
  - timeMode (MaskitoTimeMode) — Enable time input: HH:MM, HH:MM:SS, etc.
  - dateTimeSeparator (string) default: ", " — Separator between date and time parts
  - timeStep (number) default: 0 — Arrow-key increment step for time segments
  - min (DateTime) — Earliest allowed date
  - max (DateTime) — Latest allowed date
  - clearable (boolean) default: false — Show clear button when input has a value
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Input size (3xs to 3xl)
  - variant ("outline" | "soft") default: "outline" — Visual style
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded corners
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable input
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Mark as invalid
  - placeholder (string) — Generated from the format if not set

### Overview
Pass a Luxon DateTime (or null) as value with onChange. onChange fires once a complete, valid date is typed, and with null when the field is emptied or cleared. Leaving the field with a partly typed date shows the value again.
```tsx
const [date, setDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(null)

<div className="w-[200px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} size="md" variant="outline" clearable />
</div>
```

### With time
Pass timeMode="HH:MM" to enable date + time input in one field.
```tsx
<div className="w-[260px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} timeMode="HH:MM" clearable />
</div>
```

### With seconds
Use timeMode="HH:MM:SS" for second-level precision.
```tsx
<div className="w-[300px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} timeMode="HH:MM:SS" clearable />
</div>
```

### Limits
Use min and max to restrict the date range. The mask prevents entering values outside the allowed range. today is DateTime.local().
```tsx
const today = DateTime.local()
const [date, setDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(today)

<div className="w-[200px]">
<DateInput
  value={date}
  onChange={setDate}
  min={today.minus({ days: 30 }).startOf("day")}
  max={today.plus({ days: 30 }).endOf("day")}
  clearable
/>
</div>
```

### US format
Set mode="mm/dd/yyyy" and separator="/" for US-style date formatting.
```tsx
<div className="w-[200px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} mode="mm/dd/yyyy" separator="/" clearable />
</div>
```

### ISO format
Set mode="yyyy/mm/dd" and separator="-" for ISO 8601 formatting.
```tsx
<div className="w-[200px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} mode="yyyy/mm/dd" separator="-" clearable />
</div>
```

### With Field
Wrap with Field to add a label, description, and automatic accessibility attributes.
```tsx
<div className="w-[200px]">
<Field label="Date of birth" description="Enter your date of birth">
  <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} clearable />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Validation
Pass errorMessage to Field to display a validation error.
```tsx
<div className="w-[200px]">
<Field label="Date of birth" errorMessage={!date ? "Date is required" : undefined}>
  <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} clearable />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Disabled
```tsx
const [date, setDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(DateTime.local(2025, 1, 1))

<div className="w-[200px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} disabled />
</div>
```

## Date Picker
Date picker with an interactive calendar, time picker, year and month dropdowns, min/max limits, and date-of-birth presets.
Import: import { DatePicker } from "@plexui/ui/components/DatePicker"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/date-picker
Props:
  - value (DateTime | null) — Required. Selected date (luxon)
  - onChange ((date: DateTime | null) => void) — Required. Called when the date changes
  - id (string) — Id of the trigger, for forms and labels
  - min (DateTime) — Earliest selectable date (inclusive)
  - max (DateTime) — Latest selectable date (inclusive). Must not be before min
  - captionLayout ("buttons" | "dropdown") default: "buttons" — Calendar header mode. Use dropdown for date of birth
  - showTime (boolean) default: false — Show time input below calendar
  - yearRange ([number, number]) default: last 120 years — Min/max years for dropdown caption
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Trigger size (3xs to 3xl)
  - variant ("outline" | "soft" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Trigger style
  - pill (boolean) default: true — Rounded trigger
  - block (boolean) default: false — Full-width trigger
  - clearable (boolean) default: false — Show clear button
  - triggerShowIcon (boolean) default: true — Show calendar icon
  - triggerDateFormat (string) default: "MM/dd/yy" — Date format in trigger. Auto-includes time when showTime is enabled
  - triggerClassName (string) — Class applied to the trigger
  - dropdownIconType ("dropdown" | "chevronDown" | "none") default: "dropdown" — Icon at the end of the trigger
  - placeholder (string) default: "Select date..." — Trigger placeholder
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable picker
  - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "bottom" — Preferred side of the calendar popover
  - sideOffset (number) default: 8 — Distance from the trigger in pixels
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Alignment against the trigger
  - alignOffset (number) default: 0 (center), -5 (start, end) — Offset from start/end alignment in pixels

### Overview
Pass the date (a luxon DateTime, or null) as value and update it in onChange.
```tsx
const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(null)

<DatePicker
id="date-picker-base"
triggerDateFormat="MM/dd/yy"
size="lg"
pill
clearable
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
/>
```

### Limits
Use min and max to limit selectable dates to a specific timeframe. Equal bounds leave one selectable day.
```tsx
const today = DateTime.local()
const minDate = today.minus({ days: 30 }).startOf("day")
const maxDate = today.plus({ days: 30 }).endOf("day")
const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(today)

<DatePicker
id="date-picker-limits"
triggerDateFormat="MM/dd/yy"
size="lg"
pill
triggerShowIcon
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
min={minDate}
max={maxDate}
/>
```

### Date of birth
Set captionLayout="dropdown" to add month and year dropdowns inline with the arrow navigation. Ideal for selecting a date of birth where navigating month-by-month would be impractical.
```tsx
<DatePicker
id="date-picker-dob"
triggerDateFormat="MMMM d, yyyy"
size="lg"
pill
clearable
placeholder="Select your birthday"
captionLayout="dropdown"
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
max={DateTime.local()}
/>
```

### Time picker
Enable showTime to add hour and minute inputs below the calendar. The popover stays open after selecting a date so the user can adjust the time. Use arrow keys to increment or decrement values.
```tsx
<DatePicker
id="date-picker-time"
triggerDateFormat="MM/dd/yy HH:mm"
size="lg"
pill
clearable
placeholder="Select date & time"
showTime
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
/>
```

### Dropdown + time
Combine captionLayout="dropdown" with showTime for quick month/year jumps and time selection in a single picker, useful for scheduling events at a specific date and time.
```tsx
<DatePicker
id="date-picker-datetime-dropdown"
triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy HH:mm"
size="lg"
pill
clearable
placeholder="Schedule event"
captionLayout="dropdown"
showTime
yearRange={[2020, 2030]}
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
/>
```

### Two fields
Compose DatePicker and Input side by side for maximum flexibility in form layouts. Each field operates independently while sharing the same DateTime value. Here handleTimeInput masks the typed time as HH:MM and moves the date to a complete typed time, and a newly picked date takes the typed time.
```tsx
const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(null)
const [time, setTime] = useState("10:30")

// Mask the typed time as HH:MM; a complete time moves the picked date's time
const handleTimeInput = (event: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
const raw = event.target.value.replace(/[^\d:]/g, "")
const digits = raw.replace(/:/g, "")
let formatted = digits
if (digits.length >= 3) {
  formatted = digits.slice(0, 2) + ":" + digits.slice(2, 4)
} else if (digits.length === 2 && !raw.includes(":")) {
  formatted = digits + ":"
}
setTime(formatted.slice(0, 5))

const parts = formatted.split(":")
if (parts.length === 2 && parts[1].length === 2 && selectedDate) {
  const hour = Math.min(23, Number(parts[0]) || 0)
  const minute = Math.min(59, Number(parts[1]) || 0)
  setSelectedDate(selectedDate.set({ hour, minute }))
}
}

<div style={{ display: "flex", gap: "8px", alignItems: "center" }}>
<DatePicker
  id="date-picker-two-field-date"
  triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy"
  size="lg"
  pill
  captionLayout="dropdown"
  triggerShowIcon={false}
  dropdownIconType="none"
  placeholder="Select date"
  value={selectedDate}
  onChange={(next) => {
    // A picked date takes the typed time
    if (next && time) {
      const [hour, minute] = time.split(":").map(Number)
      setSelectedDate(next.set({ hour: hour || 0, minute: minute || 0 }))
    } else {
      setSelectedDate(next)
    }
  }}
/>
<Input
  id="date-picker-two-field-time"
  size="lg"
  pill
  value={time}
  onChange={handleTimeInput}
  placeholder="HH:MM"
  maxLength={5}
  style={{ width: "72px" }}
/>
</div>
```

### Date input
For typing a date directly instead of picking it, use DateInput, a masked input that auto-formats as you type.
```tsx
<div className="w-[200px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} mode="mm/dd/yyyy" separator="/" aria-label="Date" />
</div>
```

### DateTime input
Pass timeMode="HH:MM" to DateInput to type the date and time in one field.
```tsx
<div className="w-[260px]">
<DateInput
  value={dateTime}
  onChange={setDateTime}
  mode="mm/dd/yyyy"
  separator="/"
  timeMode="HH:MM"
  aria-label="Date and time"
/>
</div>
```

### Without Icon
Remove the calendar icon from the trigger by setting triggerShowIcon to false.
```tsx
<DatePicker
id="date-picker-no-icon"
triggerDateFormat="MM/dd/yy"
size="lg"
triggerShowIcon={false}
placeholder="Choose a date"
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
/>
```

### Disabled
Disable the picker to prevent user interaction.
```tsx
const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(DateTime.local())

<DatePicker
id="date-picker-disabled"
triggerDateFormat="MM/dd/yy"
size="lg"
disabled
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
/>
```

## Date Range Picker
Date range picker with an interactive calendar, min/max limits, preset shortcuts, and a month stepper for selecting start and end dates.
Import: import { DateRangePicker } from "@plexui/ui/components/DateRangePicker"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/date-range-picker
Props:
  - value (DateRange | null) — Required. Selected range ([start, end], inclusive)
  - onChange ((next: DateRange | null, shortcut?: DateRangeShortcut) => void) — Required. Called when the range changes
  - min (DateTime) — Earliest selectable date (inclusive)
  - max (DateTime) — Latest selectable date (inclusive). Must not be before min
  - maxRangeDays (number) — Max length of range in days (inclusive)
  - shortcuts (DateRangeShortcut[]) — Quick selection shortcuts ({ label, getDateRange })
  - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "bottom" — Preferred side for popover
  - sideOffset (number) default: 8 — Distance from trigger in pixels
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Preferred popover alignment
  - alignOffset (number) default: 0 (center), -5 (start, end) — Offset from start/end alignment in pixels
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable picker interactions
  - placeholder (string) default: "Select date range..." — Placeholder in trigger when value is empty
  - variant ("soft" | "outline" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Trigger style variant
  - pill (boolean) default: true — Rounded trigger shape
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Trigger size scale
  - dropdownIconType ("chevronDown" | "dropdown" | "none") default: "dropdown" — Icon shown at trigger end
  - triggerClassName (string) — Custom class for trigger
  - triggerShowIcon (boolean) default: true — Show calendar icon at trigger start
  - triggerStepperUnit ("month") — Enable month stepper mode in trigger
  - triggerDateFormat (string) default: "MM/dd/yy" — Date formatting in trigger text
  - clearable (boolean) default: false — Show clear button in trigger
  - block (boolean) default: false — Stretch trigger to full available width

### Overview
Pass the range ([start, end] luxon DateTimes, or null) as value and update it in onChange. When a shortcut was picked, onChange receives that shortcut as its second argument.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState<DateRange | null>(null)

<div style={{ width: "fit-content" }}>
<DateRangePicker
  size="lg"
  pill
  clearable
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
  shortcuts={dayShortcuts}
/>
</div>
```

### Limits
Use min and max to limit the selectable range. Use maxRangeDays to limit the range length. Here minDate is 30 days ago (start of day) and maxDate is the end of today.
```tsx
const today = DateTime.local()
const minDate = today.minus({ days: 30 }).startOf("day")
const maxDate = today.endOf("day")
const [value, setValue] = useState<DateRange | null>([
DateTime.max(minDate, today.startOf("month")),
DateTime.min(maxDate, today.endOf("month")),
])

<div style={{ width: "fit-content" }}>
<DateRangePicker
  size="lg"
  pill
  triggerShowIcon
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
  min={minDate}
  max={maxDate}
/>
</div>
```

### Shortcuts
Use the shortcuts array to provide quick date range options. When a shortcut is selected, its label is shown in the trigger. Each shortcut has a label and a getDateRange() function. A shortcut whose range falls outside min and max, or is longer than maxRangeDays, is disabled.
```tsx
const dayShortcuts: DateRangeShortcut[] = [
{
  label: "Today",
  getDateRange: () => {
    const today = DateTime.local()
    return [today.startOf("day"), today.endOf("day")]
  },
},
{
  label: "Yesterday",
  getDateRange: () => {
    const yesterday = DateTime.local().minus({ days: 1 })
    return [yesterday.startOf("day"), yesterday.endOf("day")]
  },
},
{
  label: "Last 7 days",
  getDateRange: () => {
    const today = DateTime.local().endOf("day")
    return [today.minus({ days: 6 }).startOf("day"), today]
  },
},
{
  label: "Last 30 days",
  getDateRange: () => {
    const today = DateTime.local().endOf("day")
    return [today.minus({ days: 29 }).startOf("day"), today]
  },
},
]
const [value, setValue] = useState<DateRange | null>(null)

<div style={{ width: "fit-content" }}>
<DateRangePicker
  size="lg"
  pill
  clearable
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
  shortcuts={dayShortcuts}
/>
</div>
```

### Month stepper
Enable a stepper in the trigger with triggerStepperUnit="month". When the selected range matches the unit, the trigger shows the stepper.
```tsx
const today = DateTime.local()
const maxDate = today.endOf("day")
const [value, setValue] = useState<DateRange | null>([today.startOf("month"), today])

<div style={{ width: "fit-content" }}>
<DateRangePicker
  size="lg"
  clearable
  pill
  triggerStepperUnit="month"
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
  max={maxDate}
/>
</div>
```

## Dialog
Modal dialog for confirmations, forms, and destructive alerts, with a focus trap, escape handling, and an overlay scrim.
Import: import { Dialog } from "@plexui/ui/components/Dialog"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/dialog
Props:
  - open (boolean) — Controlled open state; uncontrolled when omitted
  - onOpenChange ((open: boolean) => void) — Called when the dialog opens or closes
  Dialog.Content:
    - width (number | string) default: 480 — Panel width
    - showClose (boolean) default: true — Show close button in top-right corner
    - className (string) — Additional CSS class on the panel
    - placement ("center" | "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end" | "fullscreen") default: "center" — Where the panel sits: centered, near the top, a bottom sheet, a side panel, or the whole screen
    - mobilePlacement ("center" | "bottom" | "fullscreen") — Placement at 640px and below; defaults to placement
    - onOpenAutoFocus ((event: Event) => void) — Called when focus moves into the dialog on open; call event.preventDefault() to place it yourself, for example on the panel instead of the first field
    - onCloseAutoFocus ((event: Event) => void) — Called when focus returns on close; call event.preventDefault() to keep it elsewhere

### Overview
```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)

<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
<Dialog.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="outline">Open dialog</Button>
</Dialog.Trigger>
<Dialog.Content>
  <Dialog.Header>
    <Dialog.Title>Unsaved changes</Dialog.Title>
  </Dialog.Header>
  <p className="text-sm text-secondary">You have unsaved changes that will be lost if you close this page. Do you want to save before leaving?</p>
  <Dialog.Footer>
    <Dialog.Close>
      <Button color="primary" variant="soft">Cancel</Button>
    </Dialog.Close>
    <Button color="primary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Save changes</Button>
  </Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

### Destructive confirmation
Use color="danger" on the action button for destructive operations.
```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)

<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
<Dialog.Trigger>
  <Button color="danger" variant="outline">Delete</Button>
</Dialog.Trigger>
<Dialog.Content>
  <Dialog.Header>
    <Dialog.Title>Delete assistant?</Dialog.Title>
  </Dialog.Header>
  <p className="text-sm text-secondary">
    This change will affect all API integrations using{" "}
    <span className="font-medium text-[var(--color-text)]">asst_NAM5K9a7loKZay9W8gtQVQ3H</span>.
    It cannot be undone.
  </p>
  <Dialog.Footer>
    <Dialog.Close>
      <Button color="secondary" variant="soft">Cancel</Button>
    </Dialog.Close>
    <Button color="danger" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Delete</Button>
  </Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

### Scrolling body
Put long content in Dialog.Body: only the body scrolls, while the header and footer stay in view. Without it the whole panel scrolls.
```tsx
<Dialog.Content>
<Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Title>Terms of service</Dialog.Title>
  <Dialog.Description>Please read them before you continue.</Dialog.Description>
</Dialog.Header>
<Dialog.Body>
  {terms.map((term) => <p key={term}>{term}</p>)}
</Dialog.Body>
<Dialog.Footer>
  <Dialog.Close><Button color="secondary" variant="soft">Decline</Button></Dialog.Close>
  <Button color="primary">Accept</Button>
</Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
```

### Placement
Use placement to move the panel: top for search and command lists, bottom for a sheet along the bottom edge, start and end for a full-height side panel, fullscreen for the whole screen. mobilePlacement applies at 640px and below, so a centered dialog can become a bottom sheet on phones: {''}.
```tsx
<Dialog.Content placement="end" width={360}>
<Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Title>Filters</Dialog.Title>
</Dialog.Header>
<Dialog.Body>{/* fields */}</Dialog.Body>
<Dialog.Footer>
  <Dialog.Close><Button color="secondary" variant="soft">Clear filters</Button></Dialog.Close>
  <Button color="primary">Done</Button>
</Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
```

## Empty Message
Empty state for telling users there's nothing to show, with error, warning, no-results, and onboarding compositions.
Import: import { EmptyMessage } from "@plexui/ui/components/EmptyMessage"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/empty-message
Props:
  - fill ("static" | "absolute" | "none") default: "static" — How the container fills its parent: "static" takes full width and height, "absolute" covers a positioned parent (inset 0), "none" applies no sizing
  - size ("sm" | "md") default: "md" — sm is the compact message for a panel, a card section or an empty list
  - align ("center" | "start") default: "center" — start left-aligns the message, for an empty state under a section heading
  EmptyMessage.Icon:
    - color ("secondary" | "danger" | "warning") default: "secondary" — Semantic color
    - size ("sm" | "md") default: "md" — Icon badge size
  EmptyMessage.Title:
    - color ("secondary" | "danger" | "warning") default: "secondary" — Semantic color
  EmptyMessage.ActionRow:
    - className (string) — Additional classes for the action row container

### Composition
```tsx
<EmptyMessage>
<EmptyMessage.Icon>
  <Explore />
</EmptyMessage.Icon>
<EmptyMessage.Title>No projects yet</EmptyMessage.Title>
<EmptyMessage.Description>Create your first project to get started</EmptyMessage.Description>
<EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg">
    <Plus className="mr-[-2px]" />
    New project
  </Button>
</EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
</EmptyMessage>
```

### Error message
The color property enables you to display clearer intent with the message, such as showing an error state.
```tsx
<EmptyMessage>
<EmptyMessage.Icon color="danger">
  <Mic />
</EmptyMessage.Icon>
<EmptyMessage.Title color="danger">
  Enable microphone access in your browser's settings.
</EmptyMessage.Title>
</EmptyMessage>
```

### Warning message
```tsx
<EmptyMessage>
<EmptyMessage.Icon color="warning">
  <Sparkle />
</EmptyMessage.Icon>
<EmptyMessage.Title>o1-preview is in beta</EmptyMessage.Title>
<EmptyMessage.Description>
  System instructions and model configuration are not available yet. Responses may take
  longer.
</EmptyMessage.Description>
<EmptyMessage.ActionRow className="text-sm">
  <TextLink href="/">
    Learn more
    <ArrowUpRight />
  </TextLink>
</EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
</EmptyMessage>
```

### No results
The components of EmptyMessage are both composable and optional. This example omits the EmptyMessage.Title component, using only an icon and description for a simpler message style.
```tsx
<div className="w-full">
<EmptyMessage fill="none">
  <EmptyMessage.Icon size="sm">
    <Search />
  </EmptyMessage.Icon>
  <EmptyMessage.Description>
    No icons found matching <span className="font-semibold">"pizza"</span>
  </EmptyMessage.Description>
</EmptyMessage>
</div>
```

### Compact
Use size="sm" for an empty panel, card section or list: a smaller title, tighter spacing and no minimum width. Pair it with fill="none" when the container sets the height.
```tsx
<Card>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>Members</Card.Title>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Content>
  <EmptyMessage size="sm" fill="none">
    <EmptyMessage.Icon size="sm"><Group /></EmptyMessage.Icon>
    <EmptyMessage.Title>No members yet</EmptyMessage.Title>
    <EmptyMessage.Description>Invite people to work on this project.</EmptyMessage.Description>
    <EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
      <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" size="sm">Invite</Button>
    </EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
  </EmptyMessage>
</Card.Content>
</Card>
```

### Left aligned
Use align="start" for an empty state that sits under a section heading instead of filling a surface: a single line such as "No tags added" reads with the heading above it.
```tsx
<Card>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>Tags</Card.Title>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Content>
  <EmptyMessage size="sm" align="start" fill="none">
    <EmptyMessage.Description>No tags added.</EmptyMessage.Description>
  </EmptyMessage>
</Card.Content>
</Card>
```

## Field
Form field wrapper with a label, helper text, an error message, and automatic accessibility linking to its control.
Import: import { Field } from "@plexui/ui/components/Field"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/field
Props:
  - label (ReactNode) — Label text for the field
  - description (ReactNode) — Helper text below the label; linked via aria-describedby
  - errorMessage (ReactNode) — Error message below the control; auto-sets aria-invalid on child
  - labelAction (ReactNode) — Content at the end of the label row, such as a link that acts on the field
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: child's size, else "md" — Label font size; defaults to the child control's size
  - required (boolean) default: false — Shows a required asterisk after the label (visual only)
  - orientation ("vertical" | "horizontal") default: "vertical" — Layout direction of label and control
  - opticallyAlign ("start" | "end") — Applies optical alignment to the child control via negative margin using its gutter
  - id (string) — Override the auto-generated id used for htmlFor/aria linking
  - children (ReactElement | (fieldProps) => ReactNode) — Form control; receives id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid, plus aria-labelledby unless it has its own name. A render prop receives aria-labelledby to spread
  - className (string) — Applied to the root wrapper

### Overview
Field wraps a form control with a label, optional description, and error message. It automatically generates htmlFor, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid linking between the label, description, error, and child control.
```tsx
<div className="w-full max-w-[320px]">
<Field
  label="Email"
  size="md"
  description="We'll never share your email with anyone else."
  errorMessage="Please enter a valid email address."
  required
  orientation="vertical"
>
  <Input placeholder="Enter email..." size="md" />
</Field>
</div>
```

### With description
Use description to display helper text below the label. The description is automatically linked to the control via aria-describedby.
```tsx
<div className="w-[320px]">
<Field label="Email" description="We'll never share your email with anyone else.">
  <Input placeholder="Enter email..." />
</Field>
</div>
```

### With error message
Use errorMessage to display a validation error. When provided, the child control automatically receives aria-invalid="true". The error is rendered using the FieldError component with role="alert" for accessibility.
```tsx
<div className="w-[320px]">
<Field label="Email" errorMessage="Please enter a valid email address">
  <Input placeholder="Enter email..." />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Required
Use required to show a visual asterisk after the label. This is purely visual and does not add the required HTML attribute: pass required directly to the child control for form validation.
```tsx
<div className="w-[320px]">
<Field label="Email" required>
  <Input placeholder="Enter email..." />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Sizing
The label and description scale with the child control: Field reads the control's size, so {''} gets a lg label without repeating it. Pass size to Field to set the label size yourself, or when the child is a render prop.
```tsx
<div className="w-full max-w-[320px]">
<Field
  label="Email"
  description="We'll never share your email with anyone else."
  errorMessage="Please enter a valid email address."
  required
  orientation="vertical"
>
  <Input placeholder="Enter email..." size="md" />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Horizontal layout
Use orientation="horizontal" to render the label beside the control instead of above it.
```tsx
<div className="w-full max-w-[480px] flex flex-col gap-4">
<Field label="First name" orientation="horizontal">
  <Input placeholder="Jane" />
</Field>
<Field label="Last name" orientation="horizontal">
  <Input placeholder="Doe" />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Textarea
```tsx
<div className="w-[320px]">
<Field label="Bio" description="Write a short bio for your profile.">
  <Textarea placeholder="Tell us about yourself..." rows={3} />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Select
A Select trigger is not a native form control, so the label's htmlFor cannot name it. Field points the trigger's aria-labelledby at the label, and Select adds its value: a screen reader hears "Role, Admin". DatePicker works the same way. A control with its own aria-label, aria-labelledby or label keeps its name.
```tsx
const [role, setRole] = useState("")

<div className="w-[320px]">
<Field label="Role" description="Select your primary role.">
  <Select
    placeholder="Select a role..."
    value={role}
    onChange={(option) => setRole(option.value)}
    options={[
      { label: "Admin", value: "admin" },
      { label: "Editor", value: "editor" },
      { label: "Viewer", value: "viewer" },
    ]}
  />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Label action
Use labelAction for a link or a small control that acts on the field, at the end of the label row: a password reset, a template switch, a "Replace" link. It takes the label's font size.
```tsx
<Field
label="Password"
labelAction={<TextLink href="/reset-password">Forgot password?</TextLink>}
>
<Input type="password" placeholder="Enter password..." />
</Field>
```

### Slider
Field works with any form control. Use the description to display the current slider value.
```tsx
const [price, setPrice] = useState([200, 800])

<div className="w-[400px]">
<Field
  label="Price Range"
  description={`Set your budget range ($${price[0].toLocaleString()} – ${price[1].toLocaleString()}).`}
>
  <Slider range value={price} onChange={setPrice} min={0} max={1000} step={10} prefixUnit="$" />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Fieldset
Group related fields under a heading and description to create a logical fieldset.
```tsx
<div className="w-[400px]">
<div className="mb-3">
  <h3 className="text-xs font-medium text-secondary uppercase tracking-wider">Address Information</h3>
  <p className="text-xs text-tertiary mt-0.5">We need your address to deliver your order.</p>
</div>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
  <Field label="Street Address">
    <Input placeholder="123 Main St" />
  </Field>
  <div className="flex gap-3">
    <Field label="City" className="flex-1">
      <Input placeholder="New York" />
    </Field>
    <Field label="Postal Code" className="flex-1">
      <Input placeholder="90502" />
    </Field>
  </div>
</div>
</div>
```

### Checkbox
Wrap a group of checkboxes in a Field for a shared label and description. The render prop takes the field props, so Field renders the group as it is instead of wiring the props onto it.
```tsx
<div className="w-[320px]">
<Field label="Notifications" description="Choose which notifications you'd like to receive.">
  {() => (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 mt-1">
      <Checkbox label="Email notifications" />
      <Checkbox label="Push notifications" />
      <Checkbox label="SMS notifications" />
    </div>
  )}
</Field>
</div>
```

### Radio
Use Field with RadioGroup for labeled radio selections. Spread the field props onto the group so its aria-describedby points at the description.
```tsx
const [plan, setPlan] = useState("free")

<div className="w-[320px]">
<Field label="Subscription plan" description="Select your preferred plan.">
  {(fieldProps) => (
    <RadioGroup aria-label="Subscription plan" {...fieldProps} value={plan} onChange={setPlan} direction="col">
      <RadioGroup.Item value="free">Free</RadioGroup.Item>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="pro">Pro, $9/mo</RadioGroup.Item>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="enterprise">Enterprise, $29/mo</RadioGroup.Item>
    </RadioGroup>
  )}
</Field>
</div>
```

### Switch
Pair a Field with a Switch using orientation="horizontal" for inline toggle settings.
```tsx
const [enabled, setEnabled] = useState(false)

<div className="self-stretch mx-auto !max-w-[480px]">
<Field label="Marketing emails" orientation="horizontal" className="justify-between [--field-horizontal-label-width:auto] [--field-horizontal-control-width:auto] [--field-label-horizontal-offset:0px]">
  {(fieldProps) => <Switch id={fieldProps.id} checked={enabled} onCheckedChange={setEnabled} />}
</Field>
</div>
```

### Field group
Stack Field components with a divider to group related notification settings.
```tsx
<div className="w-[400px] divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-6">
  <Field
    label="Responses"
    description="Get notified when the assistant responds to requests that take time, like research or image generation."
  >
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 mt-1">
        <Checkbox label="Push notifications" defaultChecked />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="py-6">
  <Field label="Tasks" description="Get notified when tasks you've created have updates.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 mt-1">
        <Checkbox label="Push notifications" />
        <Checkbox label="Email notifications" />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

### Validation and Errors
Combine required and errorMessage for client-side validation feedback. Toggle errors on and off to see the visual transition.
```tsx
const [name, setName] = useState("")
const [email, setEmail] = useState("bad-email")
const nameError = showErrors && !name ? "Name is required" : undefined
const emailError = showErrors && !email.includes("@") ? "Please enter a valid email address" : undefined

<div className="w-[320px] flex flex-col gap-4">
<Field label="Name" required errorMessage={nameError}>
  <Input placeholder="Enter your name" value={name} onChange={(evt) => setName(evt.target.value)} />
</Field>
<Field label="Email" required errorMessage={emailError}>
  <Input placeholder="Enter your email" value={email} onChange={(evt) => setEmail(evt.target.value)} />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Optical alignment
Use opticallyAlign="start" to apply a negative margin on the child control, aligning its text with the surrounding content. Works with pill inputs. The label, description, and error message stay at the container edge while the control extends past it.
```tsx
<div className="w-[400px]">
<div className="border border-dashed border-alpha/20 rounded-md py-6 px-8">
  <div className="mb-5 text-secondary text-sm">opticallyAlign="start"</div>
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-5">
    <Field label="Full name" opticallyAlign="start">
      <Input placeholder="Jane Doe" />
    </Field>
    <Field
      label="Email"
      description="We'll never share your email."
      errorMessage="Please enter a valid email address."
      required
      opticallyAlign="start"
    >
      <Input placeholder="jane@example.com" />
    </Field>
  </div>
  <Button className="mt-6" color="primary" variant="soft">Submit</Button>
</div>
</div>
```

### Form example

```tsx
return { label: value, value }
})

const value = String(2025 + i)
return { label: value, value }
})
const [month, setMonth] = useState("")
const [year, setYear] = useState("")

<div className="flex flex-col gap-8 w-full !max-w-[460px]">
```

### Birthday input
A date-of-birth input with inline formatting that inserts MM / DD / YYYY separators as you type, wrapped in a Field for label and accessibility. nextBirthday is a plain helper function of the example.
```tsx
const [birthday, setBirthday] = useState("")

<div className="w-[320px]">
<Field label="Birthday">
  <Input
    placeholder="MM / DD / YYYY"
    value={birthday}
    onChange={(evt) => setBirthday(nextBirthday(evt.target.value, birthday))}
    inputMode="numeric"
    maxLength={14}
    autoComplete="off"
  />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Birthday with validation
Birthday input with errorMessage on Field: Field automatically passes aria-invalid down and renders FieldError. nextBirthday and isValidBirthday are plain helper functions of the example.
```tsx
const [birthday, setBirthday] = useState("02 / 30 / 2001")
const errorMessage = birthday && !isValidBirthday(birthday) ? "Please enter a valid date." : undefined

<div className="w-[320px]">
<Field label="Birthday" errorMessage={errorMessage}>
  <Input
    placeholder="MM / DD / YYYY"
    value={birthday}
    onChange={(evt) => setBirthday(nextBirthday(evt.target.value, birthday))}
    inputMode="numeric"
    maxLength={14}
    autoComplete="off"
  />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Birthday segmented input
Three compact Input controls composed as month/day/year with auto-advance behavior, wrapped in a Field for shared label and accessibility. The field id goes to the month input, and the day and year inputs carry their own aria-label. digitsOnly is a plain helper function of the example.
```tsx
const [month, setMonth] = useState("")
const [day, setDay] = useState("")
const [year, setYear] = useState("")
const dayRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
const yearRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)

<div className="w-[320px]">
<Field label="Birthday">
  {(fieldProps) => (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
      <Input
        id={fieldProps.id}
        value={month}
        onChange={(evt) => {
          const next = digitsOnly(evt.target.value, 2)
          setMonth(next)
          if (next.length === 2) dayRef.current?.focus()
        }}
        placeholder="MM"
        inputMode="numeric"
        maxLength={2}
        autoComplete="off"
        className="w-[56px]"
      />
      <span className="text-secondary">/</span>
      <Input
        ref={dayRef}
        value={day}
        onChange={(evt) => {
          const next = digitsOnly(evt.target.value, 2)
          setDay(next)
          if (next.length === 2) yearRef.current?.focus()
        }}
        placeholder="DD"
        aria-label="Day"
        inputMode="numeric"
        maxLength={2}
        autoComplete="off"
        className="w-[56px]"
      />
      <span className="text-secondary">/</span>
      <Input
        ref={yearRef}
        value={year}
        onChange={(evt) => setYear(digitsOnly(evt.target.value, 4))}
        placeholder="YYYY"
        aria-label="Year"
        inputMode="numeric"
        maxLength={4}
        autoComplete="off"
        className="w-[80px]"
      />
    </div>
  )}
</Field>
</div>
```

### Birthday with selects
Dropdown birthday picker with Month/Day/Year selects inside a labeled Field group. The field id goes to the month select, and the day and year selects carry their own aria-label.
```tsx
const [month, setMonth] = useState("")
const [day, setDay] = useState("")
const [year, setYear] = useState("")

<div className="w-[320px]">
<Field label="Birthday">
  {(fieldProps) => (
    <div className="flex gap-2">
      <div className="w-[130px]">
        <Select
          id={fieldProps.id}
          value={month}
          options={monthOptions}
          placeholder="Month"
          onChange={(option) => setMonth(option.value)}
        />
      </div>
      <div className="w-[84px]">
        <Select
          value={day}
          options={dayOptions}
          placeholder="Day"
          onChange={(option) => setDay(option.value)}
          aria-label="Day"
        />
      </div>
      <div className="w-[108px]">
        <Select
          value={year}
          options={yearOptions}
          placeholder="Year"
          onChange={(option) => setYear(option.value)}
          aria-label="Year"
        />
      </div>
    </div>
  )}
</Field>
</div>
```

## File Upload
Mobile-first file upload with MIME-type and size validation, multi-file selection, error states, and read-only file cards.
Import: import { FileUpload, FileCard, FileCardGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/FileUpload"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/file-upload
Props:
  - variant ("compact" | "area") default: "compact" — Visual variant: compact button or larger tappable area
  - label (string) — Button label text
  - description (string) — Helper text below the icon (area variant only)
  - accept (string) — Accepted file types (e.g. ".pdf,.png,image/*")
  - multiple (boolean) default: false — Allow selecting multiple files. Without it, a new pick replaces the current file
  - maxFiles (number) — Maximum number of files. Button disables at limit.
  - maxSize (number) — Maximum file size in bytes
  - value (File[]) — Controlled file list
  - onValueChange ((files: File[]) => void) — Callback when files are added or removed
  - onFileReject ((file: File, reason: string) => void) — Callback when a file is rejected (wrong type, too large, over limit)
  - errorMessage (string) — Error message. Sets the invalid visual state
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid state (auto-set when errorMessage is provided)
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable all interactions
  - id (string) — Id of the hidden file input
  - className (string) — Additional CSS class
  FileCard:
    - file (File) — The file to display
    - onRemove (() => void) — Remove callback. When omitted, the delete button is hidden.
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the remove button
    - className (string) — Additional CSS class
  FileCardGroup:
    - children (ReactNode) — FileCard elements
    - className (string) — Additional CSS class

### Overview
```tsx
const [files, setFiles] = useState<File[]>([])

<div className="w-[360px]">
<FileUpload
  accept=".pdf,.png,.jpg,.jpeg"
  multiple
  maxFiles={5}
  maxSize={10 * 1024 * 1024}
  value={files}
  onValueChange={setFiles}
/>
</div>
```

### With files
File list renders below the button in a bordered pill container. Each file shows a type icon, name with middle truncation, size, and a remove button. initialFiles holds three File objects.
```tsx
const [files, setFiles] = useState<File[]>(initialFiles)

<div className="w-[360px]">
<FileUpload
  accept=".pdf,.png"
  multiple
  maxFiles={5}
  value={files}
  onValueChange={setFiles}
/>
</div>
```

### Error state
```tsx
<div className="w-[360px]">
<FileUpload
  accept=".pdf"
  multiple
  value={files}
  onValueChange={setFiles}
  errorMessage="Please upload at least 2 documents."
/>
</div>
```

### Disabled
```tsx
<div className="w-[360px]">
<FileUpload disabled />
</div>
```

### Read-only
```tsx
<div className="w-[360px]">
<FileCardGroup>
  <FileCard file={file} />
</FileCardGroup>
</div>
```

### With remove
```tsx
const [file, setFile] = useState<File | null>(initialFile)

{file ? (
<div className="w-[360px]">
  <FileCardGroup>
    <FileCard file={file} onRemove={() => setFile(null)} />
  </FileCardGroup>
</div>
) : (
<div className="w-[360px] text-center text-sm text-tertiary">File removed</div>
)}
```

### Multiple files
```tsx
const [files, setFiles] = useState<File[]>(initialFiles)

<div className="w-[360px]">
<FileCardGroup>
  {files.map((file, index) => (
    <FileCard
      key={`${file.name}-${file.size}`}
      file={file}
      onRemove={() => setFiles((prev) => prev.filter((_, i) => i !== index))}
    />
  ))}
</FileCardGroup>
</div>
```

### Read-only list
```tsx
<div className="w-[360px]">
<FileCardGroup>
  {files.map((file) => (
    <FileCard key={`${file.name}-${file.size}`} file={file} />
  ))}
</FileCardGroup>
</div>
```

## Float Input
Text input whose label floats above the value, with error and helper text, a clear button, a password reveal toggle, and a multi-line variant.
Import: import { FloatingLabelInput } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelInput"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/floating-label-input
Props:
  - label (string) — Required. Floating label text
  - value (string) — Controlled value, with onChange
  - defaultValue (string) — Initial value when uncontrolled
  - errorMessage (string) — Validation message below input; sets invalid state
  - invalid (boolean) default: false (true if errorMessage) — Invalid visual state
  - description (ReactNode) — Helper text below the input
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable input interactions
  - readOnly (boolean) default: false — Read-only input state
  - type (string) default: "text" — Input type; password gets a reveal toggle
  - revealable (boolean) default: true for password without an endAdornment — Built-in reveal toggle
  - multiline (boolean) default: false — Render as an auto-growing textarea
  - rows (number) default: 2 — Initial visible text lines when multiline is true
  - allowAutofillExtensions (boolean) default: false — Let password-manager extensions decorate the input
  - startAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered before the input, inside the field. Always shown; keeps the label floated
  - endAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered after the input, before the clear button
  - onClear (() => void) — Shows a clear button when the input has a value; focus returns to the input
  - onRevealedChange ((revealed: boolean) => void) — Called when the reveal toggle is clicked
  - onAutofill (() => void) — Called when the browser autofills the input

### Overview
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" />
```

### Filled state
When the input has a value, the label stays floated above the input.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@example.com" />
```

### Textarea
Use multiline to render an auto-growing textarea with the same floating-label treatment. The textarea starts at 2 rows and grows automatically as content is added. The border radius adjusts to half the input height.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Message" multiline />
```

### With error message
Use the errorMessage prop to display a validation error below the input. When errorMessage is provided, the input automatically enters the invalid state.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput
label="Email address"
defaultValue="jane.doe@example"
invalid
errorMessage="Email is not valid."
/>
```

### With description
Use the description prop to display helper text below the input.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput
label="Email address"
description="We'll never share your email with anyone else."
/>
```

### With description and error
When both description and errorMessage are provided, the error appears first (closest to the input), followed by the description.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput
label="Email address"
defaultValue="jane.doe@example"
invalid
errorMessage="Email is not valid."
description="We'll never share your email with anyone else."
/>
```

### Clear button
Use the onClear prop to display a built-in clear button. The button appears when the input has a value and is not disabled or read-only.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("clearable@example.com")

<FloatingLabelInput
label="Email address"
value={value}
onChange={(evt) => setValue(evt.target.value)}
onClear={() => setValue("")}
/>
```

### Disabled
Use the disabled prop to disable the input, greying it out and preventing user interactions.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" defaultValue="disabled@example.com" disabled />
```

### Read only
Use the readOnly prop to make the input read-only. The user can still select and copy the text.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@example.com" readOnly />
```

### All states
Overview of all input states.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-8 py-8">
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Empty</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Filled</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@gmail.com" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Invalid</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput invalid label="Email address" defaultValue="invalid@email" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Disabled</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput disabled label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@gmail.com" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Read only</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput readOnly label="Email address" defaultValue="readonly@gmail.com" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Password input
A type="password" field ships a built-in reveal toggle: click the eye to show or hide the value. Set revealable to false to remove it.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Password" type="password" />
```

### SSN input
A Social Security Number input combining three techniques: an input mask that auto-inserts dashes (XXX-XX-XXXX) with highlighted segment, value masking that hides digits behind bullets (•••-••-••••), and a built-in revealable toggle to reveal the real value. formatSSN and extractDigits are plain helper functions of the example.
```tsx
const [rawDigits, setRawDigits] = useState("")
const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false)
const formatted = formatSSN(rawDigits)

<FloatingLabelInput
label="Social Security Number"
value={formatted}
inputMode="numeric"
maxLength={11}
onChange={(evt) => setRawDigits(extractDigits(evt.target.value))}
style={!visible && rawDigits ? { color: 'transparent', caretColor: 'var(--color-text)' } : undefined}
revealable
onRevealedChange={setVisible}
/>
```

### Birthday input
A date-of-birth input with inline formatting that inserts separators as you type (MM / DD / YYYY). formatBirthdayValue is a plain helper function of the example.
```tsx
const [birthday, setBirthday] = useState("")

<FloatingLabelInput
label="Birthday"
value={birthday}
maxLength={14}
onChange={(evt) => setBirthday(formatBirthdayValue(evt.target.value))}
/>
```

### Birthday with validation
Use errorMessage to display the birthday validation state; it also marks the input invalid. formatBirthdayValue and isValidBirthday are plain helper functions of the example.
```tsx
const [birthday, setBirthday] = useState("02 / 30 / 2001")

<FloatingLabelInput
label="Birthday"
value={birthday}
maxLength={14}
onChange={(evt) => setBirthday(formatBirthdayValue(evt.target.value))}
errorMessage={birthday && !isValidBirthday(birthday) ? "Please enter a valid date." : undefined}
/>
```

### Birthday states
Overview of birthday input states.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-8 py-8">
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Empty</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput label="Birthday" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Filled</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput label="Birthday" defaultValue="01 / 15 / 1995" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Invalid</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput invalid label="Birthday" defaultValue="02 / 30 / 2001" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Disabled</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput disabled label="Birthday" defaultValue="01 / 15 / 1995" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Select
Use FloatingLabelSelect for plain text dropdowns. The label floats up when a value is selected, matching FloatingLabelInput styling.
```tsx
import { FloatingLabelSelect } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelSelect"
import { Select } from "@plexui/ui/components/Select"

const [role, setRole] = useState("")
const selected = roles.find((option) => option.value === role)
// Select expects a stable trigger renderer
const trigger = useCallback(
({ open }: { open: boolean }) => (
  <FloatingLabelSelect
    label="Role"
    selected={!!selected}
    open={open}
    onClearClick={selected ? () => setRole("") : undefined}
  >
    {selected?.label}
  </FloatingLabelSelect>
),
[selected],
)

<div className="w-[360px]">
<Select
  value={role}
  options={roles}
  onChange={(option) => setRole(option.value)}
  searchPlaceholder="Search roles..."
  listMinWidth={360}
  block
  trigger={trigger}
  checkPosition="end"
/>
</div>
```

### Multiple selection
Pair FloatingLabelSelect with a multiple Select to collect several values while keeping the floating-label treatment. The trigger shows the selected count and exposes a clear button that resets the whole list.
```tsx
import { FloatingLabelSelect } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelSelect"
import { Select } from "@plexui/ui/components/Select"

const [skills, setSkills] = useState<string[]>([])
const hasSelection = skills.length > 0
const display =
skills.length === 1
  ? (skillOptions.find((option) => option.value === skills[0])?.label ?? "")
  : skills.length > 1
    ? `${skills.length} skills`
    : ""
const trigger = useCallback(
({ open }: { open: boolean }) => (
  <FloatingLabelSelect
    label="Skills"
    selected={hasSelection}
    open={open}
    onClearClick={hasSelection ? () => setSkills([]) : undefined}
  >
    {display}
  </FloatingLabelSelect>
),
[hasSelection, display],
)

<div className="w-[360px]">
<Select
  multiple
  clearable
  value={skills}
  options={skillOptions}
  onChange={(options) => setSkills(options.map((option) => option.value))}
  searchPlaceholder="Search skills..."
  listMinWidth={360}
  block
  trigger={trigger}
  checkPosition="end"
/>
</div>
```

### Country select
Use FloatingLabelSelect alongside FloatingLabelInput for consistent form styling. The select trigger shares the same floating-label visual shell. The label floats up when a value is selected. CountryLabel is a helper of the example that shows a flag next to the name.
```tsx
import { FloatingLabelSelect } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelSelect"
import { Select, type Option } from "@plexui/ui/components/Select"

// Outside the component: Select needs a stable OptionView
const CountryOptionView = ({ value, label }: Option) => <CountryLabel code={value} label={label} />

const [country, setCountry] = useState("")
const selected = countries.find((option) => option.value === country)
const trigger = useCallback(
({ open }: { open: boolean }) => (
  <FloatingLabelSelect
    label="Country"
    selected={!!selected}
    open={open}
    onClearClick={selected ? () => setCountry("") : undefined}
  >
    {selected && <CountryLabel code={selected.value} label={selected.label} />}
  </FloatingLabelSelect>
),
[selected],
)

<div className="w-[360px]">
<Select
  value={country}
  options={countries}
  onChange={(option) => setCountry(option.value)}
  searchPlaceholder="Search countries..."
  OptionView={CountryOptionView}
  listMinWidth={360}
  block
  trigger={trigger}
  checkPosition="end"
/>
</div>
```

### Phone input
A country code selector paired with a FloatingLabelInput that uses startAdornment to show the dial code as a non-editable prefix. The prefix is always shown, and it keeps the label floated. The country list, its search predicate and trigger, CountryOptionView, formatPhoneNumber and dialCodeOf are helpers of the example.
```tsx
const [country, setCountry] = useState("es")
const [phone, setPhone] = useState("")
const phoneInputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)

<div className="w-[360px] flex flex-col gap-3">
<Select
  value={country}
  options={phoneCountryOptions}
  onChange={(option) => {
    setCountry(option.value)
    setTimeout(() => phoneInputRef.current?.focus(), 0)
  }}
  searchPlaceholder="Search countries..."
  OptionView={CountryOptionView}
  searchPredicate={phoneCountrySearchPredicate}
  listMinWidth={360}
  block
  size="3xl"
  trigger={phoneCountryTrigger}
  checkPosition="end"
/>
<FloatingLabelInput
  ref={phoneInputRef}
  label="Phone number"
  value={phone}
  onChange={(evt) => setPhone(formatPhoneNumber(evt.target.value.replace(/\D/g, ""), country))}
  type="tel"
  inputMode="tel"
  startAdornment={<span className="text-tertiary whitespace-nowrap select-none mr-2">{dialCodeOf(country)}</span>}
/>
</div>
```

## Indicators
Loading and progress indicators, from circular spinners and determinate progress rings to animated dots, with configurable color and stroke.
Import: import { LoadingIndicator, CircularProgress, LoadingDots } from "@plexui/ui/components/Indicator"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/indicators
  LoadingIndicator:
    - size (number | string) default: "1em" — Size in px or any CSS length (or use the --indicator-size CSS variable)
    - strokeWidth (number) default: 2 — Stroke width in px
  CircularProgress:
    - progress (number) — Static progress 0-100 (disables the simulated animation)
    - done (boolean) default: false — Fills the ring and ends the simulated progress
    - maxDuration (number) default: 15000 — Duration of the simulated progress in ms
    - size (number | string) default: "28px" — Diameter in px or any CSS length
    - strokeWidth (number) default: 2 — Stroke thickness in px, capped at 4
    - trackColor (string) — Track color (CSS variable or value)
    - trackActiveColor (string) — Active segment color

### Overview
The demos restart every few seconds through a done flag that fills the ring before the simulation starts over.
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-6">
<LoadingIndicator size={20} />
<CircularProgress size={24} />
<LoadingDots />
</div>
```

### LoadingIndicator
Simple spinning indicator for general loading states.
```tsx
<LoadingIndicator />
```

### Sizing & stroke
By default, the indicator adapts to the surrounding font-size and color of text. You can control the size of the LoadingIndicator using the --indicator-size CSS custom property.
```tsx
<LoadingIndicator size={30} strokeWidth={2} />
```

### Color
The indicator defaults to currentcolor, inheriting the surrounding text color. This can also be customized by altering the --indicator-color variable around the DOM scope of the component.
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-danger">
<LoadingIndicator size={16} /> <span>Destroying forever...</span>
</div>
```

### Duration
You can control the rotation speed of the spinner with --indicator-rotate-duration.
```tsx
<div style={{ '--indicator-rotate-duration': '3s' } as React.CSSProperties}>
<LoadingIndicator />
</div>
```

### CircularProgress
Circular progress ring with simulated progress animation.
```tsx
<CircularProgress />
```

### Progress
Use progress to show static progress and prevent the animation.
```tsx
<CircularProgress progress={25} />
```

### Sizing & stroke
Use size and strokeWidth. Or use --circular-progress-size and --circular-progress-stroke CSS variables.
```tsx
<CircularProgress size={30} strokeWidth={2} />
```

### Color
Customize the color of the indicator with the --circular-progress-track-color and --circular-progress-track-active-color variables.
```tsx
<CircularProgress trackColor="var(--alpha-15)" trackActiveColor="var(--gray-1000)" />
```

### LoadingDots
Indicate typing progress with staggered pulsing dot animation.
```tsx
<LoadingDots />
```

### Color
