The indicator defaults to currentcolor, inheriting the surrounding text color. You can customize the color by providing a different color value or context.
```tsx
<div className="text-danger">
<LoadingDots />
</div>
```

## Input Group
Input or textarea with icons, text, buttons and menus attached inside one frame, inline or as header and footer rows, in every input size and style.
Import: import { InputGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/InputGroup"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/input-group
Props:
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Control height, on the same scale as Input (22px to 48px)
  - variant ("outline" | "soft") default: "outline" — Visual style of the frame
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded frame, with pill buttons inside
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disables the control and the buttons inside
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid border; sets aria-invalid on the control
  - className (string) — Applied to the root <div>
  InputGroup.Addon:
    - align ("inline-start" | "inline-end" | "block-start" | "block-end") default: "inline-start" — Before or after the control on its line, or a row above or below it
    - className (string) — Applied to the addon <div>

### Overview
Put an InputGroup.Input and one or more InputGroup.Addons inside an InputGroup. The group draws the frame and passes size, pill, disabled and invalid down to the control and the buttons.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Search..." />
<InputGroup.Addon>
  <Search />
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>12 results</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Variants
Use variant to stylize the group, like Input.
```tsx
<InputGroup variant="outline">...</InputGroup>
<InputGroup variant="soft">...</InputGroup>
```

### Sizes
Every Input size from 3xs to 3xl. Icons, text and InputGroup.Button scale with the group: buttons in inline addons fit the control height and keep a 4px inset.
```tsx
<InputGroup size="lg">
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Search..." />
<InputGroup.Addon>
  <Search />
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Button>Search</InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Align
Use align on InputGroup.Addon to place it before (inline-start, the default) or after (inline-end) the control, or as a row above (block-start) or below (block-end) it. Place addons after the control in the markup so the tab order starts with the field; align handles the visual position.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Ada Lovelace" />
<InputGroup.Addon align="block-start">
  <InputGroup.Text>Full name</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Text
Use InputGroup.Text for prefixes, suffixes, units and counters. Clicking text or icons in an addon focuses the field.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="0.00" inputMode="decimal" />
<InputGroup.Addon>
  <InputGroup.Text>$</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>USD</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Button
InputGroup.Button is a Button that defaults to ghost and secondary and takes its size from the group. Pass uniform for icon buttons.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Search the docs..." />
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Button variant="soft">Search</InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Dropdown
Wrap an InputGroup.Button in a Menu to pick a unit of measurement next to the value.
```tsx
const UNITS = [
{ value: "kg", label: "Kilograms" },
{ value: "lb", label: "Pounds" },
{ value: "st", label: "Stones" },
]
const [unit, setUnit] = useState("kg")

return (
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroup.Input defaultValue="72" inputMode="decimal" aria-label="Weight" />
  <InputGroup.Addon>
    <InputGroup.Text>Weight</InputGroup.Text>
  </InputGroup.Addon>
  <InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
    <Menu>
      <Menu.Trigger>
        <InputGroup.Button aria-label="Weight unit">
          {unit}
          <ChevronDownMd />
        </InputGroup.Button>
      </Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Content align="end" minWidth={160}>
        {UNITS.map((item) => (
          <Menu.CheckboxItem
            key={item.value}
            checked={unit === item.value}
            onCheckedChange={() => setUnit(item.value)}
            indicatorVariant="ghost"
          >
            {item.label} ({item.value})
          </Menu.CheckboxItem>
        ))}
      </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
)
```

### Spinner
Show a LoadingIndicator in an addon while a value is searched or saved.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input defaultValue="Saving changes" readOnly />
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>Saving...</InputGroup.Text>
  <LoadingIndicator />
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Textarea
With InputGroup.Textarea, use block-start and block-end addons for a header and a footer. Utility classes such as ml-auto push a button to the far side.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Textarea placeholder="console.log('Hello, world!');" rows={4} className="font-mono" />
<InputGroup.Addon align="block-start">
  <InputGroup.Text>
    <FileCode />
    script.js
  </InputGroup.Text>
  <InputGroup.Button uniform aria-label="Copy" className="ml-auto">
    <Copy />
  </InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="block-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>Line 1, Column 1</InputGroup.Text>
  <InputGroup.Button variant="solid" color="primary" className="ml-auto">
    Run
    <Play />
  </InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

## Input
Text input with start and end adornments, a clear button, a password visibility toggle, and presets for SSN and birthday.
Import: import { Input } from "@plexui/ui/components/Input"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/input
Props:
  - variant ("outline" | "soft" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Visual style of the input; ghost has no border and no fill
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Controls the size of the input
  - gutterSize ("2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl") — Controls gutter on the edges; defaults to value from size
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disables the input visually and from interactions
  - readOnly (boolean) default: false — Makes the input read-only and hides the clear button
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Mark the input as invalid
  - allowAutofillExtensions (boolean) default: type === "password" || !!name — Allow autofill extensions to appear in the input
  - autoSelect (boolean) default: false — Select all contents of the input when mounted
  - startAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered at the start of the input
  - endAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered at the end of the input
  - onClear (() => void) — When provided, displays a clear button that appears when the input has a value
  - onAutofill (() => void) — Called when the browser autofills the input
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded pill shape
  - opticallyAlign ("start" | "end") — Applies a negative margin using the current gutter to optically align with surrounding content
  Input.AdornmentButton:
    - color (SemanticColor) — Tint of the pressed (aria-pressed="true") state; the neutral primary-soft tint when unset
    - type (string) default: "button" — Button type

### Overview
```tsx
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." />
```

### Variants
Use variant to stylize the input. ghost has no border and no fill, for a field its container already frames, such as the search line at the top of a dialog; it still turns red when invalid.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 w-[320px]">
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." variant="outline" />
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." variant="soft" />
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." variant="ghost" />
</div>
```

### Sizing & roundness
Sizing of the input is controlled with size and gutterSize props. size sets the input to a specific control height, and gutterSize sets the horizontal padding. Each size provides default values for gutterSize, as well as font-size. Each of these values can be overridden independently.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5 justify-start items-start w-[320px]">
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." size="lg" />
<Input placeholder="Search..." startAdornment={<Search className="fill-tertiary" />} size="lg" />
<Input value={username} placeholder="Username" onChange={(evt) => setUsername(evt.target.value)} maxLength={16} endAdornment={<span className="mt-[1.5px] tabular-nums text-tertiary text-[.875em]">{username.length}/16</span>} />
</div>
```

### Start adornment
You can add arbitrary content to the beginning of an input with startAdornment, like a search icon. Ideally, the spacing will look pretty good by default. If you need to customize the spacing: gutterSize determines the amount of spacing on the edges of the container, which you can fine-tune as needed (if you need precise spacing not supported by gutterSize, use negative left margin on your adornment directly, e.g. -ml-2). The spacing between the adornment and the input is controlled with gap on the container, which you can customize as needed with Tailwind classes.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Start adornment"
startAdornment={<Search className="fill-tertiary" />}
/>
```

### Clear button
Use the onClear prop to display a built-in clear button. The button appears when the input has a value and is not disabled or read-only. Clicking it keeps focus in the input.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Enter text..."
value={value}
onChange={(evt) => setValue(evt.target.value)}
onClear={() => setValue("")}
pill
/>
```

### End adornment
You can add arbitrary content to the end of an input with endAdornment, like a character counter or custom icon. The same spacing guidance from startAdornment applies here.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Username"
value={username}
onChange={(evt) => setUsername(evt.target.value)}
maxLength={16}
endAdornment={
  <span className="mt-[1.5px] tabular-nums text-tertiary text-[.875em]">
    {username.length}/16
  </span>
}
/>
```

### Password with visibility toggle
Combine endAdornment with an Input.AdornmentButton to switch between type="password" and type="text". Works across all sizes, variants, and with pill.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Password"
type={visible ? 'text' : 'password'}
endAdornment={
  <Input.AdornmentButton aria-pressed={visible} onClick={toggle}>
    {visible ? <EyeOff /> : <Eye />}
  </Input.AdornmentButton>
}
/>
```

### SSN input
A masked SSN field that formats input as XXX-XX-XXXX, hides digits behind bullets when masked, and reveals the value via an Input.AdornmentButton in endAdornment. An inline mask suffix highlights the next expected segment. Adapts to all sizes automatically.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Social Security Number"
value={formatted}
inputMode="numeric"
endAdornment={
  <Input.AdornmentButton aria-pressed={visible} onClick={toggle}>
    {visible ? <EyeOff /> : <Eye />}
  </Input.AdornmentButton>
}
style={!visible && rawDigits ? { color: 'transparent', caretColor: 'var(--color-text)' } : undefined}
/>
```

### Birthday input
A date-of-birth input with inline formatting that inserts separators as you type (MM / DD / YYYY). An inline mask suffix highlights the next expected segment. Works across all sizes, variants, and with pill.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Birthday (MM / DD / YYYY)"
value={birthday}
inputMode="numeric"
maxLength={14}
/>
```

### Birthday with validation
Use invalid and FieldError to display a validation state when the entered date is not valid.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Birthday (MM / DD / YYYY)"
value={birthday}
inputMode="numeric"
invalid={!!errorMessage}
/>
```

### Disabled
Use the disabled prop to disable the input, greying it out and preventing user interactions.
```tsx
<Input disabled defaultValue="Jane Doe" />
```

### Invalid
Use the invalid prop to mark the input as invalid. You decide how this state is removed, whether that's through onFocus, onChange, an onSubmit handler, etc. Default visual styles will be applied, based on the variant. Additionally, [data-invalid] is applied to the container for custom styling.
```tsx
<Input invalid placeholder="Invalid input" />
```

### Auto select text
Pass autoSelect to select all text in the input, useful when pairing with other copy actions. This prop behaves like an imperative action when toggled and allows selection to change.
```tsx
<Input autoSelect placeholder="Add text..." defaultValue="Toggle to auto select" />
```

### Autofill extensions
By default, autofill extensions are prevented by Input. For the occasions where you want browser extensions to be present, pass allowAutofillExtensions to remove the disabling. When name is passed, or type is set to "password", this value will default to true.
```tsx
<Input allowAutofillExtensions name="email" placeholder="Allowed" />
```

### With button
You can pair Input and Button components together by using the same size value.
```tsx
<div className="flex gap-2">
<Input placeholder="jane.doe@gmail.com" size="lg" variant="outline" />
<Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="outline" pill={false}>Subscribe</Button>
</div>
```

### Optical alignment
```tsx
<Field label="Full name" opticallyAlign="start">
<Input placeholder="Jane Doe" pill />
</Field>
<Field
label="Email"
description="We'll never share your email."
errorMessage="Please enter a valid email address."
required
opticallyAlign="start"
>
<Input placeholder="jane@example.com" pill />
</Field>
<Button className="mt-6" color="primary" variant="soft" pill>
Submit
</Button>
```

## Kbd
A key or a keyboard shortcut, such as ⌘K, set inline in text, in a tooltip or at the end of a menu item.
Import: import { Kbd } from "@plexui/ui/components/Kbd"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/kbd
Props:
  - size ("xs" | "sm" | "md") default: "sm" — Height and text size: 16px, 20px or 24px
  - variant ("soft" | "outline") default: "soft" — soft fills the key, outline draws its edge; both mix the text color
  - className (string) — Applied to the kbd element

### Overview
Kbd renders a {''} element: the semantic tag for keyboard input. It sits on the text baseline, so it can stand in a sentence.
```tsx
<p>
Press <Kbd>/</Kbd> to search, <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> to close.
</p>
```

### Shortcut
Use Kbd.Group for keys pressed together. Each key keeps its own frame.
```tsx
<Kbd.Group>
<Kbd>⌘</Kbd>
<Kbd>K</Kbd>
</Kbd.Group>

<Kbd.Group>
<Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>
<Kbd>Shift</Kbd>
<Kbd>P</Kbd>
</Kbd.Group>
```

### Sizes and variants
Three sizes: xs (16px) for tooltips and menu items, sm (20px, default) for text, md (24px) next to larger controls. soft (default) fills the key, outline draws its edge. Both mix the surrounding text color, so a key reads on a page, in a dark tooltip and in a highlighted menu item alike.
```tsx
<Kbd size="xs">⌘K</Kbd>
<Kbd size="sm">⌘K</Kbd>
<Kbd size="md">⌘K</Kbd>

<Kbd variant="outline">⌘K</Kbd>
```

### In a tooltip and a menu
Show a control's shortcut in its tooltip, or at the end of a menu item. Kbd only shows the keys: announce the shortcut to assistive technology with aria-keyshortcuts on the control that has it.
```tsx
<Tooltip
content={
  <span className="flex items-center gap-2">
    Search
    <Kbd.Group>
      <Kbd size="xs">⌘</Kbd>
      <Kbd size="xs">K</Kbd>
    </Kbd.Group>
  </span>
}
>
<Button color="secondary" variant="outline" uniform aria-label="Search" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K">
  <Search />
</Button>
</Tooltip>

<Menu.Item onSelect={undo}>
<span className="flex-1">Undo</span>
<Kbd size="xs" variant="outline">⌘Z</Kbd>
</Menu.Item>
```

## Label
Accessible form label that points at any control by its id, so clicking it focuses or toggles the control, with consistent typography across forms.
Import: import { Label } from "@plexui/ui/components/Label"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/label
Props:
  - htmlFor (string) default: — — id of the associated control. Clicks on the label focus or activate the control.
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root <label> element

### Overview
Clicking the label toggles the checkbox it points at. Here accepted starts as true.
```tsx
const [accepted, setAccepted] = useState(true);

return (
<div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
  <Checkbox id="terms" checked={accepted} onCheckedChange={setAccepted} />
  <Label htmlFor="terms">Accept terms and conditions</Label>
</div>
);
```

### Label in Field
For stacked form rows with descriptions, errors, and horizontal layouts, use the Field component. It renders the label internally, hooks up htmlFor automatically, and handles the surrounding spacing.
```tsx
<Field label="Name on Card">
<Input placeholder="Aisha Cooper" />
</Field>

<Field label="Card Number" description="Enter your 16-digit card number">
<Input placeholder="1234 5678 9012 3456" />
</Field>

{/* Month / Year / CVV in a 3-col grid */}
{/* Billing Address section + checkbox */}
{/* Comments textarea + Submit / Cancel */}
```

## Markdown Editor
Compact rich text editor powered by Tiptap, embedded in a form field, with a markdown formatting toolbar, variants, and an invalid state.
Import: import { MarkdownEditor } from "@plexui/ui/components/MarkdownEditor"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/markdown-editor
Props:
  - variant ("outline" | "soft") default: "outline" — Visual style of the editor
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the editor
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Mark as invalid
  - placeholder (string) — Placeholder text when empty
  - value (string) — Controlled markdown value
  - defaultValue (string) — Initial markdown for uncontrolled mode
  - onChange ((markdown: string) => void) — Called on content change
  - toolbarEnd (ReactNode) — Content rendered at the end of the toolbar
  - rows (number) default: 1 — Minimum visible rows
  - id (string) — id of the editable element (Field sets it)
  - aria-label (string) — Accessible name of the editable element
  - aria-labelledby (string) — Id of the element that names the editor, such as a visible label
  - aria-describedby (string) — aria-describedby of the editable element (Field sets it)
  - aria-invalid (boolean) — Sets aria-invalid on the editable element and the invalid style (Field sets it with errorMessage)
  - className (string) — Applied to the container

### Placeholder
Use placeholder to display hint text when the editor is empty.
```tsx
<MarkdownEditor placeholder="Enter text..." />
```

### All formatting
Example with all supported formatting: bold, italic, links, ordered lists, and unordered lists. Click inside formatted text to see toolbar buttons toggle.
```tsx
<MarkdownEditor defaultValue={allFormattingMd} />
```

### With Field
Wrap with Field to add label, description, and error handling. The editor receives id and aria-describedby automatically.
```tsx
<Field label="Description" description="Supports bold, italic, lists, and links.">
<MarkdownEditor placeholder="Enter description..." />
</Field>
```

### Toolbar end slot
Use toolbarEnd to render custom content at the end of the toolbar, for example an &ldquo;Edit translations&rdquo; button. markdownEditorStyles.toolbarButton gives it the style of the built-in toolbar buttons.
```tsx
import { MarkdownEditor, markdownEditorStyles } from "@plexui/ui/components/MarkdownEditor"
import { Translate } from "@plexui/ui/components/Icon"

<Field label="Text markdown">
<MarkdownEditor
  placeholder="Enter text..."
  toolbarEnd={
    <button
      type="button"
      className={markdownEditorStyles.toolbarButton}
      aria-label="Edit translations"
      title="Edit translations"
    >
      <Translate />
    </button>
  }
/>
</Field>
```

### Variants
Use variant to switch between outline (default) and soft styles.
```tsx
<Field label="Outline">
<MarkdownEditor placeholder="Outline variant..." variant="outline" />
</Field>
<Field label="Soft">
<MarkdownEditor placeholder="Soft variant..." variant="soft" />
</Field>
```

### Disabled
Use disabled to prevent editing and grey out the component.
```tsx
<MarkdownEditor disabled defaultValue="This content is **read-only**." />
```

### Invalid
Use invalid or wrap with Field and pass errorMessage to show an error state.
```tsx
<Field label="Bio" errorMessage="This field is required.">
<MarkdownEditor placeholder="Tell us about yourself..." invalid />
</Field>
```

## Markdown
Markdown renderer for rich formatted content, with headings, lists, tables, code blocks, and KaTeX math expressions out of the box.
Import: import { Markdown } from "@plexui/ui/components/Markdown"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/markdown
Props:
  - children (string) — Required. Markdown source
  - includeMath (boolean) default: false — Enable LaTeX math rendering
  - breakNewLines (boolean) default: false — Turn single newlines into line breaks
  - copyableCodeBlocks (boolean) default: true — Show a copy button on code blocks
  - collapsibleCodeBlocks (boolean) default: true — Render code blocks in the collapsible view with a View Code button
  - components (Record<string, MarkdownComponent>) — Tag name to component overrides, applied over the built-in ones
  - directives (MarkdownDirective[]) — Custom directives, each rendered by its own component
  - remarkPlugins (PluggableList) — Extra remark plugins, after the built-in ones
  - rehypePlugins (PluggableList) — Extra rehype plugins
  - allowedElements (string[]) — Only render these elements
  - disallowedElements (string[]) — Never render these elements
  - skipHtml (boolean) default: false — Ignore raw HTML in the source
  - urlTransform ((url: string) => string) — Rewrites URLs; the default drops unsafe protocols (javascript:) and keeps tel: and sms:
  - className (string) — Applied to the wrapping element

### Overview
Use Markdown to render rich markdown text.
```tsx
<Markdown>{markdownContent}</Markdown>
```

### Math
Use includeMath to enable LaTeX rendering.
```tsx
<Markdown includeMath>{markdownWithLatex}</Markdown>
```

## Menu
Dropdown menu for structured actions with grouped items, submenus, checkbox and radio items, and horizontal layouts.
Import: import { Menu } from "@plexui/ui/components/Menu"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/menu
Props:
  - forceOpen (boolean) — Keep menu open (controlled)
  - onOpen (() => void) — Called when menu opens
  - onClose (() => void) — Called when menu closes
  - modal (boolean) default: false — Whether menu is modal (focus trap)
  Menu.Trigger:
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Prevent the menu from opening
  Menu.Content:
    - width (number | "auto") default: "auto" — Panel width in px
    - minWidth (number | "auto") default: 300 — Minimum panel width in px (vertical layout)
    - maxHeight (number) — Maximum panel height in px
    - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "bottom" — Preferred placement
    - sideOffset (number) default: 5 — Distance from the trigger in px
    - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Alignment relative to trigger
    - alignOffset (number) default: -5 — Offset from the start or end alignment in px
    - layout ("vertical" | "horizontal") default: "vertical" — Layout direction. Use horizontal for icon toolbars
    - size ("sm" | "md" | "lg") default: "md" — Size of horizontal menu items (icon size + padding)
    - onCloseAutoFocus ((event: Event) => void) — Called before focus returns to the trigger; call event.preventDefault() to keep it from moving there
  Menu.Item:
    - description (ReactNode) — Second line under the label. The label turns semibold on its own
    - onSelect ((event: Event) => void) — Called when item is selected; call event.preventDefault() to keep the menu open
    - onClick ((event: MouseEvent) => void) — Called when the item is clicked; also makes the item interactive
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the item
    - danger (boolean) default: false — Destructive action: the item is drawn in the danger color
    - className (string) — Applied to the item
  Menu.CheckboxItem:
    - checked (boolean | "indeterminate") — Checked state
    - onCheckedChange ((checked: boolean) => void) — When checkbox toggles
    - onSelect ((event: Event) => void) — Use with preventDefault() to keep menu open
    - indicatorPosition ("start" | "end") default: "end" — Checkbox position
    - indicatorVariant ("solid" | "ghost") default: "solid" — Checkbox indicator style
    - disabled (boolean) — Disable the item

### Overview
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost">Sample menu <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content width={210} minWidth={210}>
  <Menu.Item description="sam.smith@gmail.com">Sam Smith</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Link href="#">Your profile</Menu.Link>
  <Menu.Link href="#">Terms & policies</Menu.Link>
  <Menu.Item disabled onSelect={() => {}}>Feature flags</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Logout</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Natural sizing
Menu supports several sizing strategies:Natural sizing: use minWidth="auto" to have the menu fit naturally to the size of the content.Fixed size: use width and minWidth to set the menu to a fixed size, regardless of content size.Flexible sizing: minWidth can be used by itself to describe a menu that must be a given size, but can grow larger depending on its content.Max sizing: apply max-width to the children of Menu.Content. maxWidth isn't exposed as a prop because it's reserved for Radix variables used in collision detection.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost" className="font-semibold gap-1.5"><Tools /> Tools</Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content minWidth="auto">
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Functions height={18} width={18} /> Function</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Search height={18} width={18} /> File Search</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Globe height={18} width={18} /> Web Search</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Code height={18} width={18} /> Code Interpreter</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><ImageSquare height={18} width={18} /> Image Generation</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Horizontal (icons only)
Set layout="horizontal" on Menu.Content for an iOS-style icon toolbar. Give each icon-only item a visually hidden label so screen readers can name the action.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost">Actions <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content layout="horizontal" size="md" minWidth="auto">
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><EditPencil /><span className="sr-only">Edit</span></Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><SettingsCog /><span className="sr-only">Settings</span></Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Play /><span className="sr-only">Play</span></Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><UnfoldHorizontal /><span className="sr-only">Expand</span></Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Horizontal (icons with labels)
Add text labels below icons for a labeled toolbar. The horizontal layout automatically stacks icon and text vertically within each item.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost">Actions <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content layout="horizontal" size="md" minWidth="auto">
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><EditPencil /> Edit</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><SettingsCog /> Settings</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Play /> Play</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><UnfoldHorizontal /> Expand</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Grouped items
Use Menu.Group and Menu.Label to organize related items into labeled sections.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost" className="font-semibold gap-1.5"><FileDocument /> Templates <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content minWidth={220}>
  <Menu.Group>
    <Menu.Label>Active</Menu.Label>
    <Menu.Link href="#">Welcome email</Menu.Link>
    <Menu.Link href="#">Order confirmation</Menu.Link>
    <Menu.Link href="#">Password reset</Menu.Link>
  </Menu.Group>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Group>
    <Menu.Label>Draft</Menu.Label>
    <Menu.Link href="#">New promo campaign</Menu.Link>
    <Menu.Link href="#">Account deactivation</Menu.Link>
  </Menu.Group>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Submenus
Use Menu.Sub, Menu.SubTrigger, and Menu.SubContent for nested menus.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost">Options <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content minWidth={180}>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Edit</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Duplicate</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Sub>
    <Menu.SubTrigger>More</Menu.SubTrigger>
    <Menu.SubContent>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Move to project…</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Move to folder…</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Separator />
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Advanced options…</Menu.Item>
    </Menu.SubContent>
  </Menu.Sub>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Share</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Add to favorites</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Delete</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Checkbox items
Use Menu.CheckboxItem with checked, onCheckedChange, and {"onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}"} to keep the menu open.
```tsx
const [settings, setSettings] = useState({
showGrid: true,
showLabels: false,
enableShadows: false,
})

return (
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger>
    <Button variant="ghost" color="primary">
      Checkbox menu <ChevronDownMd />
    </Button>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Content minWidth={200}>
    <Menu.CheckboxItem
      checked={settings.showGrid}
      onCheckedChange={(checked) => setSettings((s) => ({ ...s, showGrid: checked }))}
      onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
      indicatorPosition="end"
      indicatorVariant="solid"
    >
      Show grid lines
    </Menu.CheckboxItem>
    <Menu.CheckboxItem
      checked={settings.showLabels}
      onCheckedChange={(checked) => setSettings((s) => ({ ...s, showLabels: checked }))}
      onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
      indicatorPosition="end"
      indicatorVariant="solid"
    >
      Display labels
    </Menu.CheckboxItem>
    <Menu.CheckboxItem
      checked={settings.enableShadows}
      onCheckedChange={(checked) => setSettings((s) => ({ ...s, enableShadows: checked }))}
      onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
      indicatorPosition="end"
      indicatorVariant="solid"
    >
      Enable shadows
    </Menu.CheckboxItem>
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
)
```

### Radio items
Use Menu.RadioGroup and Menu.RadioItem for single-selection options.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("any")

<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" variant="ghost">
    Radio menu <ChevronDownMd />
  </Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content align="start" minWidth="auto" width="auto">
  <Menu.RadioGroup
    indicatorPosition="end"
    value={value}
    onChange={setValue}
  >
    <Menu.RadioItem value="any">Any time</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="today" disabled>Today</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="last7d">Last 7 days</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="last30d">Last 30 days</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="last3m">Last 3 months</Menu.RadioItem>
  </Menu.RadioGroup>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Item actions
Use Menu.ItemActions and Menu.ItemAction for hover actions (e.g. delete) on an item.Accessibility note: these actions are not keyboard accessible due to how Radix Menu works, so they should not be critical actions with no other parity.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost" className="font-semibold gap-1.5"><History /> Conversations</Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content width={270}>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>
    <span className="flex-1 truncate">Sample thread title</span>
    <Menu.ItemActions>
      <Menu.ItemAction onClick={() => {}}><Trash /></Menu.ItemAction>
    </Menu.ItemActions>
  </Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>
    <span className="flex-1 truncate">Another sample thread title</span>
    <Menu.ItemActions>
      <Menu.ItemAction onClick={() => {}}><Trash /></Menu.ItemAction>
    </Menu.ItemActions>
  </Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>
    <span className="flex-1 truncate">Long thread title that is going to be clipped off</span>
    <Menu.ItemActions>
      <Menu.ItemAction onClick={() => {}}><Trash /></Menu.ItemAction>
    </Menu.ItemActions>
  </Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Destructive items
Mark a destructive action (delete, remove, leave) with danger: the label and the highlight take the danger color, and a description keeps its secondary color. Menu.Link takes danger too. Put such items last, after a separator.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform aria-label="More actions">
    <DotsHorizontal />
  </Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content align="end" minWidth={200}>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={rename}><EditPencil /> Rename</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={duplicate}>Duplicate</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Item onSelect={remove} danger><Trash /> Delete project</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

## OTP Input
Input for one-time passwords and verification codes, with split digit cells, grouped layouts, error states, and autofill.
Import: import { OTPInput } from "@plexui/ui/components/OTPInput"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/otp-input
Props:
  - length (number) default: 6 — Number of digit cells
  - value (string) — Controlled value
  - onChange ((value: string) => void) — Called when value changes
  - onComplete ((value: string) => void) — Called when all digits filled
  - grouping (number[]) — Grouping pattern with extra gap (e.g. [3,3])
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid visual state
  - errorMessage (string) — Error message below the input
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable all cells
  - autoFocus (boolean) default: false — Auto-focus first cell on mount
  - className (string) — Applied to the root element

### Overview
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("")

<OTPInput value={value} onChange={setValue} />
```

### Filled state
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("488030")

<OTPInput value={value} onChange={setValue} />
```

### Grouped (3+3)
```tsx
<OTPInput grouping={[3, 3]} />
```

### With error
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("48803")

<OTPInput value={value} onChange={setValue} invalid errorMessage="Invalid verification code." />
```

### Disabled
```tsx
<OTPInput value="488030" disabled />
```

## Popover
A floating panel for contextual UI, with flexible sizing, hover triggers, a controllable open state and nesting.
Import: import { Popover } from "@plexui/ui/components/Popover"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/popover
Props:
  - open (boolean) — Controlled open state; uncontrolled when omitted
  - onOpenChange ((nextState: boolean) => void) — Called when the popover opens or closes
  - showOnHover (boolean) default: false — Open on hover and focus instead of click
  - hoverOpenDelay (number) default: 150 — Delay before a hover popover opens (ms)
  Popover.Content:
    - width (number | "auto") default: "auto" — Panel width in px
    - minWidth (number | "auto") default: 300 — Minimum panel width in px
    - maxWidth (number) default: 700 — Maximum panel width in px, capped by the space available in the viewport
    - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "bottom" — Preferred placement; flips when it collides
    - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Alignment relative to trigger
    - sideOffset (number) default: 8 — Offset from trigger (px)
    - alignOffset (number) default: -5 — Offset from the start or end alignment (px)
    - avoidCollisions (boolean) default: true — Reposition to stay inside the viewport and scroll containers
    - translucent (boolean) default: false — Translucent, blurred surface
    - autoFocus (boolean) default: true — Move focus into the panel when it opens (hover popovers never take focus)
    - className (string) — Applied to the panel

### Overview
```tsx
<Popover>
<Popover.Trigger><Button color="primary">Generate</Button></Popover.Trigger>
<Popover.Content side="right">...</Popover.Content>
</Popover>
```

### Sizing the popover
The popover can be sized with any combination of width, minWidth, or maxWidth. All popovers default to a minWidth of 300px, and a maxWidth of 700px, capped by the space available in the viewport.
```tsx
<Popover>
<Popover.Trigger>...</Popover.Trigger>
<Popover.Content minWidth="auto" side="top">...</Popover.Content>
</Popover>
```

### Open on hover
Use showOnHover to create popovers that appear on hover and focus events. This should be used sparingly and with clear intention.By default, hover popovers will not alter the focused element on the page, nor restore focus to the trigger on close. However, if interactive content is present in the popover, and tab is used to navigate into the popover, focus will be restored to the trigger on close.
```tsx
<Popover showOnHover>
<Popover.Trigger>...</Popover.Trigger>
<Popover.Content>...</Popover.Content>
</Popover>
```

### Using the controller
You can access usePopoverController() controller context from components within Popover.Content. The hook exposes two methods, close() and shake(). They do exactly what you think they do.Attempting to submit an empty form calls the shake() methodAfter async submission occurs (faked loading state), the close() method is called to close the popup imperatively.
```tsx
const { close, shake } = usePopoverController()
// e.g. close after form submit, shake on validation error
```

## Progress Steps
Stepper for multi-step flows like checkouts and onboarding, with horizontal or vertical layout, icons, navigation, and color tokens.
Import: import { ProgressSteps } from "@plexui/ui/components/ProgressSteps"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/progress-steps
Props:
  - current (number) — Required. Current active step (1-based)
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Layout direction
  - size ("sm" | "md" | "lg") default: "md" — Step indicator size
  - color ("default" | "success") default: "default" — Color scheme for completed/active steps
  - connectorStyle ("solid" | "dashed") default: "solid" — Connector line style
  - variant ("default" | "minimal") default: "default" — "minimal" renders a compact bar (requires total)
  - total (number) — Total steps for minimal variant
  - className (string) — Class applied to the container
  ProgressSteps.Step:
    - icon (ReactNode) — Custom icon instead of step number

### Overview
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2}>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Your details</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>Please provide your name and email</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Company details</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>A few details about your company</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Invite your team</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>Start collaborating with your team</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Add your socials</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>Share posts to your social accounts</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
</ProgressSteps>
```

### Sizes
Use size to control the scale of step indicators.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2} size="md">
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 1</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 2</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 3</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 4</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
</ProgressSteps>
```

### Vertical
Use orientation="vertical" to display steps in a vertical layout, ideal for sidebar navigation or multi-step forms. The example also shows the dashed connector style.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2} orientation="vertical">...</ProgressSteps>
<ProgressSteps current={3} orientation="vertical" connectorStyle="dashed">...</ProgressSteps>
```

### With Icons
Use icon prop on ProgressSteps.Step to display custom icons instead of step numbers.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={3}>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Email />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Globe />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Users />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Bolt />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
</ProgressSteps>
```

### With Navigation
Example of integrating with navigation controls.
```tsx
const steps = ["Your details", "Company details", "Invite your team", "Add your socials"]
const [step, setStep] = useState(1)

return (
<div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-6">
  <ProgressSteps variant="minimal" current={step} total={4} />
  <div className="text-center">
    <h3 className="text-lg font-semibold">Step {step} of 4</h3>
    <p className="text-secondary mt-1">{steps[step - 1]}</p>
  </div>
  <div className="flex gap-3">
    <Button color="secondary" variant="outline" className="w-28" disabled={step === 1} onClick={() => setStep((s) => Math.max(1, s - 1))}>
      Previous
    </Button>
    <Button color="primary" className="w-28" disabled={step === 4} onClick={() => setStep((s) => Math.min(4, s + 1))}>
      Next
    </Button>
  </div>
</div>
)
```

### Minimal
Use variant="minimal" for a compact horizontal bar indicator. Requires total prop.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps variant="minimal" current={3} total={4} color="default" />
```

### Icons Only
Omit Title and Description for a minimal indicator when step details are shown elsewhere.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2}>
<ProgressSteps.Step />
<ProgressSteps.Step />
<ProgressSteps.Step />
<ProgressSteps.Step />
</ProgressSteps>
```

### Colors
Use color to change the color scheme of completed and active steps.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={3}>...</ProgressSteps>
<ProgressSteps current={3} color="success">...</ProgressSteps>
```

## Progress
A horizontal bar that shows task completion, with determinate and indeterminate modes, labelled layouts, and smooth value transitions.
Import: import { Progress } from "@plexui/ui/components/Progress"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/progress
Props:
  - value (number | null) default: null — Current progress between 0 and max. Pass null for indeterminate.
  - max (number) default: 100 — Maximum progress value
  - getValueLabel ((value: number, max: number) => string) default: — — Accessible value text (aria-valuetext). Defaults to the rounded percentage, e.g. "67%".
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root <div>

### Overview
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(13);
useEffect(() => {
const t = setTimeout(() => setValue(66), 500);
return () => clearTimeout(t);
}, []);

return <Progress value={value} aria-label="Loading" />;
```

### With label
Pair a Label with a value readout above the bar, the typical upload / onboarding progress pattern.
```tsx
<div>
<div style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <Label id="progress-upload-label">Uploading plex-ui.zip</Label>
  <span>3.2 / 4.8 MB</span>
</div>
<Progress aria-labelledby="progress-upload-label" value={67} />
</div>
```

### Controlled
Bind value to any source. Here it follows a Slider.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(50);

return (
<>
  <Progress value={value} aria-label="Progress" />
  <Slider value={value} onChange={setValue} min={0} max={100} step={1} aria-label="Progress value" />
</>
);
```

## Radio Group
Radio group for single-choice selection with row or column layout, right-aligned indicators, rich item content, and card-style options.
Import: import { RadioGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/RadioGroup"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/radio-group
Props:
  - value (string) — Controlled selected value
  - defaultValue (string) — Initial selected value (uncontrolled)
  - onChange ((value: string) => void) — Called when selected option changes
  - direction ("col" | "row") default: "row" — Item flow direction
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the whole group
  - name (string) — Name of the hidden radio inputs submitted with the owning form
  - required (boolean) default: false — Marks the group and every hidden radio input as required
  - aria-label (string) — Accessible group label
  - className (string) — Extra classes on the group element
  RadioGroup.Item:
    - value (string) — Item value
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable this item only
    - required (boolean) — Marks this item as required
    - block (boolean) default: false — Stretch item to fill available width
    - orientation ("left" | "right") default: "left" — Position of the radio indicator relative to the label
    - description (ReactNode) — Second line below the option's label, linked via aria-describedby
    - className (string) — Extra classes on the label element

### Overview
```tsx
const [frequency, setFrequency] = useState("daily")
<RadioGroup direction="col" value={frequency} onChange={setFrequency} aria-label="Notification frequency">
<RadioGroup.Item value="daily">Daily</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="weekly">Weekly</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="never">Never</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### With Checkbox
Place RadioGroup alongside Checkbox controls to verify that indicator sizes, label baselines, and spacing align consistently in both horizontal and vertical layouts.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-6 w-full max-w-md">
<Field label="Notification channel" description="Choose how you'd like to be notified.">
  {() => (
    <RadioGroup direction="col" defaultValue="email" aria-label="Notification channel">
      <RadioGroup.Item value="email">
        <div className="flex flex-col">
          <span className="font-medium">Email</span>
          <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Messages delivered to your inbox.</span>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup.Item>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="sms">
        <div className="flex flex-col">
          <span className="font-medium">SMS</span>
          <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Text messages to your phone number.</span>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup.Item>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="push">
        <div className="flex flex-col">
          <span className="font-medium">Push</span>
          <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Real-time alerts on your device.</span>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup.Item>
    </RadioGroup>
  )}
</Field>
<Field label="Topics" description="Select the topics you want to follow.">
  {() => (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5">
      <Checkbox defaultChecked label={...} />
      ...
    </div>
  )}
</Field>
</div>
```

### Descriptions
Combine Field-level label and description with item-level descriptions for options that need additional context. Use a plain label without descriptions when the options are self-explanatory.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Notification channel" description="Choose how you'd like to be notified.">
    {() => (
      <RadioGroup direction="col" value={channel} onChange={setChannel} aria-label="Notification channel">
        <RadioGroup.Item value="email">
          <div className="flex flex-col">
            <span className="font-medium">Email</span>
            <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Messages delivered to your inbox.</span>
          </div>
        </RadioGroup.Item>
        ...
      </RadioGroup>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="Notification frequency">
    {() => (
      <RadioGroup direction="col" value={frequency} onChange={setFrequency} aria-label="Notification frequency">
        <RadioGroup.Item value="daily">Daily</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="weekly">Weekly</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="never">Never</RadioGroup.Item>
      </RadioGroup>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

### Direction
Use direction to control whether the items flow in a column or row. An optimal gap will be dynamically applied based on the orientation.
```tsx
<RadioGroup direction="col" defaultValue="light" aria-label="Theme">
<RadioGroup.Item value="light">Light</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="dark">Dark</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="system">System</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Orientation
Use orientation="right" on RadioGroup.Item to place the radio indicator after the label text. Useful for settings lists and card-style selections where the content should lead.
```tsx
<RadioGroup className="w-[320px]" direction="col" defaultValue="email" aria-label="Default notification channel">
<RadioGroup.Item value="email" orientation="right" block>Email</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="sms" orientation="right" block>SMS</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="push" orientation="right" block>Push notification</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Group disabled
Use disabled on RadioGroup to disable all radio options.
```tsx
<RadioGroup disabled defaultValue="standard" aria-label="Shipping method">
<RadioGroup.Item value="standard">Standard</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="express">Express</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="overnight">Overnight</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Item disabled
Use disabled on single RadioGroup.Item to disable only that option.
```tsx
<RadioGroup aria-label="Delivery method" direction="col">
<RadioGroup.Item value="standard">Standard shipping (3-5 days)</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="express" disabled>Express shipping (1-2 days)</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="same-day">
  Same-day delivery, available in select metro areas with a minimum order of $50
</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### With description
Use description on an item for a second line under its label. It sits outside the label, so the radio keeps the label as its name and gets the description through aria-describedby; clicking it does not select the option.
```tsx
<RadioGroup direction="col" value={value} onChange={setValue} aria-label="Spacing">
<RadioGroup.Item value="default" description="Standard spacing for most use cases.">
  Default
</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="comfortable" description="More space between elements.">
  Comfortable
</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="compact" description="Minimal spacing for dense layouts.">
  Compact
</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### With Field
Wrap a RadioGroup in a Field for a shared label and description. Spread the field props from the render prop onto the group so it is described by the Field's description (aria-describedby).
```tsx
<Field label="Notification method" description="Choose how you want to receive notifications.">
{(fieldProps) => (
  <RadioGroup direction="col" value={value} onChange={setValue} aria-label="Notification method" {...fieldProps}>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="email">Email</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="sms">SMS</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="push">Push notification</RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
)}
</Field>
```

### With Field error
When a Field has an errorMessage, it sets aria-invalid on the child control for screen readers. The error message is displayed below the group.
```tsx
<Field
label="Subscription plan"
description="Select a plan to continue."
errorMessage={showError ? "Please select a subscription plan." : undefined}
>
{(fieldProps) => (
  <RadioGroup direction="col" aria-label="Subscription plan" {...fieldProps}>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly ($9.99/month)</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="yearly">Yearly ($99.99/year)</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="lifetime">Lifetime ($299.99)</RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
)}
</Field>
```

### Choice card
Style each radio option as a bordered card with visual selection state. The selected card gets a highlighted border using design tokens. Use orientation="right" to place the indicator after the content. Wrap each RadioGroup.Item in a card container with border and borderRadius on the same element.
```tsx
<RadioGroup className="flex-col w-[320px] gap-3" value={value} onChange={setValue} aria-label="Workspace type">
<div style={{
  border: "1px solid",
  borderColor: isSelected ? "var(--color-background-primary-solid)" : "var(--color-border-primary-outline)",
  borderRadius: "var(--radius-lg)",
  backgroundColor: isSelected ? "var(--color-background-primary-soft-alpha)" : undefined,
}}>
  <RadioGroup.Item value="personal" block orientation={orientation} className="gap-3 p-3">
    <div className="flex flex-col flex-1">
      <span className="font-semibold">Personal</span>
      <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">For hobby projects and experimentation.</span>
    </div>
  </RadioGroup.Item>
</div>
...
</RadioGroup>
```

### Card selection
Leverage component composition and className overrides to build card-style radio selections with rich content per option.
```tsx
<RadioGroup className="flex-col w-[390px] gap-4">
<RadioGroup.Item className="gap-2.5" value="basic">
  <div><h4>Basic Plan</h4><p className="text-secondary text-sm">5 GB storage</p></div>
</RadioGroup.Item>
...
</RadioGroup>
```

### Grouped sections
Use dividers to separate radio groups into logical sections. Each section can be wrapped in a Field with its own label and description.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col max-w-sm w-full divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Visibility" description="Control who can see project resources.">
    {() => (
      <RadioGroup direction="col" value={visibility} onChange={setVisibility} aria-label="Visibility">
        <RadioGroup.Item value="hidden">Hidden</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="owners">Visible to organization owners</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="everyone">Visible to everyone</RadioGroup.Item>
      </RadioGroup>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="Digest frequency" description="How often you receive summary emails.">
    {() => (
      <RadioGroup direction="col" value={frequency} onChange={setFrequency} aria-label="Digest frequency">
        <RadioGroup.Item value="daily">Daily</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="weekly">Weekly</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="never">Never</RadioGroup.Item>
      </RadioGroup>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

## Select Control
Select control primitive for building custom dropdowns, with variants, sizing, start and dropdown icons, and clearable, loading, and invalid states.
Import: import { SelectControl } from "@plexui/ui/components/SelectControl"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/select-control
Props:
  - selected (boolean) default: false — Whether a value is selected (affects placeholder styling)
  - variant ("soft" | "outline" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Visual variant
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Control size (3xs to 3xl)
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded trigger
  - StartIcon (ComponentType) — Icon at start
  - onClearClick (() => void) — Enables the clear button when set
  - onInteract (() => void) — Called on pointer down, ArrowDown, ArrowUp and Space. Without it, a wrapping trigger opens on pointer down
  - dropdownIconType ("chevronDown" | "dropdown" | "none") default: "dropdown" — Dropdown indicator style
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid state
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable control
  - block (boolean) default: false — Full width
  - loading (boolean) default: false — Loading state (aria-busy); hides the indicators and ignores interaction
  - opticallyAlign ("start" | "end") — Optical alignment
  - className (string) — Applied to the control

### Overview
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("")
const placeholder = "Select date..."

return (
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger>
    <SelectControl className="w-[200px]" selected={!!value} onClearClick={() => setValue("")} StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>
      {value || placeholder}
    </SelectControl>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Content minWidth={200} width={200}>
    <Menu.RadioGroup value={value} onChange={setValue}>
      <Menu.RadioItem value="Today">Today</Menu.RadioItem>
      <Menu.RadioItem value="Last week">Last week</Menu.RadioItem>
      <Menu.RadioItem value="Last month">Last month</Menu.RadioItem>
      <Menu.RadioItem value="Last 3 months">Last 3 months</Menu.RadioItem>
    </Menu.RadioGroup>
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
)
```

### Variants
Use the variant prop to stylize the select control. Available variant styles are similar to {""}, but aligned with subtle differences from {""} variant treatments.
```tsx
<SelectControl variant="soft" selected StartIcon={Cabinet} onClearClick={() => {}}>Sample value</SelectControl>
<SelectControl variant="outline" selected StartIcon={Cabinet} onClearClick={() => {}}>Sample value</SelectControl>
<SelectControl variant="ghost" selected StartIcon={Cabinet} onClearClick={() => {}}>Sample value</SelectControl>
```

### Sizing & roundness
Sizing of the control is determined with the size prop. Each size provides dynamic values for various aspects of the control, including icon and indicator placement, as well font-size and gutter values.Create fully rounded controls with the pill prop. When pill is set, extra horizontal gutter is dynamically applied, and the clear action is also set to pill.
```tsx
<SelectControl size="md" pill={false} dropdownIconType="none">Select...</SelectControl>
<SelectControl size="md" loading>Select...</SelectControl>
<SelectControl size="md">Select...</SelectControl>
<SelectControl size="md" StartIcon={Tools} dropdownIconType="none">Tool calls</SelectControl>
...
```

### Selected
Use selected to indicate if the control has a selected value, which toggles visual placeholder styling.As you'll notice here, this doesn't do anything to the content of the control. That's up to you.
```tsx
<SelectControl selected={false}>Select...</SelectControl>
```

### Start icon
Use StartIcon to display an icon in the control. Sizing, spacing, and coloring are handled automatically.
```tsx
<SelectControl StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>Select date...</SelectControl>
```

### Dropdown icon
Use dropdownIconType to control the presentation of the dropdown indicator.
```tsx
<SelectControl selected dropdownIconType="dropdown" StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>Select date...</SelectControl>
```

### Clearable
Pass a callback onClearClick to enable the clearable action.
```tsx
<SelectControl selected onClearClick={() => setValue("")} StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>
{value || "Select..."}
</SelectControl>
```

### Loading
During loading, the dropdown icon and clear action are automatically hidden, the control is marked aria-busy, and it ignores pointer and keyboard interaction. Use disabled to add visual disablement.
```tsx
<SelectControl selected loading StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>Loading...</SelectControl>
```

### Invalid
Use invalid to visually indicate the control is in an invalid state.
```tsx
<SelectControl invalid selected>Pineapple on pizza</SelectControl>
```

### Disabled
Use disabled to both visually and accessibly disable the control.
```tsx
<SelectControl disabled selected StartIcon={User}>Reader</SelectControl>
```

### Block
Create full-width controls with the block prop.
```tsx
<div className="w-[290px] text-center p-2 border border-dashed border-alpha/20 rounded-md">
<SelectControl block size="lg" StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>Select...</SelectControl>
</div>
```

### Country selector
A plain country selector built with Select. Shows flag icons with country names, no dial codes. Useful for profile forms, shipping addresses, and other country-only fields. The search box appears on its own because the list has more than 15 options; there is no prop for it.
```tsx
const countries = [
{ value: "us", label: "United States" },
{ value: "gb", label: "United Kingdom" },
// ...60 countries
];

const CountryView = ({ value, label }: Option) => (
<span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
  <img src={`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lipis/flag-icons@7.5.0/flags/4x3/${value}.svg`} alt="" width={20} />
  {label}
</span>
);

<Select
value={country}
options={countries}
onChange={(option) => setCountry(option.value)}
placeholder="Select country..."
size="lg"
block
searchPlaceholder="Search countries..."
TriggerView={CountryView}
OptionView={CountryView}
listMinWidth={300}
/>
```

### Country code selector
A searchable country selector built with Select. Custom TriggerView and OptionView render flag icons and dial codes. Search matches both country name and dial code.
```tsx
const countries = [
{ value: "us", label: "United States (+1)", dialCode: "+1" },
{ value: "gb", label: "United Kingdom (+44)", dialCode: "+44" },
// ...60 countries
];

const CountryTriggerView = ({ value }) => {
const country = lookup.get(value);
return (
  <span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
    <img src={`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lipis/flag-icons@7.5.0/flags/4x3/${value}.svg`} alt="" width={20} />
    {country.label} ({country.dialCode})
  </span>
);
};

<Select
value={country}
options={countries}
onChange={(option) => setCountry(option.value)}
placeholder="Select country..."
size="lg"
block
searchPredicate={searchPredicate}
TriggerView={CountryTriggerView}
listMinWidth={300}
/>
```

### Phone form
Country selector with flag icons and phone input composed into a form. Selecting a country updates the dial code prefix and clears the phone field. Phone numbers are formatted as you type using per-country patterns (e.g. 123 456 7890 for US, 1234 567 890 for UK). Search works by both country name and dial code. Validation runs on submit: the phone field shows an error state with FieldError when the number is too short or too long.
```tsx
import { useState, useCallback, useRef } from 'react';
import { Input } from '@plexui/ui/components/Input';
import { Select, type Option } from '@plexui/ui/components/Select';
import { Button } from '@plexui/ui/components/Button';
import { FieldError } from '@plexui/ui/components/FieldError';

// Country data: include all 245 countries in production
type Country = { value: string; label: string; dialCode: string; flag: string };

const COUNTRIES: Country[] = [
{ value: 'us', label: 'United States', dialCode: '+1', flag: '🇺🇸' },
{ value: 'gb', label: 'United Kingdom', dialCode: '+44', flag: '🇬🇧' },
{ value: 'de', label: 'Germany', dialCode: '+49', flag: '🇩🇪' },
{ value: 'fr', label: 'France', dialCode: '+33', flag: '🇫🇷' },
{ value: 'es', label: 'Spain', dialCode: '+34', flag: '🇪🇸' },
{ value: 'it', label: 'Italy', dialCode: '+39', flag: '🇮🇹' },
{ value: 'jp', label: 'Japan', dialCode: '+81', flag: '🇯🇵' },
{ value: 'au', label: 'Australia', dialCode: '+61', flag: '🇦🇺' },
{ value: 'br', label: 'Brazil', dialCode: '+55', flag: '🇧🇷' },
{ value: 'in', label: 'India', dialCode: '+91', flag: '🇮🇳' },
// ... full list of 245 countries
];

const COUNTRY_LOOKUP = new Map(COUNTRIES.map((c) => [c.value, c]));
const COUNTRY_OPTIONS = COUNTRIES.map((c) => ({
...c,
label: `${c.label} (${c.dialCode})`,
}));

// Per-country phone number format patterns
const PHONE_FORMATS: Record<string, number[]> = {
us: [3, 3, 4], ca: [3, 3, 4],   // 123 456 7890
gb: [4, 3, 3], de: [3, 4, 4],   // 1234 567 890 | 123 4567 8901
fr: [1, 2, 2, 2, 2],            // 1 23 45 67 89
es: [3, 2, 2, 2],               // 123 45 67 89
it: [3, 3, 4], jp: [2, 4, 4],
au: [3, 3, 3], br: [2, 5, 4],
in: [5, 5],                      // 12345 67890
// ... add more countries as needed
};

function formatPhoneNumber(raw: string, countryCode?: string) {
const digits = raw.replace(/\D/g, '');
if (!digits) return '';
const format = (countryCode && PHONE_FORMATS[countryCode]) || [3, 3, 4];
const groups: string[] = [];
let i = 0;
for (const size of format) {
  if (i >= digits.length) break;
  groups.push(digits.slice(i, i + size));
  i += size;
}
if (i < digits.length) groups.push(digits.slice(i));
return groups.join(' ');
}

// Flag icon: SVG flags from lipis/flag-icons, all 4:3
function FlagIcon({ code, trigger }: { code: string; trigger?: boolean }) {
return (
  <span
    style={{
      display: 'block',
      height: trigger ? 'var(--start-icon-size, 18px)' : 16,
      aspectRatio: '4 / 3',
      borderRadius: 2,
      overflow: 'hidden',
      flexShrink: 0,
    }}
  >
    <img
      src={`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lipis/flag-icons@7.5.0/flags/4x3/${code}.svg`}
      alt=""
      loading="lazy"
      style={{
        display: 'block',
        width: '100%',
        height: '100%',
      }}
    />
  </span>
);
}

// Custom trigger and option renderers
const CountryTriggerView = ({ value }: Option) => {
const country = COUNTRY_LOOKUP.get(value);
if (!country) return null;
return (
  <span style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, height: '100%' }}>
    <FlagIcon code={value} trigger />
    {country.label} ({country.dialCode})
  </span>
);
};

const CountryOptionView = ({ value, label }: Option) => (
<span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
  <FlagIcon code={value} />
  {label}
</span>
);

// Search matches country name or dial code
const searchPredicate = (option: Option, term: string) => {
const country = COUNTRY_LOOKUP.get(option.value);
if (!country) return false;
return (
  country.label.toLowerCase().includes(term) ||
  country.dialCode.includes(term)
);
};

function PhoneForm() {
const [country, setCountry] = useState('us');
const [phone, setPhone] = useState('');
const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState(false);
const phoneRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);

const dialCode = COUNTRY_LOOKUP.get(country)?.dialCode ?? '+1';
const digits = phone.replace(/\D/g, '');
const isValid = digits.length >= 7 && digits.length <= 15;
const showError = submitted && !isValid;

const handleCountryChange = useCallback((option: Option) => {
  setCountry(option.value);
  setPhone('');
  setSubmitted(false);
  setTimeout(() => phoneRef.current?.focus(), 0);
}, []);

const handlePhoneChange = useCallback(
  (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    setPhone(formatPhoneNumber(e.target.value.replace(/\D/g, ''), country));
    setSubmitted(false);
  },
  [country]
);

return (
  <form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setSubmitted(true); }} noValidate>
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <Select
        value={country}
        options={COUNTRY_OPTIONS}
        onChange={handleCountryChange}
        placeholder="Select country..."
        size="lg"
        block
        searchPlaceholder="Search countries..."
        searchPredicate={searchPredicate}
        TriggerView={CountryTriggerView}
        OptionView={CountryOptionView}
        listMinWidth={300}
      />
      <div>
        <Input
          ref={phoneRef}
          value={phone}
          onChange={handlePhoneChange}
          placeholder="Phone number"
          type="tel"
          inputMode="tel"
          size="lg"
          invalid={showError}
          startAdornment={
            <span className="text-tertiary whitespace-nowrap select-none">
              {dialCode}
            </span>
          }
        />
        {showError && (
          <FieldError className="mt-1.5">Phone number is not valid.</FieldError>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
    <Button type="submit" color="primary" variant="solid" size="lg" className="w-full mt-3">
      Continue
    </Button>
  </form>
);
}
```

### Optical alignment
Use opticallyAlign with either "start" or "end" to offset the gutter of the control.
```tsx
<SelectControl selected variant="ghost" opticallyAlign="start">Ghost control</SelectControl>
```

## Select
Select dropdown with grouped options, per-item descriptions, multiple selection, action items, and column-based layouts.
Import: import { Select } from "@plexui/ui/components/Select"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/select
Props:
  - options (Options<T>) — Array of options or grouped options
  - value (string | string[]) — Selected value (single) or values (multiple)
  - onChange ((option: T) => void | (options: T[]) => void) — Called when selection changes, with the selected option (or options with multiple)
  - multiple (boolean) default: false — Allow multiple selection
  - placeholder (string) default: "Select..." — Trigger placeholder
  - variant ("soft" | "outline" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Trigger variant
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Trigger size (3xs to 3xl)
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Rounded trigger
  - clearable (boolean) default: false — Show clear button
  - block (boolean) default: variant !== "ghost" — Full width trigger
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable select. A disabled select is not submitted or validated with its form
  - loading (boolean) default: false — Loading state; shows loadingPlaceholder and keeps the menu closed
  - loadingPlaceholder (string) default: "Loading..." — Trigger text while loading
  - name (string) — Name of the hidden form input. With multiple, every selected value is submitted
  - required (boolean) — Required for native form validation
  - id (string) — Id of the hidden form input
  - actions (array) — Actions below options list
  - checkPosition ("start" | "end" | "none") default: "start" — Where the check indicator sits in the list. "none" removes the indicator column for lists that never carry a selection
  - OptionView (React.FC) — Custom option render
  - TriggerView (React.FC) — Custom trigger render: the selected option, or { values, selectedAll } with multiple
  - TriggerStartIcon (ComponentType) — Icon at the start of the trigger
  - trigger (({ open, onToggle }) => ReactNode) — Custom trigger element, wrapped as the popover trigger
  - dropdownIconType ("chevronDown" | "dropdown" | "none") default: "dropdown" — Indicator at the end of the trigger
  - side ("top" | "bottom") default: "bottom" — Preferred side of the list
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" when block, otherwise "start" — Alignment of the list against the trigger
  - listWidth (number | "auto") default: "auto" — Width of the list in px
  - listMinWidth (number | "auto") default: trigger width (300 when not block) — Minimum width of the list in px
  - listMaxWidth (number | "auto") default: "auto" — Maximum width of the list in px
  - searchPlaceholder (string) — Search input placeholder
  - searchAriaLabel (string) default: "Search options" — Accessible name of the search input, independent of the trigger label
  - searchEmptyMessage (ReactNode) default: "No results found." — Shown when the search matches nothing
  - searchSize (ControlSize) default: "md" — Size of the search input in the menu, such as 2xl for 44px touch targets on phones
  - searchPredicate ((option, term) => boolean) — Filters options while searching
  - aria-label / aria-labelledby (string) — Accessible name of the trigger and the list

### Overview
```tsx
const [fruit, setFruit] = useState("")

<Select
value={fruit}
options={fruits}
onChange={({ value }) => setFruit(value)}
placeholder="Select a fruit..."
name="fruits"
variant="outline"
size="md"
/>
```

### With descriptions
Options carrying a description field render a secondary line under each label. The title stays semibold in every state (idle, highlighted, selected). The component handles that automatically, no optionClassName needed. Use TriggerStartIcon to reflect the selected option's identity in the trigger.
```tsx
const RoleOptionDescription = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => (
<div className="font-normal text-secondary text-[0.935em] leading-[1.45]">
  {children}
</div>
);

const roles = [
{
  value: "owner",
  label: "Owner",
  description: (
    <RoleOptionDescription>
      Can modify project information and manage project members
    </RoleOptionDescription>
  ),
},
{
  value: "reader",
  label: "Reader",
  description: (
    <RoleOptionDescription>
      Can make API requests that read or modify data
    </RoleOptionDescription>
  ),
},
];

<Select
value={role}
options={roles}
placeholder="Select role..."
align="start"
listMinWidth={260}
variant="outline"
size="md"
onChange={({ value }) => setRole(value)}
TriggerStartIcon={role === "owner" ? UserLock : User}
/>
```

### Actions
Custom, arbitrary actions can be displayed below the options list via the actions prop.
```tsx
<Select
value={value}
onChange={handleChange}
options={items}
placeholder="Select..."
align="start"
listMinWidth={240}
actions={[
  { id: "create", label: "Create project", Icon: Plus, onSelect: () => {} },
  { id: "overview", label: "Organization overview", Icon: Workspace, onSelect: () => {} },
]}
/>
```

### Grouped options
Select supports option groups, similar to the native &lt;optgroup&gt; element. Each group is announced as a group named by its label. All selects are searchable by default, but will only present a searchbox when it makes sense. Currently, this means when there are more than 15 options.
```tsx
<Select
value={value}
options={groupedItems}
onChange={(v) => setValue(v.value)}
variant="outline"
size="lg"
side="bottom"
listMinWidth={300}
searchPlaceholder="Select an option..."
clearable
/>
```

### Multiple selection
Multiple selection is supported through the multiple property. This changes how value, onChange, and TriggerView are typed, accepting and returning arrays of values.
```tsx
<Select
variant="soft"
placeholder="Select fruits..."
options={fruitsOptions}
name="fruits"
multiple
clearable
value={fruits}
onChange={(values) => setFruits(values.map(({ value }) => value))}
TriggerView={MultiFruitTriggerView}
/>
```

### Column configuration
A column-visibility panel built with Popover and Switch. Toggling a switch moves the column between shown and hidden groups.
```tsx
const [shown, setShown] = useState(["name", "email", "role", "status"])
const toggle = (id: string) => {
setShown((prev) =>
  prev.includes(id) ? prev.filter((c) => c !== id) : [...prev, id]
)
}
const shownColumns = allColumns.filter((c) => shown.includes(c.id))
const hiddenColumns = allColumns.filter((c) => !shown.includes(c.id))

return (
<Popover>
  <Popover.Trigger>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="outline" size="sm">
      <SettingsSlider width={15} height={15} /> Columns
    </Button>
  </Popover.Trigger>
  <Popover.Content minWidth={240} side="bottom" align="start">
    <div className="py-1.5">
      {shownColumns.map((col) => (
        <div
          key={col.id}
          className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4 px-3 py-1.5 cursor-pointer hover:bg-alpha/5"
          onClick={() => toggle(col.id)}
        >
          <span className="text-sm">{col.label}</span>
          <Switch checked aria-label={col.label} />
        </div>
      ))}
      {hiddenColumns.map((col) => (
        <div
          key={col.id}
          className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4 px-3 py-1.5 cursor-pointer hover:bg-alpha/5"
          onClick={() => toggle(col.id)}
        >
          <span className="text-sm text-tertiary">{col.label}</span>
          <Switch checked={false} aria-label={col.label} />
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  </Popover.Content>
</Popover>
)
```

## Separator
A thin divider between content, horizontal or vertical, decorative by default or exposed to assistive technology when it marks a real grouping.
Import: import { Separator } from "@plexui/ui/components/Separator"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/separator
Props:
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Direction of the divider
  - decorative (boolean) default: true — When true, the separator is ignored by assistive technologies. Set false when the divider carries semantic grouping (renders role="separator").
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root <div>

### Overview
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 16, maxWidth: 384 }}>
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Aisha Cooper</div>
  <div className="text-tertiary">Engineering · Platform team</div>
</div>
<Separator />
<div>Shipped 24 pull requests this week across CI/CD and developer tooling.</div>
</div>
```

### Vertical
Use orientation="vertical" between inline items. Works for meta-strips, breadcrumbs, and dot-less separators.
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', height: 20, alignItems: 'center', gap: 16 }}>
<div>MIT license</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>12k weekly downloads</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>48 kB bundle</div>
</div>
```

### Menu
Vertical separators between menu items with a short caption underneath each label.
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 16 }}>
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Starter</div>
  <div className="text-tertiary">Free · 1 project</div>
</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Pro</div>
  <div className="text-tertiary">$19/mo · Unlimited</div>
</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Enterprise</div>
  <div className="text-tertiary">Custom · Priority SLA</div>
</div>
</div>
```

### List
Horizontal separators between rows in a definition list.
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 8, maxWidth: 384 }}>
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>Version</dt><dd>0.9.0</dd>
</dl>
<Separator />
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>Published</dt><dd>2 days ago</dd>
</dl>
<Separator />
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>Bundle</dt><dd>48 kB</dd>
</dl>
<Separator />
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>License</dt><dd>MIT</dd>
</dl>
</div>
```

## Shimmer Text
Text with a shimmer animation for loading and in-progress states, always on or toggled with a graceful stop.
Import: import { ShimmerText, ShimmerableText } from "@plexui/ui/components/ShimmerText"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/shimmer-text
Props:
  - as ("p" | "span" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "h5" | "h6" | "div") default: "div" — HTML element to render
  - children (ReactNode) — Text content to shimmer
  - className (string) — Additional CSS classes
  ShimmerableText:
    - as ("p" | "span" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "h5" | "h6" | "div") default: "div" — HTML element to render
    - shimmer (boolean) default: false — Whether the shimmer animation is active
    - children (ReactNode) — Text content to shimmer
    - className (string) — Additional CSS classes

### Overview
ShimmerText applies a continuous shimmer animation to text content. Useful for loading states, AI-generated content indicators, or visual emphasis.
