```tsx
<ShimmerText className="text-lg font-semibold">
Thinking...
</ShimmerText>
```

### Semantic elements
Use the as prop to render as any text element: p, span, h1 to h6, or div.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
<ShimmerText as="h2" className="text-2xl font-bold">Heading shimmer</ShimmerText>
<ShimmerText as="p" className="text-base">Paragraph shimmer effect</ShimmerText>
<ShimmerText as="span" className="text-sm text-secondary">Inline shimmer</ShimmerText>
</div>
```

### Controllable shimmer
ShimmerableText allows toggling the shimmer on and off. When shimmer is set to false, the animation finishes its current iteration and then pauses gracefully, with no abrupt cut. Use this variant when text transitions between a loading and idle state.
```tsx
const [shimmer, setShimmer] = useState(true)

<ShimmerableText shimmer={shimmer} className="text-lg font-semibold">
Generating response...
</ShimmerableText>
```

## Sidebar
Composable navigation sidebar for app shells with collapsible sections, search and filter, tree views with hover actions, and a mobile menu
Import: import { SidebarProvider, SidebarLayout, Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarInset, SidebarTrigger } from "@plexui/ui/components/Sidebar"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/sidebar
Props:
  - variant ("sidebar" | "docs") default: "sidebar" — Visual variant
  - side ("left" | "right") default: "left" — Which side the sidebar is on
  SidebarProvider:
    - collapsible ("offcanvas" | "icon" | "none") default: "offcanvas" — Collapse behavior: offcanvas (drawer on mobile, full collapse on desktop), icon (icon rail), or none
    - defaultOpen (boolean) default: true — Initial open state (uncontrolled)
    - open (boolean) — Controlled open state
    - onOpenChange ((open: boolean) => void) — Called when open state changes. Without open the provider keeps its own state and still calls it
    - className (string) — Class of the provider's wrapper
    - style (CSSProperties) — Style of the provider's wrapper, e.g. --sidebar-width
  SidebarGroup:
    - defaultOpen (boolean) default: true — Whether the group is open initially. A closed group hides its SidebarGroupContent
    - open (boolean) — Controlled open state, also exposed as data-state. The group has no toggle of its own: change open from your own control
  SidebarGroupLabel:
    - size ("sm" | "lg") default: "lg" — sm: compact, tertiary. lg: larger, primary, more spacing
    - asChild (boolean) default: false — Render the single child element as the label
  SidebarMenuItem:
    - expanded (boolean) — Marks the item expanded, which turns its SidebarMenuChevron. Pair it with open on its SidebarMenuSub
  SidebarMenuButton:
    - isActive (boolean) default: false — Highlight the current page (aria-current="page")
    - tooltip (string | ReactNode) — Label shown on hover when collapsed (icon mode). Hidden on mobile.
    - asChild (boolean) default: false — Render the single child element (e.g. a router link) as the button. The button attributes go on the child and its content is wrapped like the button's
  SidebarMenuSub:
    - open (boolean) default: true — Whether submenu is expanded. A closed submenu is inert, so its links and buttons leave the tab order and the accessibility tree
    - hasIcons (boolean) default: false — Align child items with parent text that has icons
  SidebarMenuSubButton:
    - isActive (boolean) default: false — Highlight the current page (aria-current="page")
    - indent (0 | 1 | 2 | 3) default: 0 — Nesting level; each level adds 12px of left margin
    - asChild (boolean) default: false — Render the single child element (e.g. a router link) as the button
  SidebarCard:
    - variant ("default" | "elevated") default: "default" — Visual variant
    - dismissible (boolean) default: false — Shows dismiss button
    - onDismiss (() => void) — Callback when dismissed

### App Shell
A multi-section app shell with a workspace selector, expandable parent sections with sub-items, and a footer with a documentation link plus a user menu. When collapsed (icon mode), hovering a parent icon opens a Popover flyout listing the section&apos;s items so users keep one-click access without expanding the rail.
```tsx
<SidebarProvider collapsible="icon">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 600 }}>
  <Sidebar>
    <SidebarHeader>
      <span>Console</span>
      <SidebarTrigger />
    </SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarContent>
      {/* Workspace selector */}
      <SidebarMenuItem>
        <Menu>
          <Menu.Trigger>
            <SidebarMenuButton tooltip="Default workspace">
              <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><Cube /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
              <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Default</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
              <ChevronUpDown className="ml-auto" />
            </SidebarMenuButton>
          </Menu.Trigger>
          <Menu.Content>...</Menu.Content>
        </Menu>
      </SidebarMenuItem>

      {/* Parent section: hover flyout when collapsed */}
      {state === "collapsed" ? (
        <Popover showOnHover>
          <Popover.Trigger>
            <SidebarMenuButton>
              <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><SettingsWrench /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
              <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Build</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
              <SidebarMenuChevron />
            </SidebarMenuButton>
          </Popover.Trigger>
          <Popover.Content side="right" minWidth={220}>
            <div>Build / Workbench / Files / Skills / Batches</div>
          </Popover.Content>
        </Popover>
      ) : (
        <SidebarMenuItem expanded={isExpanded}>
          <SidebarMenuButton onClick={toggle}>
            <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><SettingsWrench /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
            <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Build</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
            <SidebarMenuChevron />
          </SidebarMenuButton>
          <SidebarMenuSub open={isExpanded} hasIcons>
            <SidebarMenuSubButton indent={1}>Workbench</SidebarMenuSubButton>
            ...
          </SidebarMenuSub>
        </SidebarMenuItem>
      )}
    </SidebarContent>
    <SidebarFooter>
      <SidebarMenuButton><Book /> Documentation</SidebarMenuButton>
      <Menu>
        <Menu.Trigger>
          <SidebarMenuButton>
            <Avatar name="Alex" />
            <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Alex · Admin</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
          </SidebarMenuButton>
        </Menu.Trigger>
        <Menu.Content>...</Menu.Content>
      </Menu>
    </SidebarFooter>
  </Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
</SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>
```

### Basic
```tsx
<SidebarProvider collapsible="icon">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 500 }}>
  <Sidebar>
    <SidebarHeader>
      <span>App</span>
      <SidebarTrigger />
    </SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarContent>
      <SidebarGroup>
        <SidebarGroupLabel size="sm">Project</SidebarGroupLabel>
        <SidebarGroupContent>
          <SidebarMenu>
            <SidebarMenuItem>
              <SidebarMenuButton isActive tooltip="Overview">
                <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><Home /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
                <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Overview</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
                <SidebarMenuBadge><Badge size="sm" color="info">3</Badge></SidebarMenuBadge>
              </SidebarMenuButton>
            </SidebarMenuItem>
            ...
          </SidebarMenu>
        </SidebarGroupContent>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarContent>
  </Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
</SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>
```

### Collapsible Sections
Build collapsible nested menus with chevron toggles for documentation and API reference sidebars. A parent is a SidebarMenuItem whose SidebarMenuSub holds the next level; expanded on the item turns its SidebarMenuChevron and open on the submenu shows it.
```tsx
const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState<string[]>([]);
const toggle = (id: string) =>
setExpanded((prev) => (prev.includes(id) ? prev.filter((i) => i !== id) : [...prev, id]));

return (
<SidebarProvider collapsible="none">
  <SidebarLayout style={{ height: 500 }}>
    <Sidebar variant="docs">
      <SidebarContent>
        <SidebarGroup>
          <SidebarGroupLabel>API Reference</SidebarGroupLabel>
          <SidebarGroupContent>
            <SidebarMenu>
              <SidebarMenuItem expanded={expanded.includes("responses")}>
                <SidebarMenuSubButton onClick={() => toggle("responses")}>
                  Responses
                  <SidebarMenuChevron />
                </SidebarMenuSubButton>
                <SidebarMenuSub open={expanded.includes("responses")}>
                  <SidebarMenuSubItem>
                    <SidebarMenuSubButton indent={1} isActive>Create</SidebarMenuSubButton>
                  </SidebarMenuSubItem>
                  ...
                </SidebarMenuSub>
              </SidebarMenuItem>
              ...
            </SidebarMenu>
          </SidebarGroupContent>
        </SidebarGroup>
      </SidebarContent>
    </Sidebar>
    <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
  </SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>
);
```

### Search and Filter
Combine search and type-based filtering with nested tree navigation. Each item has an icon based on its type. A Menu with checkbox items filters items by type.
```tsx
<SidebarProvider collapsible="none">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 650 }}>
  <Sidebar>
    <SidebarHeader>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2 w-full">
        <div className="flex-1">
          <SidebarInput
            variant="soft"
            placeholder="Search"
            value={search}
            onChange={(e) => setSearch(e.target.value)}
            onClear={() => setSearch("")}
          />
        </div>
        <Menu>
          <Menu.Trigger>
            <Button variant="soft" color="secondary" uniform aria-label="Filter by type">
              {typeFilters.length > 0 ? <FilterBadge /> : <Filter />}
            </Button>
          </Menu.Trigger>
          <Menu.Content minWidth="auto" align="end">
            {stepFilterOptions.map((option) => (
              <Menu.CheckboxItem
                key={option.value}
                checked={typeFilters.includes(option.value)}
                indicatorPosition="end"
                indicatorVariant="ghost"
                onCheckedChange={(checked) =>
                  setTypeFilters((prev) =>
                    checked ? [...prev, option.value] : prev.filter((v) => v !== option.value),
                  )
                }
                onSelect={(event) => event.preventDefault()}
              >
                {option.label}
              </Menu.CheckboxItem>
            ))}
          </Menu.Content>
        </Menu>
      </div>
    </SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarContent>
      <SidebarGroup>
        <SidebarGroupContent>
          <SidebarMenu>
            <SidebarMenuItem>
              <SidebarMenuButton isActive>
                <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><Desktop /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
                <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Start</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
              </SidebarMenuButton>
            </SidebarMenuItem>
            ...
          </SidebarMenu>
        </SidebarGroupContent>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarContent>
  </Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
</SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>
```

### Tree with Hover Actions
Tree navigation with chevrons on the left and actions on the right. Clicking a row selects the item and its chevron toggles expand/collapse. On hover, a row shows a + menu (top-level rows and nested groups) and nested rows show a drag handle for reordering. The actions sit next to the row button, not inside it, so no button is nested in another.
```tsx
<SidebarMenuItem expanded={isExpanded}>
<div className="group/row relative">
  <SidebarMenuButton isActive={activeItem === id} onClick={() => setActiveItem(id)}>
    <span
      role="none"
      className="transition-transform"
      style={{ transform: isExpanded ? "rotate(0deg)" : "rotate(-90deg)" }}
      onClick={(e) => {
        e.stopPropagation();
        toggleExpanded(id);
      }}
    >
      <ChevronDownMd />
    </span>
    <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><Icon /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
    <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Label</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
  </SidebarMenuButton>
  {/* A sibling of the row button, shown on hover */}
  <span className="absolute right-1 top-0 bottom-0 flex items-center opacity-0 pointer-events-none group-hover/row:opacity-100 group-hover/row:pointer-events-auto">
    <Menu>
      <Menu.Trigger>
        <Button variant="ghost" color="secondary" size="xs" uniform aria-label="Add">
          <Plus />
        </Button>
      </Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Content minWidth="auto" align="end">...</Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </span>
</div>
<SidebarMenuSub open={isExpanded} hasIcons>...</SidebarMenuSub>
</SidebarMenuItem>
```

### Mobile Menu
Mobile behavior is handled automatically when using SidebarProvider. The SidebarMobileMenuButton provides a standard animated hamburger trigger.
```tsx
// Desktop: standard sidebar with icon collapse
<SidebarProvider collapsible="icon">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 500 }}>
  <Sidebar>...</Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
</SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>

// Mobile: phone-sized container with hamburger menu
<SidebarProvider collapsible="offcanvas">
<header>
  <SidebarMobileMenuButton />
</header>
{openMobile ? <SidebarContent>...</SidebarContent> : <div>Page content</div>}
</SidebarProvider>
```

### Search Input
The sidebar provides a dedicated SidebarInput component for search functionality. It forwards everything to Input, so control it with value and onChange and clear it with onClear.
```tsx
<SidebarProvider collapsible="none">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 500 }}>
  <Sidebar variant="docs">
    <SidebarHeader>
      <SidebarInput
        variant="soft"
        placeholder="Search"
        value={searchValue}
        onChange={(e) => setSearchValue(e.target.value)}
        onClear={() => setSearchValue("")}
      />
    </SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarContent>
      <SidebarGroup>
        <SidebarGroupLabel>Get started</SidebarGroupLabel>
        <SidebarGroupContent>
          <SidebarMenu>
            <SidebarMenuItem>
              <SidebarMenuSubButton indent={0} isActive>Overview</SidebarMenuSubButton>
            </SidebarMenuItem>
            ...
          </SidebarMenu>
        </SidebarGroupContent>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarContent>
  </Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
</SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>
```

## Skeleton
Loading placeholders that match the shape of the content they stand in for, from avatars and text to cards, forms, and tables.
Import: import { Skeleton } from "@plexui/ui/components/Skeleton"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/skeleton
Props:
  - circle (boolean) default: false — Render a circular skeleton
  - className (string) — Set dimensions and custom styling

### Overview
Use a circular skeleton to represent loading avatars, combined with text placeholders.
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
<Skeleton circle className="size-12" />
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[200px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[150px]" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Card
Compose multiple skeletons to represent loading cards with images and text content.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 w-[300px] p-4 border border-default rounded-xl">
<Skeleton className="h-[150px] w-full rounded-lg" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-3/4" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/2" />
</div>
```

### Text
Multiple text lines with varying widths create natural-looking paragraph placeholders.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 w-[300px]">
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-4/5" />
</div>
```

### Form
Form skeletons use Plex UI control sizing (32px height for inputs and buttons).
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4 w-[300px]">
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[80px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-8 w-full rounded-lg" />
</div>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[100px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-8 w-full rounded-lg" />
</div>
<Skeleton className="h-8 w-[120px] rounded-lg" />
</div>
```

### Table
Table skeletons show header and row structure while data loads.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 w-[400px]">
<div className="flex gap-4 pb-2 border-b border-default">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[100px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[150px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[80px]" />
</div>
{Array.from({ length: 4 }).map((_, i) => (
  <div key={i} className="flex gap-4 py-2">
    <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[100px]" />
    <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[150px]" />
    <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[80px]" />
  </div>
))}
</div>
```

## Slider
Slider for fine-tuning numeric values with single or range thumbs, marks, an editable value input, and vertical orientation.
Import: import { Slider } from "@plexui/ui/components/Slider"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/slider
Props:
  - value (number | number[]) — Required. Current value; array when range is true
  - min (number) — Required. Minimum value
  - max (number) — Required. Maximum value
  - step (number) — Required. Step increment
  - range (boolean) default: false — Enable multi-thumb range mode
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Layout direction of the slider
  - resetValue (number) — Value for reset option (single mode only)
  - resetTooltip (string) default: "Reset to default" — Tooltip and accessible name of the reset button
  - unit (string) — Unit displayed (e.g. ms, px)
  - prefixUnit (string) — Unit displayed before the value (e.g. $)
  - label (ReactNode) — Label (string or JSX). Also names the slider thumbs for assistive technology
  - aria-label (string) — Accessible name when there is no visible label. Range thumbs add Minimum / Maximum (or Value n of m)
  - aria-labelledby (string) — Id of an element that names the slider; takes precedence over label
  - marks (Array<{ value: number, label: string }>) — Marks below track (horizontal only)
  - onChange ((value: number | number[]) => void) — Required. Change handler; receives array when range is true
  - minStepsBetweenThumbs (number) — Minimum steps between thumbs (range mode only)
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable slider
  - trackColor (string) — Color of the slider track
  - rangeColor (string) — Color of the filled range
  - className (string) — Applied to the root element
  - onFocus ((event: FocusEvent) => void) — Called when the value input or a thumb gains focus
  - onBlur ((event: FocusEvent) => void) — Called when the value input or a thumb loses focus

### Overview
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(1000)
<Slider
label="Example field"
min={0}
max={2000}
resetValue={1000}
step={10}
unit="ms"
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
/>
```

### Adding a tooltip
A tooltip can easily be added to the Slider label by providing JSX instead of a simple string.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(1000)

return (
<Slider
  label={
    <Tooltip content="More details about this field">
      <Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>Example field</Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>
    </Tooltip>
  }
  min={0}
  max={2000}
  resetValue={1000}
  step={10}
  unit="ms"
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
/>
)
```

### Marks
Slider marks can be easily added by passing an array of values to the marks prop. Responsive behaviors are handled automatically.
```tsx
<Slider
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
label="Passing grade"
min={1}
max={5}
step={1}
marks={[
  { value: 1, label: "1" },
  { value: 2, label: "2" },
  { value: 3, label: "3" },
  { value: 4, label: "4" },
  { value: 5, label: "5" },
]}
trackColor="#61C454"
rangeColor="#EF4146"
/>
```

### Range
Set range to enable a dual-thumb slider for selecting a value range. The value and onChange props accept arrays instead of single numbers.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState([25, 75])
<Slider
range
label="Price range"
min={0}
max={100}
step={1}
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
prefixUnit="$"
/>
```

### Multiple thumbs
Pass three or more values to create a multi-thumb slider. Use minStepsBetweenThumbs to enforce minimum spacing between thumbs.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState([10, 40, 70])
<Slider
range
label="Breakpoints"
min={0}
max={100}
step={1}
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
minStepsBetweenThumbs={5}
/>
```

### Vertical
Set orientation="vertical" to render a vertical slider. Marks are not supported in vertical orientation.
```tsx
<Slider
label="Volume"
min={0}
max={100}
step={1}
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
orientation="vertical"
/>
```

### Disabled
Set disabled to prevent interaction with the slider.
```tsx
<Slider
label="Disabled"
min={0}
max={100}
step={1}
value={50}
onChange={() => {}}
disabled
/>
```

## Stat Card
Stat card for dashboards displaying KPIs with trend deltas, an info tooltip, an icon, a progress bar, and accent border styling.
Import: import { StatCard } from "@plexui/ui/components/StatCard"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/stat-card
Props:
  - label (string) — Required. Label describing the metric
  - value (ReactNode) — Required. The primary metric value
  - description (string) — Subtitle below the value
  - trend ({ value: number; label?: string }) — Trend indicator with percentage
  - invertTrend (boolean) default: false — Invert trend colors (positive = bad)
  - trendPosition ("value" | "header") default: "value" — Where the trend indicator is rendered
  - trendVariant ("text" | "badge") default: "text" — Render trend as text or badge
  - size ("default" | "sm") default: "default" — Card size. Use sm for compact analytics layouts
  - icon (ReactNode) — Icon displayed on the left with a soft background
  - sparkline (ReactNode) — Chart rendered at the bottom
  - progress (number) — Progress bar value (0-100)
  - progressLabel (string) — Label next to progress bar
  - tooltip (string) — Shows an info icon next to the label with tooltip text
  - variant ("default" | "accent") default: "default" — Visual variant
  - accentColor ("primary" | "secondary" | "danger" | "info" | "discovery" | "success" | "caution" | "warning") default: "primary" — Left border color (accent variant)
  - className (string) — Extra classes on the card element

### Overview
Dashboard-ready stat cards with trends, icons, and progress bars. Use the controls below to explore all available props.
```tsx
const [size, setSize] = useState("default")
const [variant, setVariant] = useState("default")
const [trendPosition, setTrendPosition] = useState("value")
const [trendVariant, setTrendVariant] = useState("text")
const [showTrend, setShowTrend] = useState(true)
const [showTooltip, setShowTooltip] = useState(false)
const [invertTrend, setInvertTrend] = useState(false)

<StatCard
label="Total Revenue"
value="$45,231"
size={size}
variant={variant}
trendPosition={trendPosition}
trendVariant={trendVariant}
trend={showTrend ? { value: 12.5, label: "vs last month" } : undefined}
tooltip={showTooltip ? "Sum of all revenue streams" : undefined}
invertTrend={invertTrend}
/>
```

### Sizes
Use size="sm" for compact analytics rows with denser spacing and smaller typography. The small size also pairs well with the tooltip prop for info icons.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
{/* Default size */}
<div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-4">
  <StatCard label="Total Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} />
  <StatCard label="Active Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} />
  <StatCard label="Conversion Rate" value="3.24%" trend={{ value: -1.8 }} />
</div>
{/* Small size */}
<div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-3">
  <StatCard size="sm" label="Total Inquiries" value="3,544" trend={{ value: -2.6 }} tooltip="Total inquiries in period" />
  <StatCard size="sm" label="Completion Rate" value="89.2%" trend={{ value: 0.5 }} tooltip="Average across templates" />
  <StatCard size="sm" label="Approval Rate" value="84.6%" trend={{ value: 1.8 }} tooltip="Average across templates" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Trend position
Control where the trend appears: next to the value (default) or right-aligned in the header row.
```tsx
<div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4" style={{ maxWidth: 480 }}>
<StatCard label="Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} trendPosition="value" />
<StatCard label="Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} trendPosition="header" />
</div>
```

### Trend variant
Display the trend as plain text or wrapped in a badge.
```tsx
<div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4" style={{ maxWidth: 480 }}>
<StatCard label="Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} trendVariant="text" />
<StatCard label="Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} trendVariant="badge" />
</div>
```

### Info tooltip
Pass a tooltip string to render an info icon next to the label with a tooltip on hover.
```tsx
<StatCard label="Avg Completion Rate" value="89.2%" trend={{ value: 0.5 }} tooltip="Percentage of inquiries reaching final state" />
```

### With icon
Pass an icon to display it on the left side with a soft background. The layout automatically switches to a horizontal icon + content arrangement. Works with both default and sm sizes.
```tsx
import { DollarCircle, Users, ShoppingBag } from "@plexui/ui/components/Icon"

{/* Default size */}
<div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<StatCard icon={<DollarCircle />} label="Total Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} />
<StatCard icon={<Users />} label="Active Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} />
</div>

{/* Small size */}
<div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-3">
<StatCard size="sm" icon={<DollarCircle />} label="Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} />
<StatCard size="sm" icon={<Users />} label="Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} />
<StatCard size="sm" icon={<ShoppingBag />} label="Orders" value="1,234" trend={{ value: -3.1 }} />
</div>
```

### With progress
Progress bars show a visual representation of completion or usage percentage.
```tsx
<StatCard label="Storage Used" value="7.2 GB" progress={72} progressLabel="72%" description="of 10 GB" />
```

### Accent border
The accent variant adds a colored left border. Choose from eight semantic colors.
```tsx
const [accentColor, setAccentColor] = useState("primary")

<StatCard
label="Total Revenue"
value="$45,231"
variant="accent"
accentColor={accentColor}
trend={{ value: 12.5, label: "vs last month" }}
/>
```

### Inverted trend
Use invertTrend for metrics where positive values are bad (e.g., error rate, response time). Toggle the switch to see the color flip.
```tsx
const [invertTrend, setInvertTrend] = useState(true)

<StatCard
label="Avg Response Time"
value="234ms"
trend={{ value: 15.3, label: "vs last hour" }}
invertTrend={invertTrend}
/>
```

## Switch
Toggle switch for turning settings on or off, with an optional label, a supporting description linked for screen readers, and a configurable label position.
Import: import { Switch } from "@plexui/ui/components/Switch"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/switch
Props:
  - checked (boolean) — Controlled state
  - defaultChecked (boolean) — Initial state (uncontrolled)
  - onCheckedChange ((next: boolean) => void) — Called when toggled
  - label (ReactNode) — Accessible label rendered next to the switch
  - description (ReactNode) — Secondary text below the label, linked via aria-describedby
  - labelPosition ("start" | "end") default: "end" — Label on left (start) or right (end)
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Prevent interaction
  - required (boolean) — Required for form submission
  - name (string) — Form field name
  - value (string) default: "on" — Value when submitted
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to wrapper node
  - id (string) — The id of the switch element (generated when omitted)
  - onFocus (FocusEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>) — Called when the switch gains focus
  - onBlur (FocusEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>) — Called when the switch loses focus

### Overview
```tsx
<Switch aria-label="Notifications" />
```

### With label
Add a label using the label prop. The label is automatically connected to the switch via id.
```tsx
<Switch label="Notifications" />
```

### With description
Add a description below the label for additional context. Linked to the switch via aria-describedby.
```tsx
<Switch
label="Disable user API keys"
description="Disable user-based API keys across your entire organization."
/>
```

### Label position
Set {'labelPosition="start"'} to place the label on the left side of the switch control.
```tsx
<Switch label="Right aligned" labelPosition="start" />
```

### Label position with description
The description follows the label position: both move together when {'labelPosition="start"'} is set.
```tsx
<Switch
label="Dark mode"
description="Use dark theme across the entire application."
labelPosition="start"
/>
```

### Default checked
Initialize the switch with defaultChecked when you don't need to control its state. Use the name prop to read the value on form submission.
```tsx
<Switch label="Enable notifications" name="notifications" defaultChecked />
```

### Controlled
Pass checked and onCheckedChange to manage the state in a controlled manner.
```tsx
const [checked, setChecked] = useState(false)
<Switch label="Airplane mode" checked={checked} onCheckedChange={setChecked} />
```

### Disabled
Use disabled to prevent the user from toggling the control.
```tsx
<div className="flex gap-6">
<Switch disabled aria-label="Notifications" />
<Switch disabled checked aria-label="Dark mode" />
</div>
```

### Disabled with label
Disabled state works with labels: both the toggle and the label show a not-allowed cursor.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
<Switch label="Notifications" disabled />
<Switch label="Notifications" disabled defaultChecked />
</div>
```

### Disabled with description
Combine disabled with label and description for read-only settings that need explanation.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
<Switch
  label="Enable SSO"
  description="Requires an Enterprise plan to configure."
  disabled
/>
<Switch
  label="Two-factor authentication"
  description="Enforced by organization policy."
  disabled
  defaultChecked
/>
</div>
```

### With Field
Pair a Switch with Field using orientation="horizontal" for inline toggle settings.
```tsx
<Field label="Marketing emails" orientation="horizontal">
{(fieldProps) => (
  <Switch id={fieldProps.id} checked={enabled} onCheckedChange={setEnabled} />
)}
</Field>
```

### With Field and description
Use Field with description for the settings pattern with a section heading, description, and a labeled switch underneath.
```tsx
<Field
label="Access Control"
description="Disable user-based API keys across your entire organization. You can also choose to disable them on a project-by-project basis if needed."
>
{(fieldProps) => (
  <Switch
    id={fieldProps.id}
    label="Disable user API keys"
    checked={enabled}
    onCheckedChange={setEnabled}
  />
)}
</Field>
```

### Settings panel
Combine label and description to build settings-style toggle panels.
```tsx
<div className="flex w-full max-w-lg flex-col gap-8">
<Switch
  label="Enable custom providers for evals"
  description="Allow eval runs to use third-party models you configure under Custom model providers."
/>
<Switch
  label="Enable OpenRouter models"
  description="Make OpenRouter models available for evaluation runs."
/>
<Switch
  label="Disable user API keys"
  description="Disable user-based API keys across your entire organization."
  defaultChecked
/>
</div>
```

### Grouped sections
Use dividers to separate switch groups into logical sections. Each section can be wrapped in a Field with its own label and description.
```tsx
<div className="w-full max-w-lg divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Notifications" description="Configure how you receive notifications.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
        <Switch
          label="Push notifications"
          description="Receive push notifications on your devices."
          defaultChecked
        />
        <Switch
          label="Email notifications"
          description="Get notified via email for important updates."
        />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="Privacy" description="Control your data sharing preferences.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
        <Switch
          label="Share usage data"
          description="Help us improve by sharing anonymous usage statistics."
        />
        <Switch
          label="Personalized content"
          description="Allow personalized recommendations based on your activity."
          defaultChecked
        />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

## Table
Styled table primitives for structured data, with header, body, footer, row, cell and caption parts on native table elements.
Import: import { Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell } from "@plexui/ui/components/Table"
Import: import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/table
  Table Primitives:
    - Table (table) — Root table container with horizontal scroll wrapper
    - TableHeader (thead) — Table header group
    - TableBody (tbody) — Table body group
    - TableFooter (tfoot) — Table footer group
    - TableRow (tr) — Table row
    - TableHead (th) — Table header cell
    - TableCell (td) — Table data cell
    - TableCaption (caption) — Table caption
  DataTable:
    - columns (ColumnDef<TData>[]) — Column definitions following TanStack Table v8 API (required)
    - data (TData[]) — Data array to display (required)
    - variant ("default" | "bordered") default: "default" — Visual variant: bordered adds a rounded border and tinted header
    - pageSize (number) default: 10 — Rows per page. Set 0 or Infinity to disable pagination. The rows-per-page select offers 10, 20, 50, 100 and this size
    - initialSorting (SortingState) — Initial column sorting state
    - globalFilter (string) — Controlled search/filter string
    - onGlobalFilterChange ((value: string) => void) — Callback when filter changes
    - onRowClick ((row: TData) => void) — Click handler for rows. Makes rows interactive: they take Tab and call it on Enter or Space
    - columnVisibility (VisibilityState) — Controlled column visibility state
    - onColumnVisibilityChange ((visibility: VisibilityState) => void) — Callback when visibility changes
    - enableRowSelection (boolean) default: false — Adds a first column (id select) with a checkbox per row and a header checkbox that selects every row on all pages, mixed when some are selected. A click on a checkbox is not a row click
    - rowSelection (RowSelectionState) — Controlled row selection state
    - onRowSelectionChange ((selection: RowSelectionState) => void) — Callback when selection changes
    - getRowId ((row: TData) => string) — Custom row ID accessor; selection keys use it
    - emptyMessage (ReactNode) default: "No results." — Shown when no rows
    - showPagination (boolean) default: true — Whether to show pagination controls. They hide on their own when every row fits on one page
    - className (string) — Class applied to outermost wrapper
  DataTableColumnHeader:
    - column (Column<TData, TValue>) — TanStack Table column object (required)
    - title (string) — Display text for the header (required)
    - className (string) — Class applied to the header button (or text when the column cannot sort)
  Column helpers:
    - idCell(accessor) (CellComponent) — Monospace ID with copy-on-click tooltip
    - dateTimeCell(accessor, options?) (CellComponent) — Formatted datetime with Intl.DateTimeFormat
    - statusCell(accessor, colorMap?) (CellComponent) — Badge cell with automatic status-to-color mapping
    - tooltipHeader(label, description) (HeaderComponent) — Header with dashed underline and info tooltip

### Overview
A complete table with header, body, footer, and caption showing invoice data.
```tsx
const invoices = [
{ invoice: "INV001", status: "Paid", method: "Credit Card", amount: "$250.00" },
{ invoice: "INV002", status: "Pending", method: "PayPal", amount: "$150.00" },
{ invoice: "INV003", status: "Unpaid", method: "Bank Transfer", amount: "$350.00" },
{ invoice: "INV004", status: "Paid", method: "Credit Card", amount: "$450.00" },
{ invoice: "INV005", status: "Paid", method: "PayPal", amount: "$550.00" },
]

return (
<Table>
  <TableCaption>A list of your recent invoices.</TableCaption>
  <TableHeader>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHead>Invoice</TableHead>
      <TableHead>Status</TableHead>
      <TableHead>Method</TableHead>
      <TableHead className="text-right">Amount</TableHead>
    </TableRow>
  </TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    {invoices.map((invoice) => (
      <TableRow key={invoice.invoice}>
        <TableCell className="font-medium">{invoice.invoice}</TableCell>
        <TableCell>{invoice.status}</TableCell>
        <TableCell>{invoice.method}</TableCell>
        <TableCell className="text-right">{invoice.amount}</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    ))}
  </TableBody>
  <TableFooter>
    <TableRow>
      <TableCell colSpan={3}>Total</TableCell>
      <TableCell className="text-right">$1,750.00</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
  </TableFooter>
</Table>
)
```

### Minimal
A simple table without caption or footer, showing a list of people.
```tsx
const people = [
{ name: "Lindsay Walton", title: "Front-end Developer", email: "lindsay@example.com" },
{ name: "Courtney Henry", title: "Designer", email: "courtney@example.com" },
{ name: "Tom Cook", title: "Director of Product", email: "tom@example.com" },
]

return (
<Table>
  <TableHeader>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHead>Name</TableHead>
      <TableHead>Title</TableHead>
      <TableHead>Email</TableHead>
    </TableRow>
  </TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    {people.map((person) => (
      <TableRow key={person.email}>
        <TableCell className="font-medium">{person.name}</TableCell>
        <TableCell>{person.title}</TableCell>
        <TableCell>{person.email}</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    ))}
  </TableBody>
</Table>
)
```

### Variant
Use variant="bordered" for a card-like table with a rounded border and tinted header background.
```tsx
import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader, statusCell, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{ accessorKey: "role", header: "Role" },
{ accessorKey: "department", header: "Department" },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: statusCell<User>((row) => row.status) },
]

export function UsersTable() {
return <DataTable columns={columns} data={users.slice(0, 6)} variant="bordered" pageSize={Infinity} />
}
```

### Sorting
Click column headers to toggle sort direction. Columns use DataTableColumnHeader for sort controls.
```tsx
import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{
  accessorKey: "role",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Role" />,
},
{
  accessorKey: "status",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Status" />,
},
]

export function UsersTable() {
return (
  <DataTable
    columns={columns}
    data={users}
    pageSize={5}
    initialSorting={[{ id: "name", desc: false }]}
  />
)
}
```

### Pagination
Automatic pagination with rows-per-page selector and navigation controls. Set pageSize to control the initial page size; the select offers 10, 20, 50 and 100 plus that size. The controls hide when every row fits on one page.
```tsx
import { DataTable, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{ accessorKey: "id", header: "ID" },
{ accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
{ accessorKey: "department", header: "Department" },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status" },
]

export function UsersTable() {
return <DataTable columns={columns} data={users} pageSize={5} />
}
```

### Row click
Pass onRowClick to make rows clickable. Clickable rows also take Tab and call it on Enter or Space.
```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{ accessorKey: "email", header: "Email" },
{ accessorKey: "role", header: "Role" },
]

export function UsersTable() {
const [selectedUser, setSelectedUser] = useState<User | null>(null)

return (
  <>
    <DataTable columns={columns} data={users.slice(0, 8)} pageSize={4} onRowClick={setSelectedUser} />
    <p className="mt-3 text-sm text-secondary">
      {selectedUser
        ? "Clicked: " + selectedUser.name + " (" + selectedUser.id + ") - " + selectedUser.department
        : "Click a row to see selected user details."}
    </p>
  </>
)
}
```

### Row selection
Set enableRowSelection to add a first column of checkboxes. The header checkbox selects every row on all pages and shows a mixed state when only some are selected. Bind rowSelection and onRowSelectionChange to read the selection; getRowId keys it by your own ids.
```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import {
DataTable,
DataTableColumnHeader,
statusCell,
type ColumnDef,
type RowSelectionState,
} from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{ accessorKey: "role", header: "Role" },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: statusCell<User>((row) => row.status) },
]

export function UsersTable() {
const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = useState<RowSelectionState>({})

return (
  <>
    <DataTable
      columns={columns}
      data={users}
      pageSize={5}
      enableRowSelection
      rowSelection={rowSelection}
      onRowSelectionChange={setRowSelection}
      getRowId={(user) => user.id}
    />
    <p className="mt-3 text-sm text-secondary">
      {Object.keys(rowSelection).length} of {users.length} rows selected
    </p>
  </>
)
}
```

### Cell variants
Column helpers render common cells: idCell (monospace ID with copy-on-click), statusCell (status badge), dateTimeCell (formatted date) and tooltipHeader (header with an info tooltip). Other formats, like the salary below, are plain cell renderers; meta.align aligns a column.
```tsx
import { DataTable, dateTimeCell, idCell, statusCell, tooltipHeader, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD", maximumFractionDigits: 0 })

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{ accessorKey: "id", header: "ID", cell: idCell<User>((row) => row.id) },
{ accessorKey: "name", header: "Name", cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span> },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: statusCell<User>((row) => row.status) },
{ accessorKey: "joined", header: "Joined", cell: dateTimeCell<User>((row) => row.joined) },
{
  accessorKey: "salary",
  header: tooltipHeader("Salary", "Annual base salary in USD."),
  meta: { align: "right" },
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{money.format(row.original.salary)}</span>,
},
]

export function UsersTable() {
return <DataTable columns={columns} data={users} pageSize={6} />
}
```

### Filtering
Control search with globalFilter and onGlobalFilterChange. The filter searches across all columns.
```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Input } from "@plexui/ui/components/Input"
import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader, statusCell, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{ accessorKey: "role", header: "Role" },
{ accessorKey: "department", header: "Department" },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: statusCell<User>((row) => row.status) },
]

export function UsersTable() {
const [globalFilter, setGlobalFilter] = useState("")

return (
  <>
    <Input
      value={globalFilter}
      onChange={(event) => setGlobalFilter(event.target.value)}
      placeholder="Search name, role, department..."
    />
    <DataTable
      columns={columns}
      data={users}
      globalFilter={globalFilter}
      onGlobalFilterChange={setGlobalFilter}
      pageSize={5}
    />
  </>
)
}
```

### Column visibility
Toggle column visibility with the columnVisibility and onColumnVisibilityChange props.
```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader, statusCell, type ColumnDef, type VisibilityState } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD", maximumFractionDigits: 0 })

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{ accessorKey: "role", header: "Role" },
{ accessorKey: "department", header: "Department" },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: statusCell<User>((row) => row.status) },
{
  accessorKey: "salary",
  header: "Salary",
  meta: { align: "right" },
  cell: ({ row }) => <span>{money.format(row.original.salary)}</span>,
},
]

export function UsersTable() {
const [columnVisibility, setColumnVisibility] = useState<VisibilityState>({
  role: true,
  department: true,
  status: true,
  salary: true,
})

return (
  <DataTable
    columns={columns}
    data={users}
    pageSize={5}
    columnVisibility={columnVisibility}
    onColumnVisibilityChange={setColumnVisibility}
  />
)
}
```

### Empty state
Customize the empty state message with the emptyMessage prop.
```tsx
import { DataTable, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import type { User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{ accessorKey: "id", header: "ID" },
{ accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
{ accessorKey: "email", header: "Email" },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status" },
]

export function UsersTable() {
return <DataTable columns={columns} data={[]} emptyMessage="No users found." />
}
```

## Tabs
Switch between grouped views with segmented or underline tabs, icon-only triggers, and badge counts on each tab.
Import: import { Tabs } from "@plexui/ui/components/Tabs"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/tabs
Props:
  - value (string) — Selected tab value (controlled, required)
  - onChange ((value: string) => void) — Called when selection changes
  - onClick (() => void) — Called on any click in the group, even when the selection does not change
  - variant ("segmented" | "underline") default: "segmented" — Visual style: segmented (background highlight) or underline (line indicator)
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Layout direction of the tab group
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Control height (3xs through 3xl)
  - gutterSize ("2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl") — Horizontal padding of tabs
  - pill (boolean) default: true — Fully rounded control (segmented variant only)
  - flush (boolean) default: false — Text-width indicator, no border, gap spacing (underline variant only)
  - block (boolean) default: false — Full-width control with equal-width tabs
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable all tabs
  - aria-label (string) — Accessible name (required)
  - overflow ("scroll" | "menu") default: "scroll" — Tabs that do not fit: scroll sideways, or move into a menu at the end (horizontal, not block)
  - overflowLabel (string) default: "More" — Text of the menu button with overflow="menu"
  - className (string) — Extra classes on the group element
  - children (ReactNode) — Tabs.Tab children
  Tabs.Tab:
    - value (string) — Tab value (required)
    - disabled (boolean) — Disable this tab
    - icon (ReactNode) — Icon element (sized automatically)
    - badge (ReactNode | { content: ReactNode; color?: "secondary" | "success" | "danger" | "warning" | "info" | "discovery" | "caution"; variant?: "soft" | "solid"; pill?: boolean; loading?: boolean }) — Badge content (for example a count) or a badge config
    - aria-label (string) — Accessible name (required for icon-only tabs)
    - children (ReactNode) — Tab label

### Overview
Tabs provides two visual variants: segmented (default) with a sliding background highlight, and underline with an animated line indicator. Both support horizontal and vertical orientations.
```tsx
const [tab, setTab] = useState("overview")

return (
<Tabs value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Demo tabs">
  <Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="reports">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
)
```

### Segmented with icons
Icons work with the segmented variant. Use the icon prop on individual tabs. Icons are automatically sized to match the current size.
```tsx
<Tabs size="lg" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Navigation">
<Tabs.Tab value="home" icon={<Home />}>Home</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="settings" icon={<SettingsCog />}>Settings</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications" icon={<Bell />}>Notifications</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Icon only
Omit the text children and pass only the icon prop for compact icon-only tabs. Always provide an aria-label on each tab for accessibility.
```tsx
<Tabs value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Navigation">
<Tabs.Tab value="home" icon={<Home />} aria-label="Home" />
<Tabs.Tab value="settings" icon={<SettingsCog />} aria-label="Settings" />
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications" icon={<Bell />} aria-label="Notifications" />
</Tabs>
```

### Segmented with badge
Pass a number or an object with content, color, variant, and pill to the badge prop. Badges render inline after the tab label inside the segmented container.
```tsx
<Tabs size="lg" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Filter">
<Tabs.Tab value="all" badge={{ content: 128, pill: true }}>All</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="unread" badge={{ content: 12, color: "info", pill: true }}>Unread</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="flagged" badge={{ content: 3, color: "danger", pill: true }}>Flagged</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Underline
Set variant="underline" for a minimal tab style with an animated line indicator under the active tab. No background container is rendered.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Sections">
<Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="reports">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Underline flush
Add flush with variant="underline" for minimal tabs where the indicator matches the text width exactly. No container border is rendered, and spacing between tabs uses gap instead of padding.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" flush value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Sections">
<Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="reports">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Underline block
Use block with the underline variant for full-width tabs that stretch evenly across the container.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" block value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Sections">
<Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="reports">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Underline with icons
Icons work with the underline variant the same way as with segmented. Use the icon prop on individual tabs.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" size="lg" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Navigation">
<Tabs.Tab value="home" icon={<Home />}>Home</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="settings" icon={<SettingsCog />}>Settings</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications" icon={<Bell />}>Notifications</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Underline with badge
Badges are supported with the underline variant. Pass a simple value or an object with content, color, variant, and pill.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" size="lg" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Filter">
<Tabs.Tab value="all" badge={{ content: 128, pill: true }}>All</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="unread" badge={{ content: 12, color: "info", pill: true }}>Unread</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="flagged" badge={{ content: 3, color: "danger", pill: true }}>Flagged</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Vertical segmented
Set orientation="vertical" to stack tabs vertically. The sliding thumb animates up and down.
```tsx
<Tabs orientation="vertical" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Settings">
<Tabs.Tab value="account">Account</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="password">Password</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications">Notifications</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="display">Display</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Vertical underline
Combine variant="underline" with orientation="vertical" for a sidebar-style navigation pattern. The line indicator appears on the left side.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" orientation="vertical" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Settings">
<Tabs.Tab value="account">Account</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="password">Password</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications">Notifications</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="display">Display</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Vertical underline with icons
Vertical underline tabs with icons provide a rich navigation experience commonly used in settings or admin panels.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" orientation="vertical" size="lg" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Navigation">
<Tabs.Tab value="home" icon={<Home />}>Home</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="settings" icon={<SettingsCog />}>Settings</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications" icon={<Bell />}>Notifications</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Disabled tab
Use disabled on individual Tabs.Tab elements to prevent interaction. Disabled tabs appear dimmed and cannot be selected.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Sections">
<Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="reports" disabled>Reports</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Sizing
Both variants support the full 9-step size scale. The size prop controls the height, font size, icon size, and spacing of tabs.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" size="md" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Demo tabs">
<Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="reports">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Scrollable
When tabs overflow their container, they automatically become horizontally scrollable. The active tab scrolls into view smoothly. No extra prop is needed: just constrain the container width.
```tsx
<div className="max-w-[400px] flex">
<Tabs value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Scrollable tabs">
  <Tabs.Tab value="1">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="2">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="3">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="4">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="5">Members</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="6">Billing</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="7">Security</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="8">Integrations</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
</div>
```

### Overflow menu
With overflow="menu", the tabs that do not fit stay out of the row and move into a menu at its end, instead of a sideways scroll that a phone does not show. When the active tab is a hidden one, the menu button shows its name and carries the selection. A tab's badge moves into the menu with it. overflowLabel sets the button's text (default "More"). Works for horizontal tabs without block.
```tsx
<div className="flex w-[360px]">
<Tabs value={tab} onChange={setTab} variant="underline" overflow="menu" aria-label="Repository">
  <Tabs.Tab value="code">Code</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="issues" badge={12}>Issues</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="pulls" badge={3}>Pull requests</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="actions">Actions</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="projects">Projects</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="insights">Insights</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
</div>
```

## Tag Input
Input for entering multiple unique values as chip-style tokens, with suggestions and keyboard editing.
Import: import { TagInput } from "@plexui/ui/components/TagInput"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/tag-input
Props:
  - value (Tag[]) — Controlled value
  - defaultValue (Tag[]) — Uncontrolled initial tags
  - onChange ((tags: Tag[]) => void) — Change handler
  - id (string) — Id of the text input, so a label can target it with htmlFor
  - placeholder (string) — Input placeholder
  - validator ((value: string) => boolean) — Validates each tag when it is created; invalid tags shown in red
  - maxTags (number) — Maximum number of tags. At the limit the text input hides and a count shows below; the container then takes the tab stop, so arrow keys and Backspace still select and remove tags
  - rows (number) default: 1 — Min rows
  - size ('sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | '3xl') default: xl — Control height when rows=1; matches Input height of the same size
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully-rounded container and chips; matches Input/SelectControl pill
  - delimiters (string[]) default: [",", " "] — Characters that commit the current text as a tag
  - disabled (boolean) — Disables the input: tags cannot be added or removed, and pending text stays as typed
  - autoFocus (boolean) default: false — Focus on mount

### Overview
```tsx
<TagInput placeholder="Add a tag..." size="md" rows={1} pill={false} />
```

### Inline filter row
When rows=1, TagInput matches the height of an Input or SelectControl of the same size, so it composes cleanly into horizontal filter rows. Toggle pill on both controls to keep the pair visually consistent.
```tsx
const FIELD_OPTIONS = [
{ value: "email", label: "Email" },
{ value: "name", label: "Name" },
{ value: "role", label: "Role" },
{ value: "team", label: "Team" },
{ value: "country", label: "Country" },
]

const [field, setField] = useState("email")
const [tags, setTags] = useState<Tag[]>([
{ value: "ada@plexui.com", valid: true },
{ value: "grace@plexui.com", valid: true },
])
const fieldLabel = FIELD_OPTIONS.find((option) => option.value === field)?.label ?? ""

return (
<div className="flex w-full max-w-2xl items-start gap-2">
  <Field label="Where" className="w-[160px] shrink-0">
    <Menu>
      <Menu.Trigger>
        <SelectControl size="md" pill={false} selected={!!field} className="w-full">
          {fieldLabel}
        </SelectControl>
      </Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Content minWidth={160} onCloseAutoFocus={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
        {FIELD_OPTIONS.map((option) => (
          <Menu.CheckboxItem
            key={option.value}
            checked={field === option.value}
            onCheckedChange={() => setField(option.value)}
            indicatorVariant="ghost"
          >
            {option.label}
          </Menu.CheckboxItem>
        ))}
      </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </Field>
  <Field label="Is in" className="flex-1">
    <TagInput size="md" pill={false} value={tags} onChange={setTags} placeholder="Add value, press Enter…" />
  </Field>
</div>
)
```

### Suggestions
Combine TagInput with clickable buttons to let users add tags by clicking suggestions or typing manually. Suggestions disappear once selected.
```tsx
const SUGGESTIONS = ['React', 'TypeScript', 'Next.js', 'Tailwind CSS', 'Node.js', 'GraphQL', 'PostgreSQL', 'Redis', 'Docker', 'AWS'];

const [tags, setTags] = useState([
{ value: 'React', valid: true },
{ value: 'TypeScript', valid: true },
]);

const selectedValues = new Set(tags.map((t) => t.value));
const available = SUGGESTIONS.filter((s) => !selectedValues.has(s));

return (
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <TagInput value={tags} onChange={setTags} placeholder="Add a skill..." size="md" />
  {available.length > 0 && (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-1.5">
      {available.map((s) => (
        <Button key={s} size="xs" color="secondary" variant="soft" pill={false}
          onClick={() => setTags([...tags, { value: s, valid: true }])}>
          {s}
        </Button>
      ))}
    </div>
  )}
</div>
);
```

## Text Link
Text link for inline internal and external links with router integration, color inheritance, underline control, and weight options.
Import: import { TextLink } from "@plexui/ui/components/TextLink"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/text-link
Props:
  - children (ReactNode) — Link content
  - href (string) — URL. An http:// or https:// URL is external
  - to (string | object) — Router link destination (internal); its type comes from the link component
  - primary (boolean) default: false — Primary color, no default underline
  - underline (boolean) default: true — Underline (default true unless primary)
  - forceExternal (boolean) — Force external link behavior
  - as (Component) — Link component (e.g. Next Link)
  - target (string) — Where to open the link. External links default to _blank
  - className (string) — Extra classes on the link

### Overview
```tsx
<div className="flex gap-4">
<TextLink href="#">Read more</TextLink>
<TextLink href="#" primary>External link <ArrowUpRight /></TextLink>
</div>
```

### Inline usage
```tsx
<p>
You can use the <TextLink href="#">responses endpoint</TextLink> to generate text. You can
either use the API directly from an HTTP client of your choice, or use one of the{" "}
<TextLink href="#">official SDKs</TextLink> for your preferred language.
</p>
```

### Default inheritance
By default, TextLink uses currentcolor inheritance and text-decoration: underline to create subtle visual differentiation from surrounding text. The hover effect is a dynamic deemphasis of the currentcolor, with some special cases for text-secondary and text-tertiary contexts.You can see this behavior by changing the text color context of the paragraph the links are in below:
```tsx
<p className="text-secondary">
You can use the <TextLink href="#">responses endpoint</TextLink> to generate text. You can
either use the API directly from an HTTP client of your choice, or use one of the{" "}
<TextLink href="#">official SDKs</TextLink> for your preferred language.
</p>
```

### Primary color
You can create a colorful link style with the primary prop, which uses color for visual differentiation.Primary links also remove the default underline treatment: pass underline to re-apply that style.
```tsx
<p>
Sample text with a <TextLink href="#" primary>primary link</TextLink>
</p>
```

### Underline
Links have an underlined aesthetic by default.Pass {'underline={false}'} to remove the underline from the link.
```tsx
<p className="text-secondary">
Sample text with a <TextLink href="#" underline={false}>subtle link</TextLink>
</p>
```

### External links
When external paths are provided, {''} will be used with {'target="_blank"'} and {'rel="noopener noreferrer"'} included by default. You can also compose icons along with the text to add visual indication.
```tsx
<TextLink href="#" primary underline>
External link <ArrowUpRight />
</TextLink>
```

### Font weight
Use the className prop to customize font weight.
```tsx
<TextLink href="#" className="font-semibold" underline={false}>
Contact support <ArrowRight />
</TextLink>
```

## Textarea
Multi-line text input that can grow with its content, with a size scale, autofill extension control, and invalid state styling.
Import: import { Textarea } from "@plexui/ui/components/Textarea"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/textarea
Props:
  - value (string | number) — Controlled value; uncontrolled when omitted
  - defaultValue (string | number) — Initial value when uncontrolled
  - onChange ((event: ChangeEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement>) => void) — Called on every input
  - variant ("outline" | "soft") default: "outline" — Visual style of the textarea
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Control height for single-line equivalent
  - gutterSize ("2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl") — Horizontal padding; defaults from size
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the textarea
  - readOnly (boolean) default: false — Make the textarea read-only
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Mark as invalid
  - allowAutofillExtensions (boolean) default: !!name — Allow autofill extensions
  - autoSelect (boolean) default: false — Select all contents when mounted
  - rows (number) default: 3 — Initial row count
  - autoResize (boolean) default: false — Grow/shrink with content
  - maxRows (number) — Max rows when autoResize; defaults to the larger of rows and 10
  - onAutofill (() => void) — Called when the browser autofills the textarea
  - className (string) — Applied to the container <div>
  - ref (Ref<HTMLTextAreaElement>) — Ref to the <textarea>

### Overview
```tsx
<div className="w-[400px]">
<Textarea placeholder="Enter text..." autoResize rows={3} />
</div>
```

### Variants
Use variant to stylize the textarea.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-6 w-[400px]">
<Textarea placeholder="Enter text..." variant="outline" rows={3} />
<Textarea placeholder="Enter text..." variant="soft" rows={3} />
</div>
```

### Auto resize
Enable autoResize to automatically grow/shrink the textarea as the user types. Control the bounds with rows (initial height) and maxRows.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("Line 1\nLine 2\nLine 3")

return (
<div className="w-[400px]">
  <Textarea value={value} onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)} placeholder="Type to grow..." autoResize rows={3} maxRows={8} />
</div>
)
```

### Sizing
Sizing of the textarea is controlled with size and gutterSize props. size sets the textarea to a specific control height for single-line equivalent, and gutterSize sets the horizontal padding.Each size provides default values for gutterSize, as well as font-size and border-radius. Each of these values can be overridden independently.
```tsx
<div className="w-[400px]">
<Textarea placeholder="Write a message..." size="lg" gutterSize="md" />
</div>
```

### Disabled
Use the disabled prop to disable the textarea, greying it out and preventing user interactions.
```tsx
<div className="w-[400px]">
<Textarea disabled defaultValue="Jane Doe" aria-label="Name" />
</div>
```

### Invalid
Use the invalid prop to mark the textarea as invalid. You decide how this state is removed, whether that's through onFocus, onChange, an onSubmit handler, etc.Default visual styles will be applied, based on the variant. Additionally, [data-invalid] is applied to the container for custom styling.
```tsx
<div className="w-[400px]">
<Textarea invalid placeholder="Invalid textarea" />
</div>
```

### Auto select text
Pass autoSelect to select all text in the textarea, useful when pairing with other copy actions. This prop behaves like an imperative action when toggled and allows selection to change.
```tsx
<div className="w-[400px]">
<Textarea defaultValue="Toggle to auto select" autoSelect={false} aria-label="Notes" />
</div>
```

### Autofill extensions
By default, autofill extensions are prevented by Textarea. For the occasions where you want browser extensions to be present, pass allowAutofillExtensions to remove the disabling.When name is passed this value will default to true.
```tsx
<div className="w-[400px]">
<Textarea name="email" placeholder="Allowed" allowAutofillExtensions />
</div>
```

## Toast
Toast notifications for transient feedback, with semantic variants, descriptions, action buttons, promise integration, and persistent toasts.
Import: import { Toaster, toast } from "@plexui/ui/components/Toast"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/toast
  Toaster:
    - position ("top-left" | "top-center" | "top-right" | "bottom-left" | "bottom-center" | "bottom-right") default: "top-center" — Where toasts anchor on the viewport
    - duration (number) default: 3000 — Default auto-dismiss duration in ms
    - offset (string | number | { top?; right?; bottom?; left? }) — Distance from the viewport edge
    - gap (number) — Gap between stacked toasts in px

### Overview
```tsx
toast("Inquiry ID copied")
```

### Variants
Semantic variants map to PlexUI's success / danger / warning / info tokens. No richColors is passed, so variants retheme automatically with data-theme.
```tsx
toast("Changes saved")
toast.success("Inquiry ID copied")
toast.error("Failed to assign owner")
toast.warning("Session expires in 2 minutes")
toast.info("New version available")
```

### Description
```tsx
toast("Changes saved", {
description: "Your profile is live for everyone on the team.",
})
```

### Action
```tsx
toast("Message sent", {
description: "Delivered to #design channel.",
action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => toast.success("Message recalled") },
})
```

### Promise
Use toast.promise to tie a single toast to an async operation. The toast shows a loading state, then swaps to success or error. Here saveProfile() resolves with {"{ name: \"Profile\" }"} after 1.5 seconds.
```tsx
toast.promise(saveProfile(), {
loading: "Saving…",
success: (data) => `${data.name} saved`,
error: "Save failed",
})
```

### Long content
```tsx
toast("Your deployment is still running", {
description:
  "This is a long message to show how the toast handles multi-line content without clipping or awkward wrapping. The title and description should both wrap cleanly.",
})
```

### Compact
Spread compact into any toast(...) options for a centered-text layout. Toast width shrinks to content by default regardless; the compact helper only adds center alignment for short status messages.
```tsx
import { toast, compact } from "@plexui/ui/components/Toast"

toast.success("Inquiry ID copied", compact)
```

### Persistent
Pass duration: Infinity for toasts that stay open until the user acts on them. There are no close (×) affordances, so put a labelled action on the toast so dismissal is intentional and keyboard-accessible.
```tsx
const id = toast("Backup scheduled for 2:00 AM UTC", {
description: "This stays open until you dismiss it.",
duration: Infinity,
action: { label: "Dismiss", onClick: () => toast.dismiss(id) },
})
```

## Tooltip
Brief informative text shown on hover or focus, for any trigger element, with conditional enabling and a compact variant.
Import: import { Tooltip } from "@plexui/ui/components/Tooltip"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/tooltip
Props:
  - children (ReactElement) — The trigger: a single element. Wrap plain text in Tooltip.TriggerDecorator
  - content (ReactNode) — Tooltip content (null = no tooltip)
  - compact (boolean) default: false — Short 1-3 word tooltips, inverse styling
  - interactive (boolean) default: false — Content is interactive, stays open when hovered
  - maxWidth (number | "none") default: 300 — Max width of tooltip
  - openDelay (number) default: 150 — Delay before showing (ms)
  - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "top" — Preferred side
  - sideOffset (number) default: 5 — Distance from trigger
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Alignment
  - alignOffset (number) default: 0 — Alignment offset
  - gutterSize ("sm" | "md" | "lg") default: "md" — Content padding
  - contentClassName (string) — Class for tooltip content
  - forceOpen (boolean) — Force open or closed
  - preventUnintentionalClickToClose (true) — Keeps the tooltip open when the trigger is clicked right after it opened

### Overview
```tsx
<Tooltip content="This is additional context that appears when the trigger is hovered or focused">
<Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>Simple text with tooltip</Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>
</Tooltip>
```

### Different triggers
Tooltip provides an optional component, Tooltip.TriggerDecorator, to help create accessible tooltip triggers. However, any component can be used as a trigger.
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
<Tooltip content="Tooltip on button">
  <Button color="primary" size="lg">Sample button</Button>
</Tooltip>
<Tooltip content="Tooltip on span">
  <span>Inaccessible trigger</span>
</Tooltip>
</div>
```

### Conditionally enabled
Sometimes a tooltip should only be disabled under certain conditions, such as when a component is disabled, providing more context as to why that is. Below is an example of how to do this by conditionally passing in null content.
```tsx
<Tooltip
content={disabled ? "This action is disabled for reasons" : null}
>
<Button color="primary" size="lg" disabled={disabled}>
  Sample button
</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

### Compact tooltips
Compact tooltips are designed for short, 1-3 word tooltips with inverted styling. They feature minimal padding, a dark background with white text, and no box shadows. Use {'compact={true}'} for brief status messages.
```tsx
<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard" compact>
<Button color="secondary" variant="ghost" size="md" aria-label="Copy to clipboard"><Copy /></Button>
</Tooltip>
```
